title.zh: 卷506 列傳二百九十三 畴人一
title.raw: 卷506 列傳二百九十三 畴人一

sentences.zh: 推步之學，由疏漸密。

translations.literal: The study of calendrical astronomy, from coarse gradually became refined.
translations.idiomatic: The science of calendrical astronomy grew ever more precise, advancing step by step from rough methods to refined ones.

sentences.zh: 泰西新法，晚明始入中國，至清而中、西薈萃，遂集大成。

translations.literal: The new Western methods first entered China in the late Ming; by the Qing, Chinese and Western [learning] gathered together, and thus reached full maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Western astronomical techniques reached China only in the late Ming, but under the Qing Chinese and European scholarship converged until the tradition reached its full flowering.

sentences.zh: 聖祖聰明天亶，研究曆算，妙契精微。

translations.literal: The Sacred Ancestor [Kangxi] was intelligent and heaven-endowed; he researched calendar and calculation, wonderfully grasping the subtle and refined.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor, endowed with brilliant native genius, studied calendrical astronomy until he mastered its finest subtleties.

sentences.zh: 一時承學之士，蒸蒸鄉化，肩背相望。

translations.literal: At one time the scholars who received his learning, eagerly followed and transformed, shoulder to shoulder they could be seen one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who studied under him turned to the discipline in ever-growing numbers, crowding the field shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 二百年來，推步之學，日臻邃密，匪特闢古學之榛蕪，抑且補西人之罅漏。

translations.literal: Over two hundred years, the study of calendrical astronomy daily became more profound and precise; not only did it clear the thicket and weeds of ancient learning, but also repaired the cracks and leaks of Westerners.
translations.idiomatic: Over two centuries calendrical astronomy grew daily more rigorous—clearing away the tangle of obsolete Chinese methods while also filling gaps in Western theory.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，阮元撰疇人傳，後學一再續之，唐、宋以來，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiaqing reign, Ruan Yuan compiled the Biographies of Astronomers and Mathematicians; later scholars repeatedly continued it—since the Tang and Song, in this respect it has been most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiaqing era Ruan Yuan compiled the Biographies of Astronomers and Mathematicians, and later scholars added to it again and again; never since the Tang and Song had the field been so richly documented.

sentences.zh: 今甄其卓然名家者著於篇，其政事、文學登於列傳及儒林、文苑者；

translations.literal: Now we select those who were outstanding established masters and record them in this chapter; those whose political affairs and literary accomplishments appear in other biographies, the Confucian scholars section, and the literary garden;
translations.idiomatic: Here we record those who stood out as masters of the discipline; those whose careers in government or letters are treated in other biographical chapters, in the Confucian scholars section, or in the literary garden;

sentences.zh: 西人官欽天監，廁於卿貳，各自有傳者：不具列焉。

translations.literal: Westerners who held office in the Directorate of Astronomy, ranked among vice-ministers, each have their own biographies elsewhere: they are not all listed here.
translations.idiomatic: and Westerners who served in the Directorate of Astronomy at vice-ministerial rank, each with a biography of their own, are not listed in full here.

sentences.zh: 薛鳳祚，字儀甫，淄川人。

translations.literal: Xue Fengzuo, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengzuo, whose courtesy name was Yifu, came from Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 少習算，從魏文魁遊，主持舊法。

translations.literal: In youth he studied calculation, followed Wei Wenkui in study, and upheld the old methods.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied mathematics under Wei Wenkui and championed the traditional Chinese methods.

sentences.zh: 順治中，與法人穆尼閣談算，始改從西學，盡傳其術，因著算學會通正集十二卷，考驗二十八卷，致用十六卷。

translations.literal: During the Shunzhi reign, he discussed calculation with the Frenchman Ferdinand Verbiest, and then first changed to follow Western learning, fully transmitting his techniques; he therefore wrote the Main Collection of the Comprehensive Mastery of Mathematical Learning in twelve juan, Examination and Verification in twenty-eight juan, and Practical Application in sixteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi era he discussed mathematics with the French Jesuit Ferdinand Verbiest, converted to Western methods, and mastered them fully. He then produced three works: the twelve-juan Main Collection of the Comprehensive Mastery of Mathematical Learning, the twenty-eight-juan Examination and Verification, and the sixteen-juan Practical Application.

sentences.zh: 其曰對數比例者，乃西算以假數求真數之便法也；

translations.literal: What he calls logarithmic proportion is the convenient Western method of using artificial numbers to seek true numbers;
translations.idiomatic: His section on logarithmic proportion explains the Western shortcut of using artificial numbers to obtain true values;

sentences.zh: 曰中法四線，以西法六十分為度，不便以十進位，改從古法，以百分為度，所列止正弦、餘弦、正切、餘切，故曰四線。

translations.literal: What he calls the Chinese method of four lines: because the Western method uses sixty parts to the degree, which is inconvenient for decimal reckoning, he reverted to the ancient method of one hundred parts to the degree; what is listed is only sine, cosine, tangent, and cotangent—hence it is called four lines.
translations.idiomatic: and his "Chinese method of four lines" reverts from the Western sexagesimal degree to the ancient centesimal division, listing only sine, cosine, tangent, and cotangent—hence the name "four lines."

sentences.zh: 其推步諸書：曰太陽太陰諸行法原，曰木火土三星經行法原，曰交食法原，曰歷年甲子，曰求歲實，曰五星高行，曰交食表，曰經星中星，曰西域回回術，曰西域表，曰今西法選要，曰今法表，皆會中、西以立法。

translations.literal: His books on astronomical calculation include: Origins of the Motions of the Sun, Moon, and Other Bodies; Origins of the Motions of Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn; Origins of Eclipses; Chronological Cycles of the Sexagenary Years; Seeking the True Length of the Year; High Motions of the Five Planets; Tables of Eclipses; Fixed Stars and Culminating Stars; Islamic Methods of the Western Regions; Tables of the Western Regions; Selected Essentials of the Present Western Method; and Tables of the Present Method—all combining Chinese and Western [principles] to establish rules.
translations.idiomatic: His works on astronomical calculation include Origins of the Motions of the Sun, Moon, and Other Bodies; Origins of the Motions of Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn; Origins of Eclipses; Chronological Cycles of the Sexagenary Years; Finding the True Length of the Year; High Motions of the Five Planets; Eclipse Tables; Fixed Stars and Culminating Stars; Islamic Methods of the Western Regions; Tables of the Western Regions; Selected Essentials of the Present Western Method; and Tables of the Present Method. All combined Chinese and Western principles to establish their methods.

sentences.zh: 以順治十二年乙未天正冬至為元，諸應皆從以起算。

translations.literal: Taking the winter solstice of the celestial first month of the twelfth year of Shunzhi, year yiwei, as the epoch, all correspondences are calculated from this starting point.
translations.idiomatic: He took the winter solstice of Shunzhi 12 (1655) as his epoch, and derived all calendrical correspondences from that starting point.

sentences.zh: 以三百六十五日二十三刻三分五十七秒五微為歲實，黃、赤道交度有加減，恆星歲行五十二秒，與天步真原法同。

translations.literal: He took 365 days, 23 ke, 3 fen, 57 miao, and 5 wei as the true length of the year; the intersection of the yellow and red equators has additions and subtractions; fixed stars advance 52 seconds per year—the same as the True Origins of Celestial Paces method.
translations.idiomatic: He set the tropical year at 365 days, 23 ke, 3 fen, 57 miao, and 5 wei, with adjustments for the obliquity of the ecliptic and a precession of 52 seconds per year—matching the True Origins of Celestial Paces method.

sentences.zh: 梅文鼎謂其書詳於法，而無快論以發其趣，蓋其時新法初行，中、西文字輾轉相通，故詞旨未能盡暢。

translations.literal: Mei Wending said his books are detailed in method but lack spirited discussion to bring out their interest; probably because at that time the new methods had just been introduced, and Chinese and Western texts passed back and forth in translation, so the wording could not be fully clear.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Wending observed that Xue's works are meticulous in technique but lack the lively exposition that would reveal their deeper interest—understandable, since the new Western methods had only just arrived and terms were still passing awkwardly between Chinese and European usage.

sentences.zh: 然貫通其中、西，要不愧為一代疇人之功首云。

translations.literal: Yet in penetrating and connecting Chinese and Western [learning], he truly does not disgrace being the foremost achiever among a generation of astronomers and mathematicians.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in uniting Chinese and Western learning he remains without question the leading figure of his generation among astronomers and mathematicians.

sentences.zh: 鳳祚定歲實秒數為五十七，與奈端合，與穆尼閣以為四十五秒者不同，則其學非墨守穆氏可知。

translations.literal: Fengzuo fixed the seconds of the true year at fifty-seven, agreeing with Newton, differing from Verbiest who took it as forty-five seconds—thus it is clear his learning was not slavishly adhering to the Mu [Verbiest] school.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzuo set the fractional seconds of the tropical year at fifty-seven, agreeing with Newton rather than Verbiest's figure of forty-five—showing that he did not merely parrot Verbiest's teachings.

sentences.zh: 或譏其謹守穆尼閣成法，依數推衍，非篤論也。

translations.literal: Some ridicule him for strictly adhering to Verbiest's established methods and deriving by numbers alone—this is not sound criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Critics who charge him with merely following Verbiest's formulas and pushing numbers without insight are not offering fair judgment.

sentences.zh: 杜知耕，字端甫，號伯瞿，柘城舉人。

translations.literal: Du Zhigeng, courtesy name Duanfu, style name Boqu, was a juren of Zhecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhigeng, whose courtesy name was Duanfu and style name Boqu, was a provincial graduate of Zhecheng.

sentences.zh: 精研幾何，以利瑪竇、徐光啟所譯幾何原本復加刪削，作幾何論約七卷，後附十條，則知耕所作也。

translations.literal: He deeply studied geometry, further abridging the Elements of Geometry translated by Matteo Ricci and Xu Guangqi, and wrote the Concise Discourse on Geometry in seven juan; the ten appended items at the end were composed by Zhigeng himself.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in geometry and produced a seven-juan Concise Discourse on Geometry by further abridging Ricci and Xu Guangqi's translation of Euclid; the ten supplementary propositions appended at the end are his own work.

sentences.zh: 言其法似為本書所無，其理實涵各題之內，非能於本書之外別生新義也。

translations.literal: It is said that his methods seem not to be in the original book, but their principles are actually contained within the various propositions; he could not outside the original book separately produce new meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Although his methods appear to go beyond the original text, their principles are already implicit in Euclid's propositions; he did not invent doctrines outside the book itself.

sentences.zh: 稱後附者，以​​別於丁氏、利氏之增題也。

translations.literal: They are called appended items to distinguish them from the added propositions of the Ding family and Ricci.
translations.idiomatic: They are called "appendices" to distinguish them from the supplementary propositions added by Ding and Ricci.

sentences.zh: 又雜取諸家算學，參以西人之說，依古九章為目，作《數學鑰》六卷。

translations.literal: He also gathered miscellaneous mathematical works of various schools, consulting Westerners' explanations, taking the ancient Nine Chapters as its framework, and wrote the Key to Mathematics in six juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the six-juan Key to Mathematics, drawing on various schools of mathematics and Western explanations, organized according to the topics of the ancient Nine Chapters.

sentences.zh: 言數非圖不明，圖非指不明，圖中用甲乙等字作志者，代指也，故其書於圖解尤詳。

translations.literal: He said numbers cannot be understood without diagrams, and diagrams cannot be understood without labels; the use of jia, yi, and other characters as markers in diagrams are substitutes for pointers—therefore his book is especially detailed in diagrammatic explanation.
translations.idiomatic: He held that numbers require diagrams to be understood and diagrams require labels—and that the jia, yi, and other symbols in his figures serve as pointers. For this reason his book is especially rich in illustrated explanations.

sentences.zh: 梅文鼎稱其圖註九章，頗中肯綮雲。

translations.literal: Mei Wending praised his illustrated commentary on the Nine Chapters as quite hitting the vital point.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Wending praised his illustrated commentary on the Nine Chapters as striking right at the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 龔士燕，字武任，武進人。

translations.literal: Gong Shiyan, courtesy name Wuren, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shiyan, whose courtesy name was Wuren, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 少穎異能文，講求性理，旁通算術，發明蔡氏律呂新書，推演黃鍾圜徑、開方密率諸法，而於元太史郭守敬授時術尤得其秘。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious and skilled in letters, pursued Neo-Confucian principle, and was broadly versed in calculation; he developed Cai Yuan's New Book on Pitch Pipes and Tones, deduced methods for the diameter of the yellow bell pipe and root-extraction density ratios, and especially grasped the secrets of the Yuan dynasty Grand Astrologer Guo Shoujing's Season-Granting system.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was precocious in letters and devoted to Neo-Confucian philosophy while also mastering mathematics. He elaborated Cai Yuan's treatise on pitch pipes, worked out methods for pipe diameters and root-extraction ratios, and above all penetrated the secrets of Guo Shoujing's Season-Granting calendar.

sentences.zh: 如求冬​​至時刻，上推百年加一算，以為歲週三百六十五日二十四刻二十五分之內，滿百年消長一分。

translations.literal: For example, in seeking the moment of the winter solstice, projecting upward by a century adds one count; he held that within the year's circuit of 365 days and 24 ke and 25 parts, each full century gains or loses one part.
translations.idiomatic: To find the moment of the winter solstice, for example, he projected backward century by century, holding that within a tropical year of 365 days, 24 ke, and 25 parts, one part accumulates or diminishes over each hundred years.

sentences.zh: 核之春秋日食三十七事，多與符合。

translations.literal: Checking against the thirty-seven solar eclipses recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, most accorded with his results.
translations.idiomatic: Checked against the thirty-seven solar eclipses recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals, his results agreed in most cases.

sentences.zh: 又如推晦、朔、弦、望，以太陽之盈與太陰之遲，以太陰之疾與太陽之縮皆相並，為同名相從；

translations.literal: Again, in calculating dark moon, new moon, first and last quarter, and full moon: the sun's excess and the moon's slowness, and the moon's speed and the sun's contraction, are all combined—this is combining like terms;
translations.idiomatic: In calculating new moons, first and last quarters, and full moons, he combined the sun's excess with the moon's slowness and the moon's speed with the sun's contraction—adding terms of the same sign;

sentences.zh: 以太陽之盈與太陰之疾，以太陰之遲與太陽之縮皆相減，為異名相消：乃得盈縮遲疾化為加減時刻之差。

translations.literal: the sun's excess and the moon's speed, and the moon's slowness and the sun's contraction, are all subtracted—this is canceling unlike terms: thus excess, contraction, speed, and slowness are transformed into differences of additive and subtractive moments.
translations.idiomatic: while subtracting the sun's excess from the moon's speed and the moon's slowness from the sun's contraction—canceling unlike terms—thereby converting excess, contraction, speed, and slowness into corrections to the calculated times.

sentences.zh: 以此加減朔望之大、小餘分，得定朔弦望諸時刻。

translations.literal: By these additions and subtractions to the great and small remainder parts of new and full moon, he obtained the fixed moments of new moon, first and last quarter, and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Applying these corrections to the remainder terms for new and full moons yielded the definitive times of new moons, quarters, and full moons.

sentences.zh: 至盈、縮、遲、疾，郭守敬創平、立、定三差，理隱數繁，能審其機括，繪圖以明之。

translations.literal: As for excess, contraction, speed, and slowness, Guo Shoujing created the three differences of level, standing, and fixed [interpolation]; the principle was hidden and the numbers complex—[Gong] could discern their mechanism and draw diagrams to clarify them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shoujing's three-tier interpolation for excess, contraction, speed, and slowness was conceptually obscure and numerically intricate; Gong Shiyan grasped its inner logic and illustrated it with diagrams.

sentences.zh: 又如赤道變黃道之法，謂在二至後者，以度率一零八六五除赤道積度變為黃道宿度；

translations.literal: Again, the method of converting equatorial to ecliptic [coordinates]: for [periods] after the solstices, divide accumulated equatorial degrees by the degree ratio 10865 to convert to ecliptic lodge degrees;
translations.idiomatic: In converting equatorial to ecliptic coordinates, after the solstices he divided accumulated equatorial degrees by the ratio 10865 to obtain ecliptic lodge degrees;

sentences.zh: 在二分後者，以度率一零八六五乘赤道積度變為黃道宿度。

translations.literal: for [periods] after the equinoxes, multiply accumulated equatorial degrees by the degree ratio 10865 to convert to ecliptic lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: and after the equinoxes he multiplied accumulated equatorial degrees by the same ratio.

sentences.zh: 凡此授時之術，引伸益明。

translations.literal: All such methods of the Season-Granting [calendar], he extended and made increasingly clear.
translations.idiomatic: In all such techniques of the Season-Granting calendar he extended and clarified Guo's methods.

sentences.zh: 其餘月離五星等法，與回回、西洋諸算，遇有疑難，無不洞悉。

translations.literal: As for the remaining methods of lunar departure and the five planets, and Islamic and Western calculations—whenever difficulties arose, none escaped his thorough understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise mastered lunar theory, planetary methods, and Islamic and Western calculations, leaving no difficulty unresolved.

sentences.zh: 至日、月體徑有大小，交食限數有淺深，具見其奧。

translations.literal: As for the varying sizes of the sun and moon disks and the shallow or deep limits of eclipses, he fully perceived their profundities.
translations.idiomatic: He fully grasped the varying apparent diameters of the sun and moon and the depth of eclipse limits.

sentences.zh: 且悟唐順之弧容直闊之法，以推求太陰出入黃道，在內在外，不離乎六度。

translations.literal: He also understood Tang Shunzhi's method of arc, chord, straight line, and width, using it to calculate the moon's entry and exit from the ecliptic; whether inside or outside, it never departed from six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He also applied Tang Shunzhi's method of arc, chord, and width to calculate the moon's latitude north and south of the ecliptic, which never exceeds six degrees.

sentences.zh: 自是一應七政、氣朔、交食諸端，按法而推，百不失一。

translations.literal: From then on, in all matters of the seven luminaries, qi and new moon, and eclipses, calculating by the methods, not one in a hundred failed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, in all calculations involving the seven luminaries, seasonal qi, new moons, and eclipses, his predictions scarcely missed once in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，詔募天下知算之士，於是入都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, an edict summoned men skilled in calculation from throughout the realm; he then entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1667 an edict called for mathematicians from across the empire, and he went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其時欽天監用大統算七政多不合天，奉旨在觀像台每日測驗，而金星比算差至十度。

translations.literal: At that time the Directorate of Astronomy used the Datong calendar to calculate the seven luminaries, which often did not accord with heaven; by imperial order daily tests were conducted at the Observatory, and Venus differed from calculation by as much as ten degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate was then using the Datong calendar, whose planetary positions often failed to match observation; ordered to test daily at the observatory, he found Venus off by as much as ten degrees.

sentences.zh: 因修改古法，乃據七年所測表景推測太盈縮，又據日測五星行度，考其遲疾。

translations.literal: He therefore revised the ancient methods, basing himself on gnomon shadow measurements taken over seven years to deduce solar excess and contraction, and also on daily observations of the five planets' motions to examine their speed and slowness.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the old methods accordingly, using seven years of gnomon measurements to determine solar excess and contraction and daily planetary observations to establish their varying speeds.

sentences.zh: 彼此推求加減，氣、閏、轉、交諸應，測驗皆與天合。

translations.literal: Mutually deriving additions and subtractions, the correspondences of qi, intercalation, rotation, and crossing—all tests accorded with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-checking these results, he found that all correspondences—for seasonal qi, intercalation, lunar rotation, and eclipses—matched observation.

sentences.zh: 蓋其法亦本郭守敬，太陽為氣應，推冬至日躔用之；

translations.literal: His methods also fundamentally followed Guo Shoujing: the sun as qi correspondence, used for calculating the winter solstice solar position;
translations.idiomatic: His system, like Guo Shoujing's, used the sun's motion as the qi correspondence for calculating the winter solstice;

sentences.zh: 太陰週天為轉應，朔望用之；

translations.literal: the moon's circuit of heaven as rotation correspondence, used for new and full moon;
translations.idiomatic: the moon's circuit as the rotation correspondence for new and full moons;

sentences.zh: 日月地球之運，同在一直線，視點上為交應，推日月食用之；

translations.literal: the motions of sun, moon, and earth on the same straight line, with the point of view above as crossing correspondence, used for calculating solar and lunar eclipses;
translations.idiomatic: the alignment of sun, moon, and earth as the crossing correspondence for eclipses;

sentences.zh: 合氣盈、朔虛之奇零為閏應，推閏月用之；

translations.literal: combining the odd remainders of qi excess and new-moon deficit as intercalation correspondence, used for calculating intercalary months;
translations.idiomatic: and the fractional remainders of qi excess and new-moon deficit as the intercalation correspondence for leap months;

sentences.zh: 此外又有金、木、水、火、土同聚一宿為合應，推五星用之。

translations.literal: besides these, when metal, wood, water, fire, and earth all gather in one lodge as conjunction correspondence, used for calculating the five planets.
translations.idiomatic: with the conjunction of all five planets in one lodge as a further correspondence for planetary calculations.

sentences.zh: 修改諸應，取順治元年甲申為元，以應世祖章皇帝撫有中夏之祥，欽天監名為『改應法』。

translations.literal: Revising all correspondences, he took the first year of Shunzhi, year jiashen, as the epoch, to respond to the auspicious omen of the Founding Emperor's pacification of China; the Directorate of Astronomy named it the 'Revised Correspondences Method.'
translations.idiomatic: He revised all these correspondences, taking Shunzhi 1 (1644) as the epoch to mark the Shunzhi Emperor's pacification of China. The Directorate named the system the Revised Correspondences Method.

sentences.zh: 既改氣、閏、轉、交諸應，復改遲、疾限及求差諸法，又改冬至黃道日出分依步中星內法。

translations.literal: Having revised the qi, intercalation, rotation, and crossing correspondences, he further revised the limits of speed and slowness and methods of seeking differences, and also revised the winter solstice ecliptic sunrise fraction according to the inner method of pacing culminating stars.
translations.idiomatic: Having revised the qi, intercalation, rotation, and crossing correspondences, he also revised the limits for planetary speed and slowness, the methods for calculating differences, and the winter-solstice ecliptic sunrise fraction using the inner method of pacing culminating stars.

sentences.zh: 又盈縮遲疾無積度，日食無時差，皆與天合。

translations.literal: Moreover, excess, contraction, speed, and slowness had no accumulated degrees, and solar eclipses had no time difference—all accorded with heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Excess, contraction, speed, and slowness required no accumulated degrees, and solar eclipses showed no time discrepancy—all matching observation.

sentences.zh: 台官交章保薦。

translations.literal: Observatory officials submitted successive memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Observatory officials submitted memorial after memorial recommending him.

sentences.zh: 八年，曆書告成，奏對武英殿，授歷科博士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the calendrical book was completed; he was received in audience at the Hall of Martial Eminence and appointed Doctor of the Calendar Section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1669 the calendrical treatise was finished; he was received in audience at the Hall of Martial Eminence and appointed Doctor of the Calendar Section.

sentences.zh: 時有薦西人南懷仁等於朝，及其實測諸術，驗且捷，遂定用西法，而古歷卒不行。

translations.literal: At that time Westerners such as Ferdinand Verbiest were recommended at court; when their observational techniques were tested, they proved accurate and swift, and it was decided to adopt the Western method—while the ancient calendar in the end was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners including Ferdinand Verbiest were then recommended at court; their observational methods proved both accurate and efficient, and the Western calendar was adopted—Gong's revised traditional system never took effect.

sentences.zh: 十年，以疾歸，著有像緯考一卷、歷言大略一卷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he returned home due to illness; he wrote the Examination of Astral Images and Constellations in one juan and the General Outline of Calendrical Discourse in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1671 he returned home on account of illness. He left behind the one-juan Examination of Astral Images and Constellations and the one-juan General Outline of Calendrical Discourse.

sentences.zh: 其天體論一卷及闇虛、中星、交食、定朔、五星諸論俱佚。

translations.literal: His Treatise on Celestial Bodies in one juan, and his discourses on dark void, culminating stars, eclipses, fixed new moon, and the five planets are all lost.
translations.idiomatic: His Treatise on Celestial Bodies and his essays on the dark void, culminating stars, eclipses, fixed new moons, and the five planets are all lost.

sentences.zh: 王錫闡，字曉菴，吳江人。

translations.literal: Wang Xichan, courtesy name Xiao'an, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xichan, whose courtesy name was Xiao'an, came from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 兼通中、西之學，自立新法，用以測日、月食不爽秒忽。

translations.literal: He was versed in both Chinese and Western learning, established his own new methods, and used them to predict solar and lunar eclipses without missing by a second or instant.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered both Chinese and Western astronomy, devised his own methods, and predicted solar and lunar eclipses to the nearest second.

sentences.zh: 每遇天晴霽，輒登屋臥鴟吻察星象，竟夕不寐。

translations.literal: Whenever the sky cleared after rain, he would climb onto the roof and lie on the owl-tail ridge ornament to observe the stars, staying awake all night.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the sky cleared, he would climb onto the roof ridge to watch the stars and stay awake through the night.

sentences.zh: 著曉庵新法六卷，序曰；

translations.literal: He wrote the New Methods of Xiao'an in six juan; the preface says:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the six-juan New Methods of Xiao'an, whose preface reads:

sentences.zh: 『炎帝八節，曆之始也，而其書不傳。

translations.literal: 'The eight seasonal nodes of the Flame Emperor were the beginning of calendrics, but his book has not been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: 'The Flame Emperor's eight seasonal divisions marked the origin of calendrics, but no text survives.

sentences.zh: 黃帝、虞、夏、殷、周、魯七曆，先儒謂系偽作。

translations.literal: The seven calendars of the Yellow Emperor, Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Lu—earlier Confucians said they were forged works.
translations.idiomatic: The seven calendars attributed to the Yellow Emperor, Yu, Xia, Shang, Zhou, and Lu were dismissed by earlier scholars as forgeries.

sentences.zh: 今七曆俱存，大指與漢曆相似，而章蔀氣朔，未睹其真，為漢人所託無疑。

translations.literal: Now all seven calendars survive; their general purport resembles the Han calendar, but their cycle, obscuration, qi, and new moon—we have not seen their true form; they were certainly forged by Han people.
translations.idiomatic: All seven texts survive today and broadly resemble Han calendrics, but their cycle, obscuration, qi, and new-moon systems are clearly Han fabrications.

sentences.zh: 太初、三統，法雖疏遠，而創始之功，不可泯也。

translations.literal: The Taichu and Santong [calendars], though their methods were coarse and distant, yet their pioneering achievement cannot be erased.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichu and Santong calendars, though crude in method, deserve credit as pioneering efforts.

sentences.zh: 劉洪、姜岌，次第闡明，何、祖專力表、圭，益稱精切。

translations.literal: Liu Hong and Jiang Kui clarified them in succession; He [Chengtian] and Zu [Chongzhi] devoted themselves to the gnomon table and measuring rod, and were increasingly praised as precise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong and Jiang Kui developed them further; He Chengtian and Zu Chongzhi concentrated on gnomon tables and measuring rods with ever greater precision.

sentences.zh: 自此南、北曆象，率能好學深思，多所推論，皆非淺近所及。

translations.literal: From this time, calendrical astronomers of north and south were generally able to love learning and think deeply, making many deductions—none of which shallow minds could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter calendrical astronomers north and south studied deeply and advanced many theories beyond the reach of superficial minds.

sentences.zh: 唐曆大衍稍密，然開元甲子當食不食，一行乃為諛詞以自解，何如因差以求合乎？』

translations.literal: The Tang Dayan calendar was somewhat more precise, yet at the jiazi year of the Kaiyuan era an eclipse that should have occurred did not; Yixing then composed flattering words to excuse himself—why not seek agreement by calculating the discrepancy?'
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Dayan calendar was somewhat more precise, yet it failed to predict the Kaiyuan eclipse; Yixing offered flattery instead of explanation—why not have adjusted the constants to match observation?'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『明初元統造大統曆，因郭守敬遺法，增損不及百一，豈以守敬之術果能度越前人乎？

translations.literal: He also said: 'At the beginning of the Ming, Yu Tong created the Datong calendar following Guo Shoujing's legacy methods, with additions and subtractions of less than one part in a hundred—could Guo Shoujing's techniques truly have surpassed all predecessors?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'At the founding of the Ming, Yu Tong produced the Datong calendar from Guo Shoujing's legacy with changes of less than one part in a hundred—did Guo's methods truly surpass all who came before?

sentences.zh: 守敬治曆，首重測日，余嘗取其表景，反覆布算，前後牴牾。

translations.literal: Shoujing in making the calendar first emphasized measuring the sun; I have taken his gnomon shadows and calculated back and forth repeatedly—the results contradict each other before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Guo prioritized solar measurement in calendar-making; I have recalculated from his gnomon data repeatedly and found internal contradictions.

sentences.zh: 餘所創改，多非密率。

translations.literal: The revisions I myself created are mostly not precise ratios.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the constants I devised are not precise ratios.

sentences.zh: 在當日已有失食失推​​之咎，況乎遺籍散亡，法意無徵。

translations.literal: Even in his own day there were faults of missed eclipses and failed predictions—how much more when the transmitted records are scattered and lost, and the intent of the methods has no evidence?
translations.idiomatic: Even in Guo's own day the calendar missed eclipses and failed predictions; how much worse now that his texts are lost and their rationale cannot be verified?

sentences.zh: 兼之年遠數盈，違天漸遠，安可因循不變耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, as years pass the numbers accumulate excess and gradually depart from heaven—how can one follow the old ways unchanged?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as the centuries pass the constants drift further from observation—how can one cling to the old system unchanged?

sentences.zh: 元氏藝不逮郭，在廷諸臣，又不逮元，卒使昭代大典，踵陋襲偽。

translations.literal: The Yuan [officials'] skill did not reach Guo's; the ministers at court did not reach the Yuan—ultimately causing the great canon of a brilliant age to follow vulgarity and inherit forgery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan officials fell short of Guo; Ming ministers fell short of the Yuan—so the calendrical canon of a glorious age descended into mediocrity and inherited error.

sentences.zh: 雖有李德芳苦爭之，然德芳不能推理，而株守陳言，無以相勝，誠可嘆也！』

translations.literal: Although Li Defang bitterly contested this, yet Defang could not reason deductively and clung to stale words, having no means to prevail—truly lamentable!'
translations.idiomatic: Li Defang fought hard against this, but he could not argue from principle and merely repeated old formulas, unable to prevail—a truly lamentable outcome!'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『萬曆季年，西人利氏來華，頗工曆算。

translations.literal: He also said: 'In the final years of Wanli, the Westerner Ricci came to China, quite skilled in calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'In the late Wanli era the Jesuit Matteo Ricci came to China, well versed in calendrical astronomy.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，命禮臣徐光啟譯其書，有曆指為法原，曆表為法數，書百餘卷，數年而成，遂盛行於世。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, the ritual official Xu Guangqi was ordered to translate his books; there was the Calendar Guide as origins of methods and Calendar Tables as method numbers—over a hundred juan, completed in several years, and then widely circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign Xu Guangqi was ordered to translate his works—the Calendar Guide as theoretical foundation and Calendar Tables as numerical methods—more than a hundred juan completed over several years and soon dominant everywhere.

sentences.zh: 言曆者莫不奉為俎豆。

translations.literal: Those who spoke of calendrics all regarded them as sacrificial vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Every calendrical scholar treated them as canonical scripture.

sentences.zh: 吾謂西曆善矣，然以為測候精詳可也，以為深知法意未可也。

translations.literal: I say the Western calendar is good; yet one may regard it as precise in observation and testing, but one may not regard it as deeply understanding the intent of the methods.
translations.idiomatic: I grant that the Western calendar is excellent for precise observation, but I do not grant that its authors fully understood the principles behind their methods.

sentences.zh: 循其理而求通，可也；

translations.literal: Following their principles to seek understanding is acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: One may follow their reasoning to reach understanding;

sentences.zh: 安其誤而不辨，不可也。

translations.literal: accepting their errors without distinguishing them is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: but one must not accept their errors without question.

sentences.zh: 姑舉其概：二分者，春、秋平氣之​​中；

translations.literal: Let me briefly cite an outline: the two equinoxes are the midpoints of spring and autumn mean qi;
translations.idiomatic: Consider one example: the equinoxes mark the midpoints of mean spring and autumn qi;

sentences.zh: 二至者，日道南、北之中也。

translations.literal: the two solstices are the midpoints of the sun's path south and north.
translations.idiomatic: the solstices mark the sun's southern and northern limits.

sentences.zh: 大統以平氣授人時，以盈縮定日躔。

translations.literal: The Datong [calendar] used mean qi to grant human seasons and used excess and contraction to fix the sun's daily motion.
translations.idiomatic: The Datong calendar used mean qi for seasonal division and excess and contraction for the sun's daily position.

sentences.zh: 西人既用定氣，則分、正為一，因譏中歷節氣差至二日。

translations.literal: Since Westerners used fixed qi, equinox and solstice became one; they therefore ridiculed the Chinese calendar's solar terms as differing by as much as two days.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners used fixed qi, conflating equinoxes with solstices, and mocked the Chinese calendar for solar terms off by as much as two days.

sentences.zh: 夫中曆歲差數強，盈縮過多，惡得無差？

translations.literal: The Chinese calendar's precession figure was too large and excess and contraction too great—how could there be no discrepancy?
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese precession constant was too large and the excess-contraction values excessive—some discrepancy was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 然二日之異，乃分、正殊科，非不知日行之朓朒而致誤也。

translations.literal: Yet the two-day difference arose because equinox and solstice are separate categories—not from ignorance of the sun's waxing and waning that caused error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two-day gap arose because equinoxes and solstices belong to different categories—not from ignorance of the sun's varying speed.

sentences.zh: 歷指直以怫己而譏之，不知法意一也。

translations.literal: The Calendar Guide directly criticized out of contrariness to oneself, not understanding the intent of the methods—this is the first [error].
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Guide criticized out of partisan spirit without grasping the underlying rationale—its first error.

sentences.zh: 諸家造曆，必有積年日法，多寡任意，牽合由人。

translations.literal: All schools in making calendars necessarily had accumulated years and day divisors, whose amounts were arbitrary and whose fitting together depended on the person.
translations.idiomatic: Every traditional calendar relied on accumulated epoch years and day divisors, arbitrarily chosen and fitted by hand.

sentences.zh: 守敬去積年而起自辛巳，屏日法而斷以萬分，識誠卓也。

translations.literal: Shoujing discarded accumulated years and began from xinsi, set aside day divisors and decided by ten-thousandths—his insight was truly outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shoujing discarded epoch years, beginning from the xinsi year, and replaced day divisors with decimal parts—a truly remarkable insight.

sentences.zh: 西曆命日之時以二十四，命時之分以六十，通計一日為分一千四百四十，是復用日法矣。

translations.literal: The Western calendar names the hours of the day by twenty-four, names the minutes of the hour by sixty—in all one day is 1,440 minutes; this is again using day divisors.
translations.idiomatic: The Western calendar divides the day into twenty-four hours and each hour into sixty minutes, totaling 1,440 parts per day—a return to the old day-divisor system.

sentences.zh: 至於刻法，彼所無也。

translations.literal: As for the ke method of division, they had none.
translations.idiomatic: They had no equivalent of the Chinese ke division.

sentences.zh: 近始每時四分之，為一日之刻九十六。

translations.literal: Only recently did they begin to quarter each hour, making ninety-six ke in one day.
translations.idiomatic: Only recently did they quarter each hour to produce ninety-six ke per day.

sentences.zh: 彼先求度而後日，尚未覺其繁，施之中曆則窒矣。

translations.literal: They first seek degrees and then days—they have not yet felt this is cumbersome; applied to the Chinese calendar it would be obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: They calculate degrees before days—a procedure they find manageable but that would cripple the Chinese system.

sentences.zh: 乃執西法反謂中曆百刻不適於用，何也？

translations.literal: Yet they cling to Western methods and in turn say the Chinese calendar's hundred ke is unsuitable for use—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they insist on Western methods and declare the Chinese hundred-ke system useless—on what grounds?

sentences.zh: 且日食時差法之九十有六，與日刻之九十六何與乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, the ninety-six of the solar eclipse time-difference method—what has it to do with the ninety-six ke of the day?
translations.idiomatic: And what connection does the ninety-six in the eclipse time-difference formula bear to the ninety-six ke of the day?

sentences.zh: 而援以為據，不知法意二也。

translations.literal: Yet they cite it as evidence, not understanding the intent of the methods—this is the second [error].
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cite it as proof without grasping the underlying rationale—its second error.

sentences.zh: 天體渾淪，初無度分可指，昔人因一日日躔命為一度，日有疾徐，斷以平行，數本順天，不可損益。

translations.literal: The celestial body is a unified sphere, at first with no degrees or parts to point to; the ancients therefore named one day's solar motion as one degree. The sun has faster and slower [motion]; they decided by mean motion—the numbers fundamentally follow heaven and cannot be increased or diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is a single sphere, originally without fixed degrees to mark; the ancients therefore defined one day's solar travel as one degree. Because the sun moves unevenly, they used mean motion—the reckoning follows heaven itself and cannot be arbitrarily adjusted.

sentences.zh: 西人去週天五度有奇，斂為三百六十，不過取便割圜，豈真天道固然？

translations.literal: The Westerners subtracted a bit more than five degrees from the circuit of heaven and contracted it to 360—nothing more than taking convenience to divide the circle; how could this truly be the way of heaven as such?
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners trimmed a little more than five degrees from the celestial circuit and rounded it to 360—merely a convenient way to divide the circle. How could that truly be heaven's own measure?

sentences.zh: 而黨同伐異，必曰日度為非，詎知三百六十尚非天真有此度數乎？

translations.literal: Yet in partisan alignment they attack dissenters, insisting that solar degrees are wrong—do they not know that even 360 is not a number heaven truly possesses?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in partisan spirit they attack rivals and declare solar degrees wrong—do they not realize that even 360 is not a number heaven truly ordained?

sentences.zh: 不知法意三也。

translations.literal: Not understanding the intent of the methods—this is the third [error].
translations.idiomatic: Failure to grasp the underlying rationale—its third error.

sentences.zh: 上古置閏，恆於歲終，蓋歷術疏闊，計歲以置閏也。

translations.literal: In antiquity intercalation was set, mutually placed at year-end—because calendar methods were crude and broad, they reckoned by the year to set intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: In earliest times intercalary months were placed mutually at year's end, because calendar methods were still crude and intercalation was reckoned by the year.

sentences.zh: 中古法日趨密，始計月以置閏，而閏於積終，故舉中氣以定月，而月無中氣者即為閏。

translations.literal: In middle antiquity methods grew daily more precise; they began to reckon by month to set intercalation, and intercalation came at the end of accumulation. Therefore they took the median qi to fix the month, and a month without median qi was the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: In middle antiquity methods grew steadily finer; intercalation was reckoned by month and placed at the end of accumulated surplus. Months were fixed by median qi, and any month lacking median qi was declared intercalary.

sentences.zh: 大統專用平氣，置閏必得其月，新法改用定氣，致一月有兩中氣之時，一歲有兩可閏之月，若辛丑西曆者，不亦盭乎！

translations.literal: The Great Uniformity calendar exclusively used mean qi; setting intercalation always obtained the correct month. The new methods changed to true qi, causing times when one month has two median qi, and one year has two months that could be intercalary—as in the xinchou Western calendar, is this not perverse!
translations.idiomatic: The Great Uniformity calendar used mean qi exclusively and always placed intercalation in the correct month. The new methods switched to true qi, producing months with two median qi and years with two eligible intercalary months—as in the xinchou Western calendar. Is that not perverse?

sentences.zh: 夫月無平中氣者，乃為積餘之終，無定中氣者，非其月也。

translations.literal: Now, a month without mean median qi marks the end of accumulated remainder; one without true median qi is not a [proper] month.
translations.idiomatic: A month without mean median qi marks the end of accumulated surplus; one without true median qi is not a proper month at all.

sentences.zh: 不能虛衷深考，而以鹵莽之習，侈支離之學，是以歸餘之後，氣尚在晦；

translations.literal: Unable to examine with open mind and deep study, they follow crude habits and indulge in fragmented learning—hence after returning the remainder, the qi is still at the new moon;
translations.idiomatic: Unable to investigate with open-minded rigor, they fall back on crude habits and indulge in fragmented learning—so that after returning the remainder, the qi still falls on the new moon;

sentences.zh: 季冬中氣，已入仲冬；

translations.literal: the last-winter median qi has already entered mid-winter;
translations.idiomatic: the midwinter median qi has already shifted into mid-winter's second month;

sentences.zh: 首春中氣，將歸臘杪。

translations.literal: the first-spring median qi is about to return to the end of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: and the first-spring median qi is about to slip back to the end of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 不得已而退朔一日以塞人望，亦見其技之窮矣，不知法意四也。

translations.literal: Having no choice, they retreated the new moon one day to satisfy people's expectations—also showing the limits of their technique; not understanding the intent of the methods—this is the fourth [error].
translations.idiomatic: Forced to retreat the new moon by one day to satisfy public expectation, they revealed the limits of their art—failure to grasp the underlying rationale, its fourth error.

sentences.zh: 天正日躔，本起子半，後因歲差，自丑及寅。

translations.literal: The celestial New Year's solar position originally began at half zi, later because of precession, from chou to yin.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's position at celestial New Year originally began at half zi; later, through precession, it shifted from chou toward yin.

sentences.zh: 若夫合神之說，乃星命家猥言，明理者所不道。

translations.literal: As for the doctrine of 'harmonizing with the spirit,' it is vulgar talk of astrologers—those who understand reason do not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine of 'harmonizing with the spirit' is vulgar astrological chatter—serious thinkers do not entertain it.

sentences.zh: 西人自命歷宗，何至反為所惑，謂天正日躔定起丑初乎？

translations.literal: Westerners style themselves masters of calendrical astronomy—how could they in turn be deluded, claiming the celestial New Year's solar position must begin at the start of chou?
translations.idiomatic: Westerners style themselves masters of calendrical astronomy—how could they be taken in and insist that the celestial New Year's solar position must begin at the start of chou?

sentences.zh: 況十二次命名，悉依星象，如隨節氣遞遷，雖子午不妨異地，豈玄枵、鳥咮亦無定位耶？

translations.literal: Moreover the twelve stations are all named by star images—if they shifted with the solar terms, though zi and wu might not mind different locations, would Xuanxiao and Niaozhui also have no fixed positions?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the twelve celestial stations are all named from star patterns—if they shifted with the solar terms, zi and wu might tolerate different locations, but would Xuanxiao and Niaozhui also lose fixed positions?

sentences.zh: 不知法意五也。

translations.literal: Not understanding the intent of the methods—this is the fifth [error].
translations.idiomatic: Failure to grasp the underlying rationale—its fifth error.

sentences.zh: 歲實消長，昉於統天，郭氏用之，而未知所以當用；

translations.literal: The variation in the true length of the year began with the Tongtian calendar; Guo Shoujing used it, yet did not know why it should be used;
translations.idiomatic: Variation in the true length of the year began with the Tongtian calendar; Guo Shoujing adopted it without knowing why it should be used;

sentences.zh: 元氏去之，而未知所以當去。

translations.literal: the Yuan makers removed it, yet did not know why it should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: the Yuan calendar makers discarded it without knowing why it should be discarded.

sentences.zh: 西人知以日行最高求之。

translations.literal: Westerners know to seek it from the sun's apogee.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners know to derive it from the sun's apogee.

sentences.zh: 而未知以二道遠近求之，得其一而遺其一。

translations.literal: Yet they do not know to seek it from the differing distances of the two paths—they obtain one and lose one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they do not know to derive it from the differing distances of the two paths—they grasp one factor and neglect the other.

sentences.zh: 當辨者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 歲差不齊，必緣天運緩疾，今欲歸之偶差，豈前此諸家皆妄作乎？

translations.literal: Precession is not uniform—it must arise from the slowing and quickening of celestial motion. Now to attribute it to mere accidental discrepancy—were all previous schools fabricating nonsense?
translations.idiomatic: Precession is not uniform; it must arise from the varying speed of celestial motion. To reduce it to mere accidental error—is every earlier school to be dismissed as fabricating nonsense?

sentences.zh: 黃、白異距，生交行之進退；

translations.literal: The differing distances of the yellow and white [paths] produce the advance and retreat of syzygies;
translations.idiomatic: The differing distances between the yellow and white paths produce the advance and retreat of syzygies;

sentences.zh: 黃、赤異距，生歲差之屈伸；

translations.literal: the differing distances of the yellow and red [paths] produce the flexing and extension of precession;
translations.idiomatic: the differing distances between the yellow and red paths produce the flexing and extension of precession;

sentences.zh: 其理一也。

translations.literal: the principle is one.
translations.idiomatic: the underlying principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 曆指已明於月，何蔽於日？

translations.literal: The Calendar Guide has already clarified this for the moon—why be blind to it for the sun?
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Guide already explains this for the moon—why remain blind to it for the sun?

sentences.zh: 當辨者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 日躔盈縮最高，斡運古今不同，揆之臆見，必有定數。

translations.literal: The solar motion's excess-contraction and apogee, revolving through past and present, differ; judged by conjecture, there must be a fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's excess-contraction and apogee have revolved differently through past and present ages; by reason there must be a fixed value.

sentences.zh: 不惟日月星應同，但行遲差微，非畢生歲月所可測度耳。

translations.literal: Not only sun, moon, and stars should be the same—all merely differ in slowness and speed in small measure, not what a lifetime of years and months can measure.
translations.idiomatic: Not the sun and moon alone but the stars as well should follow the same law—the differences in speed are slight and cannot be measured within a single lifetime.

sentences.zh: 西人每詡數千年傳人不乏，何以亦無定論？

translations.literal: Westerners often boast that for thousands of years their line has never lacked successors—why then do they also have no settled conclusion?
translations.idiomatic: Westerners boast that their tradition has never lacked successors for thousands of years—why then do they still have no settled conclusion?

sentences.zh: 當辨者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 日月去人時分遠近，兒徑因分大小，則遠近大小，宜為相似之比例。

translations.literal: When sun and moon are at different times and fractional distances from people, apparent diameter varies with the parts in size—then distance and size ought to follow similar proportions.
translations.idiomatic: As the sun and moon vary in fractional distance from the observer, their apparent diameters vary in size—distance and size ought therefore to stand in similar proportion.

sentences.zh: 西法日則遠近差多，而兒徑差少；

translations.literal: In Western methods for the sun, the distance difference is great but the apparent diameter difference is small;
translations.idiomatic: In Western methods the sun shows a large difference in distance but a small difference in apparent diameter;

sentences.zh: 月則遠近差少，而兒徑差多。

translations.literal: for the moon, the distance difference is small but the apparent diameter difference is great.
translations.idiomatic: for the moon, a small difference in distance but a large difference in apparent diameter.

sentences.zh: 因數求理，難會其通。

translations.literal: Seeking principle from numbers, it is hard to grasp the coherence.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking principle from the numbers alone, one can hardly grasp the underlying coherence.

sentences.zh: 當辨者四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 日食變差，機在交分，日軌交分，與月高交分不同；

translations.literal: Solar eclipse parallax variation—the key lies in node distance; the sun's orbital node distance differs from the moon's altitude node distance;
translations.idiomatic: Parallax variation in solar eclipses turns on node distance—the sun's orbital node distance differs from the moon's altitude node distance;

sentences.zh: 月高交於本道，與交於黃道者又不同。

translations.literal: the moon's altitude node on its own path also differs from that at the ecliptic intersection.
translations.idiomatic: and the moon's altitude node on its own path differs again from that at the ecliptic intersection.

sentences.zh: 曆指不詳其理，歷表不著其數，豈黃道一術足窮日食之變乎？

translations.literal: The Calendar Guide does not detail this principle, the Calendar Tables do not set forth its numbers—can ecliptic methods alone exhaust the changes of solar eclipses?
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Guide does not explain this principle and the Calendar Tables do not give its numbers—can ecliptic methods alone exhaust the variations of solar eclipses?

sentences.zh: 當辨者五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 中限左右，日月兒差，時或一東一西。

translations.literal: To the left and right of the central limit, solar and lunar apparent parallax differences may at times be one east and one west.
translations.idiomatic: To the left and right of the central limit, solar and lunar parallax may at times run one east and one west.

sentences.zh: 交、廣以南，日月兒差，時或一南一北。

translations.literal: South of the intersection breadth, solar and lunar apparent parallax differences may at times be one south and one north.
translations.idiomatic: South of the intersection breadth, solar and lunar parallax may at times run one south and one north.

sentences.zh: 此為兒差異向與兒差同向者加減迥別，歷指豈以非所常遇，故置不講耶？

translations.literal: This is because apparent parallax in opposite directions and in the same direction differ greatly in addition and subtraction—does the Calendar Guide perhaps because these are not commonly encountered, set them aside and not discuss them?
translations.idiomatic: Because parallax in opposite directions and in the same direction require very different additions and subtractions—does the Calendar Guide pass over them simply because they are rarely encountered?

sentences.zh: 萬一遇之，則學者何以立算？

translations.literal: If one meets it once in ten thousand cases, how can students establish their calculations?
translations.idiomatic: If such a case occurs once in ten thousand, how are students to establish their calculations?

sentences.zh: 當辨者六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 日光射物，必有虛景，虛景者，光徑與實徑之所生也。

translations.literal: When sunlight strikes objects, there must be a virtual image; the virtual image is produced by the light radius and the real radius.
translations.idiomatic: When sunlight strikes an object it always casts a virtual image, produced by the light radius together with the real radius.

sentences.zh: 闇虛恆縮，理不出此。

translations.literal: The dark shadow cone is always contracted—the principle does not go beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: The dark shadow cone is always contracted—the principle admits no exception.

sentences.zh: 西人不知日有光徑，僅以實徑求闇虛。

translations.literal: Westerners do not know the sun has a light radius; they seek the dark shadow cone only by the real radius.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners do not recognize that the sun has a light radius and compute the shadow cone from the real radius alone.

sentences.zh: 及至推步不符，复酌損徑分以希偶合。

translations.literal: When calculation fails to match, they then adjust and reduce the radius parts hoping for chance agreement.
translations.idiomatic: When their calculations fail to match observation, they trim the radius parts hoping for a chance fit.

sentences.zh: 當辨者七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh point that ought to be clarified.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh matter requiring clarification.

sentences.zh: 月食定望，惟食甚為然，虧复四限，距望有差。

translations.literal: Lunar eclipses occur at exact full moon only at greatest eclipse; the four limits of eclipse beginning and end differ in distance from full moon.
translations.idiomatic: A lunar eclipse falls at exact full moon only at greatest eclipse; the four limits of beginning and end of eclipse stand at varying distances from full moon.

sentences.zh: 日食稍離中限，即食甚已非定朔。

translations.literal: For solar eclipses, slightly departing from the central limit, even greatest eclipse is no longer at exact new moon.
translations.idiomatic: For solar eclipses, once the path departs even slightly from the central limit, greatest eclipse no longer falls at exact new moon.

sentences.zh: 至於虧复，相去尤遠。

translations.literal: As for eclipse beginning and end, the distance is especially great.
translations.idiomatic: At the limits of beginning and end, the distance is especially great.

sentences.zh: 西曆乃言交食必在朔、望，不用朓朒次差。

translations.literal: The Western calendar nevertheless says syzygy eclipses must occur at new and full moon, not using the secondary difference of waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: The Western calendar nevertheless insists that eclipses must fall at new and full moon and makes no use of the secondary waxing-and-waning correction.

sentences.zh: 當辨者八也。』

translations.literal: This is the eighth point that ought to be clarified.'
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth matter requiring clarification.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：『語云：「步歷甚難，辨歷甚易。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'As the saying goes: "Computing the calendar is very hard; distinguishing calendars is very easy."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'As the saying goes: "Computing a calendar is very hard; judging one is very easy."

sentences.zh: 蓋言象緯森羅，得失無所遁也。

translations.literal: It means that the stars and constellations stand densely arrayed—right and wrong cannot escape detection.
translations.idiomatic: It means that the stars stand densely arrayed in the sky—right and wrong cannot escape them.

sentences.zh: 據彼所說，亦未嘗自信無差。

translations.literal: According to what they say, they also have never confidently believed themselves without error.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by their own statements, they have never been fully confident of their own accuracy.

sentences.zh: 五星經度，或失二十餘分，躔離表驗，或失數分，交食值此，所失當以刻計；

translations.literal: The five planets' ecliptic longitudes may err by more than twenty minutes; transit and departure table verification may err by several minutes—when eclipses encounter this, the loss should be reckoned in ke;
translations.idiomatic: The five planets' ecliptic longitudes may err by more than twenty minutes, and transit tables by several minutes—when eclipses are affected, the error should be reckoned in ke;

sentences.zh: 凌犯值此，所失當以日計矣。

translations.literal: when occultations encounter this, the loss should be reckoned in days.
translations.idiomatic: when occultations are affected, the error should be reckoned in days.

sentences.zh: 故立法不久，違錯頗多，餘於歷說已辨一二。

translations.literal: Therefore the methods have not long been established and discrepancies are quite numerous—I have already clarified one or two points in my Discourse on Calendars.
translations.idiomatic: The system has not long been established and errors are numerous—I have already addressed one or two of them in my Discourse on Calendars.

sentences.zh: 乃癸卯七月望食當既不既，與夫失食失推者何異乎？

translations.literal: Yet the full-moon eclipse of the seventh month of guimao should not have been total—is this not the same as missing an eclipse or failing in prediction?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the full-moon eclipse of the seventh month of guimao should not have been total—how does that differ from missing an eclipse or botching a prediction?

sentences.zh: 且譯書之初，本言取西曆之材質，歸大統之型範，不謂盡隳成憲，而專用西法，如今日者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of translating the books, it was originally said to take the substance of the Western calendar and fit it to the model of the Great Uniformity—not to say utterly destroy established institutions and exclusively use Western methods, as today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the books were first translated the aim was to take the substance of the Western calendar and fit it to the Great Uniformity model—not to destroy established institutions entirely and rely exclusively on Western methods, as is done today.

sentences.zh: 餘故兼採中、西，去其疵類，參以己意，著曆法六篇，會通若干事，改正若干事，表明若干事，增輯若干事，立法若干事。

translations.literal: I therefore drew on both Chinese and Western [sources], removed their flaws, added my own views, and wrote six treatises on calendar methods—several matters harmonized, several corrected, several clarified, several supplemented and compiled, several methods newly established.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore drew on both Chinese and Western sources, removed their defects, added my own views, and wrote six treatises on calendar methods—harmonizing, correcting, clarifying, supplementing, and establishing new rules in various matters.

sentences.zh: 舊法雖舛，而未遽廢者，兩存之；

translations.literal: Though old methods are wrong, those not yet hastily abolished are preserved side by side;
translations.idiomatic: Where old methods are wrong but not yet ready for abolition, both versions are preserved;

sentences.zh: 理雖可知，而上下千年不得其數者，缺之；

translations.literal: though the principle can be known, where the numbers cannot be obtained across a thousand years up and down, gaps are left;
translations.idiomatic: where the principle is clear but the numbers cannot be obtained across a thousand years, gaps are left;

sentences.zh: 雖得其數，而遠引古測，未經目信者，別見補遺，而正文仍襲其故。

translations.literal: though the numbers are obtained, where ancient measurements are cited at far remove and not personally verified, separate supplements are given, while the main text still follows the old.
translations.idiomatic: where numbers are obtained but rest on ancient measurements at far remove and not personally verified, supplements are given separately while the main text retains the old reckoning.

sentences.zh: 為日一百幾十有幾，為文萬有千言，非敢妄雲窺其堂奧，庶幾初學之津梁也。』

translations.literal: It took more than a hundred and some days, and runs to more than ten thousand words—I do not dare presumptuously claim to have glimpsed the inner hall; I hope only to serve as a bridge for beginners.'
translations.idiomatic: The work took more than a hundred days and runs to more than ten thousand words. I do not dare claim to have glimpsed the inner sanctum; I hope only to serve as a bridge for beginners.'

sentences.zh: 其法：度法百分，日法百刻，週天三百六十五度二十五分六十五秒五十九微三十二纖，內外準分三十九分九十一秒四十九微，次準九十一分六十八秒八十六微，黃道歲差一分四十三秒七十三微二十六纖。

translations.literal: His method: the degree divisor is one hundred parts; the day divisor is one hundred ke; the circuit of heaven is 365 degrees 25 parts 65 seconds 59 micro-units 32 fibrils; inner and outer standard parts 39 parts 91 seconds 49 micro-units; secondary standard 91 parts 68 seconds 86 micro-units; ecliptic precession 1 part 43 seconds 73 micro-units 26 fibrils.
translations.idiomatic: His system used a degree divisor of one hundred parts and a day divisor of one hundred ke; the celestial circuit was 365° 25′ 65″ 59 micro-units 32 fibrils; inner and outer standard parts 39′ 91″ 49 micro-units; secondary standard 91′ 68″ 86 micro-units; and ecliptic precession 1′ 43″ 73 micro-units 26 fibrils.

sentences.zh: 列宿經緯：角一十度七十三分七十九秒，南二度一分二十三秒，亢一十度八十二分二十四秒，北三度一分一秒，氐一十八度一十六分一十四秒，北四十三分九十六秒，房四度八十三分六十三秒，南五度四十六分一十九秒，心七度六十六分二秒，南三度九十七分三十八秒，尾一十五度八十二分七十八秒，南一十五度二十一分九十秒，箕九度四十六分九十六秒，南六度五十九分四十九秒，南斗二十四度一十九分八十二秒，南三度八十八分九十三秒，牽牛七度七十九分五十五秒，北四度七十五分一十七秒，婺女一十一度八十二分二秒，北八度二十分五十九秒，虛一十度一十二分九十一秒，北八度八十二分七十秒，危二十度四十一分四秒，北一十度八十五分六十二秒，營室一十五度九十二分二十秒，北一十度七十一分七十一秒。

sentences.zh: 先是曉菴新法未成，作歷說六篇，歷策一篇，其說精核，與新法互有詳略。

translations.literal: Previously, before Xiao'an's new methods were complete, he wrote six essays in the Discourse on Calendars and one essay in Calendar Strategy—their arguments are precise and penetrating, and with the new methods each has areas of greater or lesser detail.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Xiao'an's new methods were complete, he wrote six essays in the Discourse on Calendars and one in Calendar Strategy—arguments precise and penetrating, each complementing the new methods with greater or lesser detail.

sentences.zh: 又隱括中、西步術，作大統西曆啟蒙。

translations.literal: He also compactly summarized Chinese and Western step methods and wrote Introduction to the Great Uniformity and Western Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He also compactly summarized Chinese and Western computational methods in Introduction to the Great Uniformity and Western Calendar.

sentences.zh: 丁未歲，因推步大統法作丁未歷稿。

translations.literal: In the dingwei year, applying the Great Uniformity step methods he wrote the Dingwei Calendar Draft.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingwei year he applied the Great Uniformity step methods to write the Dingwei Calendar Draft.

sentences.zh: 辛酉八月朔日食，以中、西法及己法豫定時刻分秒，至期，與徐發等以五家法同測，己法獨合，作推步交朔測小記。

translations.literal: At the new-moon solar eclipse of the eighth month of xinyou, using Chinese, Western, and his own methods he predetermined the hour, minute, and second; when the day came, together with Xu Fa and others he observed with five schools' methods—his alone matched; he wrote a brief record of step-method conjunction and new-moon observation.
translations.idiomatic: At the new-moon solar eclipse of the eighth month of xinyou he predetermined the hour, minute, and second using Chinese, Western, and his own methods; when the day came he observed with Xu Fa and others using five schools' methods—his alone matched—and he wrote a brief record of computational conjunction and new-moon observation.

sentences.zh: 又以治歷首重割圜，作圜解。

translations.literal: Also, because governing the calendar foremost emphasizes dividing the circle, he wrote Circle Solution.
translations.idiomatic: Because calendar-making above all depends on dividing the circle, he also wrote Circle Solution.

sentences.zh: 測天當據儀晷，造三晷，兼測日、月、星，因作三辰晷志。

translations.literal: Observing heaven should rely on instruments and gnomons; he made three gnomons for jointly observing sun, moon, and stars, and therefore wrote the Record of the Three Luminaries Gnomon.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly observation should rely on instruments and gnomons; he built three gnomons for joint observation of sun, moon, and stars and wrote the Record of the Three Luminaries Gnomon.

sentences.zh: 俱能究術數之微奧，補西人所不逮。

translations.literal: All were able to plumb the subtle profundities of calendrical arithmetic and remedy what Westerners did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: All these works plumb the subtle depths of calendrical arithmetic and remedy what Westerners had not reached.

sentences.zh: 與同時青州薛鳳祚齊名，稱『南王北薛』雲。

translations.literal: Contemporary with him, Qingzhou's Xue Fengzuo shared equal fame; they were called 'Wang in the south, Xue in the north,' it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He shared equal fame with his contemporary Xue Fengzuo of Qingzhou, and the pair were known as 'Wang in the south, Xue in the north.'

sentences.zh: 歷策有云：『每遇交會，必以所步、所測課較疏密，疾病寒暑無間，變週、改應、增損、經緯、遲疾諸率，於茲三十年所。』

translations.literal: Calendar Strategy says: 'Whenever conjunction occurred, he always compared computed and observed results for accuracy; through sickness, cold, and heat without interruption he altered cycle periods, adjusted epochs, increased and decreased, [revised] longitude and latitude, slow and fast ratios—all this for some thirty years.'
translations.idiomatic: Calendar Strategy says: 'At every conjunction he compared computed and observed results for accuracy; through sickness, cold, and heat without interruption he revised cycle periods, epochs, increments and decrements, longitudes and latitudes, and slow-and-fast ratios—for some thirty years.'

sentences.zh: 亦可以想見作者實測之詣力矣。

translations.literal: One can thus imagine the author's mastery and effort in actual observation.
translations.idiomatic: One can thus imagine the author's mastery and dedication in actual observation.

sentences.zh: 潘檉樟，字力田。

translations.literal: Pan Chengzhang, courtesy name Litian.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Chengzhang, whose courtesy name was Litian.

sentences.zh: 與王錫闡同邑友善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Wang Xichan, being from the same district.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Wang Xichan, being from the same district.

sentences.zh: 錫闡嘗館其家，講論算法，常窮日夜。

translations.literal: Xichan once lodged at his home, discussing calculation methods, often through entire days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: Xichan once lodged at his home and discussed calculation methods, often through entire days and nights.

sentences.zh: 檉樟著辛丑歷辨曰：『昔堯命羲和，曰以閏月定四時成歲，蓋曆法首重置閏。

translations.literal: Chengzhang wrote the Xinchou Calendar Discourse, saying: 'In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He, saying to fix the four seasons and complete the year by intercalary months—calendar methods from the first heavily emphasize setting intercalation.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhang wrote the Xinchou Calendar Discourse, saying: 'In antiquity Yao charged Xi and He to fix the four seasons and complete the year by intercalary months—calendar methods from the outset give foremost weight to intercalation.

sentences.zh: 而春秋傳曰：「先王之正時也，履端於始，舉正於中，歸餘於終。」

translations.literal: Yet the Zuo Commentary says: "When the former kings corrected the seasons, they tread the beginning at the start, raise correctness at the middle, and return the remainder at the end."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Zuo Commentary says: "When the former kings corrected the seasons, they tread the beginning at the start, raise correctness at the middle, and return the remainder at the end."

sentences.zh: 所謂始者，取氣朔分齊為曆元也；

translations.literal: What is called 'start' means taking the division and alignment of qi and new moon as the calendar epoch;
translations.idiomatic: What is called 'start' means taking the alignment of qi and new moon as the calendar epoch;

sentences.zh: 所謂中者，月以中氣為定，無中氣者則為閏也；

translations.literal: what is called 'middle' means fixing the month by median qi—one without median qi is intercalary;
translations.idiomatic: what is called 'middle' means fixing the month by median qi—a month without median qi is intercalary;

sentences.zh: 所謂終者，積氣盈、朔虛之數而閏生焉也。

translations.literal: what is called 'end' means that when accumulated qi surplus and new-moon deficit reach their number, intercalation arises.
translations.idiomatic: what is called 'end' means that when accumulated qi surplus and new-moon deficit reach their limit, intercalation arises.

sentences.zh: 自漢以降，歷術雖屢變，未有能易此者。

translations.literal: From Han downward, though calendar methods changed repeatedly, none could alter this.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasty onward, though calendar methods changed repeatedly, none could alter this principle.

sentences.zh: 唯西域諸歷則不然，其法有閏年、有閏日，而無閏月。

translations.literal: Only the various Western-region calendars are not so—their methods have intercalary years and intercalary days, but no intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Only the various Western-region calendars differ—their systems have intercalary years and intercalary days, but no intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 蓋中歷主日，而西曆主度，不可強同也。

translations.literal: For the Chinese calendar is day-centered while the Western calendar is degree-centered—they cannot be forcibly made the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Chinese calendar is day-centered and the Western calendar degree-centered—they cannot be forcibly equated.

sentences.zh: 今之為西曆者，乃以日躔求定氣、求閏月，不惟盡廢中國之成憲，而亦自悖西域之本法矣。

translations.literal: Those who now make the Western calendar seek true qi and intercalary months from solar motion—not only utterly abolishing China's established institutions, but also contradicting the Western region's original methods.
translations.idiomatic: Those who now compile the Western calendar seek true qi and intercalary months from solar motion—not only abolishing China's established institutions but contradicting the Western region's own original methods.

sentences.zh: 故十餘年來，宮度既紊，氣序亦訛。

translations.literal: Therefore over more than ten years, lodge degrees are already in disorder and the sequence of qi is also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years lodge degrees have fallen into disorder and the sequence of qi has gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 如戊子之閏三月也，而置在四月；

translations.literal: For example, intercalation should have been the third month of wuzi, yet it was placed in the fourth;
translations.idiomatic: In wuzi, intercalation should have fallen in the third month but was placed in the fourth;

sentences.zh: 庚寅之閏十一月也，而置在明年之二月；

translations.literal: intercalation should have been the eleventh month of gengyin, yet it was placed in the second month of the following year;
translations.idiomatic: in gengyin, intercalation should have fallen in the eleventh month but was placed in the second month of the following year;

sentences.zh: 癸巳之閏七月也，而置在六月；

translations.literal: intercalation should have been the seventh month of guisi, yet it was placed in the sixth.
translations.idiomatic: in guisi, intercalation should have fallen in the seventh month but was placed in the sixth.

sentences.zh: 己亥之閏正月也，而置在三月。

translations.literal: intercalation should have been the first month of jihai, yet it was placed in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: in jihai, intercalation should have fallen in the first month but was placed in the third.

sentences.zh: 其為舛誤，何可勝言！

translations.literal: as for its errors and mistakes, how can one speak of them all!
translations.idiomatic: such errors are beyond reckoning!

sentences.zh: 然非深於歷者，未易指摘。

translations.literal: yet unless one is deeply versed in calendrics, it is not easy to point them out.
translations.idiomatic: yet only those deeply versed in calendrics can readily expose them.

sentences.zh: 至於辛丑之閏月，則其失顯然無以自解矣。

translations.literal: as for the intercalary month of xinchou, its error is plainly obvious and cannot be explained away.
translations.idiomatic: but in xinchou, the error in placing the intercalary month is plainly indefensible.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 閏法論平氣而不當論定氣，若以平氣，則是年小雪在十月晦，冬至在十一月朔，而閏在兩月之間。

translations.literal: intercalation law discusses mean qi and ought not discuss true qi; if one uses mean qi, then that year Minor Snow falls on the last day of the tenth month, the winter solstice on the first day of the eleventh month, and intercalation falls between the two months.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation law treats mean qi, not true qi; under mean qi, that year Minor Snow would fall on the last day of the tenth month, the winter solstice on the first of the eleventh, and intercalation would fall between the two months.

sentences.zh: 所謂閏前之月中氣在晦，閏後之月中氣在朔者也。

translations.literal: this is what is meant by 'before intercalation the month's median qi is on the last day, after intercalation the month's median qi is on the first day.'
translations.idiomatic: This is the principle that before intercalation the month's median qi falls on the last day, and after intercalation on the first.

sentences.zh: 今以定氣，則秋分居九月朔，故預於七月朔置閏，然後秋分仍在八月，而霜降、小雪各歸其月。

translations.literal: now using true qi, the autumn equinox falls on the first of the ninth month, hence intercalation is placed in advance at the first of the seventh month, so that the autumn equinox still remains in the eighth month, and Frost Descent and Minor Snow each return to their proper months.
translations.idiomatic: Under true qi, the autumn equinox falls on the first of the ninth month, so they place intercalation early, at the first of the seventh, to keep the equinox in the eighth month and restore Frost Descent and Minor Snow to their proper months.

sentences.zh: 無如大寒定氣乃在十一月朔，而十二月又無中氣，既不可再置一閏，則是同一無中氣之月，而或閏或否。

translations.literal: but alas, true qi for Major Cold falls on the first of the eleventh month, and the twelfth month again has no median qi; since one cannot again place an intercalation, the same kind of month without median qi is sometimes intercalary and sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Major Cold falls on the first of the eleventh month, and the twelfth month again lacks median qi; unable to add another intercalation, they leave the same kind of month sometimes intercalary and sometimes not.

sentences.zh: 彼所云太陽不及交宮即置為閏者，何獨於此而自背其法乎？

translations.literal: what they call 'when the sun fails to reach the palace of intersection, set it as intercalation'—why alone here do they turn against their own rule?
translations.idiomatic: They say that when the sun fails to reach the palace of intersection, intercalation is required—why do they alone abandon that rule here?

sentences.zh: 蓋孟秋非歸餘之終，故天正不能履端於始，地正不能舉正於中也。

translations.literal: for the first month of autumn is not the end of the accumulated remainder, hence the heavenly first month cannot 'tread the beginning at the start,' nor the earthly first month 'raise the correct at the middle.'
translations.idiomatic: The first month of autumn does not mark the end of the accumulated remainder, so the heavenly year cannot begin at the proper start, nor the earthly year hold its proper middle.

sentences.zh: 如此，則四時不定，歲功不成，而閏法又安用之？

translations.literal: if so, the four seasons are unsettled, the year's work cannot be accomplished, and of what use is intercalation law?
translations.idiomatic: Then the four seasons lose their order, the year's work cannot be completed, and what use remains for intercalation law?

sentences.zh: 且壬寅正月，定朔舊法在丙子丑初，即彼法亦在丙子子正，則辛丑之季冬當為大盡，而明年正月中氣复移於今歲之秒。

translations.literal: moreover, for the first month of renyin, the old fixed-new-moon method places it at the beginning of the second quarter of bingzi; even by their method it falls at the first quarter of bingzi, so the last winter month of xinchou ought to be a full month, yet next year's first-month median qi again shifts into the last moments of this year.
translations.idiomatic: In renyin, the old fixed-new-moon method puts the first month at the beginning of the second quarter of bingzi; even by their own reckoning it falls at the first quarter of bingzi, so xinchou's last winter month should be a full month—yet next year's first-month median qi shifts back into the final moments of this year.

sentences.zh: 彼亦自覺其未安，故進歲朔於乙亥，而季冬為小盡之月，皆所謂欲蓋彌彰者耳。

translations.literal: they too felt their method was unsound, hence they advanced the year's new moon to yihai and made the last winter month a short month—all what is called 'trying to cover up only reveals more.'
