translations.idiomatic: Finding their own method unsatisfactory, they advanced the year's new moon to yihai and made the last winter month short—a classic case of trying to cover up only to reveal more.

sentences.zh: 即辛丑歲朔，以彼法推，當會於亥正，而今在戌正，差至六刻，其他牴牾，更難枚舉。

translations.literal: even for xinchou's year new moon, calculated by their method it ought to coincide at the first quarter of hai, yet now it falls at the first quarter of xu—a discrepancy of six quarters; other contradictions are even harder to enumerate.
translations.idiomatic: For xinchou's year new moon, their method would place it at the first quarter of hai, yet it falls at the first quarter of xu—a six-quarter error; other contradictions are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 作法如是，而猶自以為盡善，可乎​​？

translations.literal: to make a method like this and still deem it perfect—is that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: To craft a method like this and still call it perfect—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: 蓋其說以日行盈縮為節氣短長，每遇日行最盈，則一月可置一氣，是古有氣盈、朔虛，而今更有氣虛、朔盈矣。

translations.literal: their doctrine takes solar motion's excess and deficit as the shortening and lengthening of qi; whenever solar motion is most full, one month can hold one qi—in antiquity there were qi surplus and new-moon deficit, but now there are also qi deficit and new-moon surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Their doctrine treats the sun's varying speed as the shortening and lengthening of qi; when the sun moves fastest, one month can hold only one qi—in antiquity there were qi surplus and new-moon deficit, but now qi deficit and new-moon surplus appear as well.

sentences.zh: 然或晦朔兩節而中氣介其間。

translations.literal: yet sometimes the last and first days are two qi with median qi intervening between them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sometimes two qi fall on the last and first days with median qi sandwiched between.

sentences.zh: 如丙戌仲冬，去閏稍遠，猶可不論；

translations.literal: as in the mid-winter of bingxu, far from intercalation, one may still leave it aside;
translations.idiomatic: In bingxu's mid-winter, far from intercalation, one might overlook the point;

sentences.zh: 獨辛丑仲冬，冬至、大寒俱在晦朔，去閏最近，進退無據。

translations.literal: only in the mid-winter of xinchou, the winter solstice and Major Cold both fall on the last and first days, nearest to intercalation, with no ground for advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: but in xinchou's mid-winter, the winter solstice and Major Cold both fall on the last and first days, closest to intercalation, leaving no firm ground for either course.

sentences.zh: 苟且遷就，有不勝其弊者。

translations.literal: making shift as best one can, there are harms one cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: Patchwork compromises produce evils that cannot be borne.

sentences.zh: 夫閏法之主平氣，行之已數千年矣，今一變其術，未久而輒窮，至於無可如何，則又安取紛更為也！』

translations.literal: intercalation law chiefly uses mean qi and has been practiced for several thousand years; now changing the art, before long it is exhausted, until nothing can be done—then why bother with constant revisions!'
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation law has rested on mean qi for thousands of years; change the method and it is soon exhausted, until nothing can be done—why then pursue endless revisions!'

sentences.zh: 檉樟後坐法死。

translations.literal: Chengzhang afterward was put to death under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhang was later executed under the law.

sentences.zh: 弟耒，亦學曆算，見文苑傳。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lei also studied calendrics and calculation; see the Literary Worthies biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lei also studied calendrics and calculation; see the Literary Worthies biography.

sentences.zh: 方中通，字位伯，桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Zhongtong, courtesy name Weibo, a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhongtong, whose courtesy name was Weibo, was a native of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 集諸家之說，著數度衍二十四卷，附錄一卷。

translations.literal: He collected the theories of various schools and wrote Shudu Yan in twenty-four juan, with one supplementary juan.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the theories of various schools and wrote Shudu Yan in twenty-four juan, with one supplementary juan.

sentences.zh: 言：『九章皆出於句股，環矩以為圓，合矩以為方，方數為典。

translations.literal: He wrote: 'The Nine Chapters all derive from right triangles; circling the square makes a circle, joining squares makes a square, and square numbers are the standard.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'The Nine Chapters all derive from right triangles; circling the square yields a circle, joining squares yields a square, and square numbers are the standard.

sentences.zh: 以方出圓，句股之所生也；

translations.literal: deriving circle from square is what right triangles produce;
translations.idiomatic: deriving the circle from the square is what right triangles produce;

sentences.zh: 少廣，方圓所出也。

translations.literal: finding side and breadth is what square and circle produce.
translations.idiomatic: Finding side and breadth derives from square and circle.

sentences.zh: 方田、商功，皆少廣所出。

translations.literal: Field measurement and construction works both derive from finding side and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Field measurement and construction works both derive from finding side and breadth.

sentences.zh: 一方一圓，其間不齊，始出差分，而均輸對差分之數，盈朒借差求均。

translations.literal: One square and one circle, between them unequal, first produce proportional division; fair distribution counters proportional division, surplus and deficit borrows differences to seek balance.
translations.idiomatic: Where square and circle do not align, proportional division first arises; fair distribution counters proportional division, and surplus and deficit borrow differences to seek balance.

sentences.zh: 又差分、均輸所出，而以方程濟其窮。

translations.literal: These again derive from proportional division and fair distribution, while simultaneous equations resolve what they cannot.
translations.idiomatic: These in turn derive from proportional division and fair distribution, while simultaneous equations resolve what they cannot.

sentences.zh: 度量衡原出黃鍾，粟佈出焉，黃鍾出於方圓者也。』

translations.literal: Weights and measures originally derived from the Yellow Bell; millet spread out came from it—the Yellow Bell comes from square and circle.'
translations.idiomatic: Weights and measures originally derived from the Yellow Bell, and millet spread out from it—the Yellow Bell itself comes from square and circle.'

sentences.zh: 又言：『古法用竹徑一寸長六分二百七十一而成六觚為一握，後世有珠算而古法亡矣。

translations.literal: He also wrote: 'The ancient method used bamboo one inch in diameter and two hundred seventy-one six-tenths long, shaped into a hexagonal grip; later generations had the abacus and the ancient method was lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: 'The ancient method used bamboo one inch in diameter and two hundred seventy-one six-tenths long, shaped into a hexagonal grip; later generations had the abacus, and the ancient method was lost.

sentences.zh: 泰西之筆算、籌算，皆出九九。

translations.literal: Western pen calculation and tally calculation both derive from the nine-nine table.
translations.idiomatic: Western pen calculation and tally calculation both derive from the nine-nine multiplication table.

sentences.zh: 尺算即比例規，出三角。

translations.literal: Ruler calculation is the proportional compass, derived from trigonometry.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler calculation is the proportional compass, derived from trigonometry.

sentences.zh: 乘莫善於籌，除莫善於筆，加減莫善於珠，比例莫善於尺。』

translations.literal: For multiplication nothing beats tallies, for division nothing beats the pen, for addition and subtraction nothing beats the abacus, for proportion nothing beats the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: For multiplication nothing beats tallies, for division nothing beats the pen, for addition and subtraction nothing beats the abacus, and for proportion nothing beats the ruler.'

sentences.zh: 其珠算歸法，三一三十一，四一二十二之類，『十』字俱作『餘』字。

translations.literal: His abacus 'return' methods—such as 'three-one thirty-one, four-one twenty-two'—all write the character 'ten' as 'remainder.'
translations.idiomatic: In his abacus division mnemonics—such as 'three-one thirty-one, four-one twenty-two'—the character for 'ten' is always written as 'remainder.'

sentences.zh: 其尺算以三尺交加，取數祗用平分一線。

translations.literal: His ruler calculation joins three rulers crosswise and takes numbers using only one bisecting line.
translations.idiomatic: In his ruler calculation three rulers are joined crosswise, and numbers are taken using only a single bisecting line.

sentences.zh: 時廣昌揭暄亦明算術，與中通論難日輪大小，得光肥影瘦之故，及古今歲差之不同，須測算消長以齊之。

translations.literal: At the time Jie Xuan of Guangchang also mastered calculation; he and Zhongtong debated the size of the solar wheel, arriving at why light is broad and shadow narrow, and that ancient and modern precession differ and must be matched by measurement and calculation of waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jie Xuan of Guangchang also mastered calculation; he and Zhongtong debated the size of the solar wheel, explaining why light appears broad and shadow narrow, and that ancient and modern precession differ and must be reconciled by measurement and calculation of their waxing and waning.

sentences.zh: 一晝夜人一萬三千五百息，每息宗動天行十萬里有奇。

translations.literal: In one day and night a person breathes thirteen thousand five hundred breaths; each breath the Primum Mobile travels more than one hundred thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In one day and night a person takes thirteen thousand five hundred breaths; with each breath the Primum Mobile travels more than one hundred thousand li.

sentences.zh: 別錄為一書，曰揭方問答。

translations.literal: This was separately recorded as a book called Jie Fang Wend Da.
translations.idiomatic: This was separately recorded as a book called Questions and Answers with Jie on Surveying.

sentences.zh: 揭暄，字子宣，廣昌人。

translations.literal: Jie Xuan, courtesy name Zixuan, a native of Guangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Xuan, whose courtesy name was Zixuan, was a native of Guangchang.

sentences.zh: 著璇璣遺述七卷，一名寫天新語。

translations.literal: He wrote Xuanji Yishu in seven juan, also called Xietian Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Xuanji Yishu in seven juan, also known as Xietian Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 論日月東行如槽之滾丸，而月質不變。

translations.literal: He argued that sun and moon move eastward like a ball rolling in a trough, while the moon's substance does not change.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the sun and moon move eastward like a ball rolling in a trough, while the moon's substance remains unchanged.

sentences.zh: 又謂七政之小輪。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the minor epicycles of the seven luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke of the minor epicycles of the seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 皆出自然，如盤水之運旋而周遭，以行疾而成旋渦，遂成留逆。

translations.literal: all arising naturally, like water swirling in a basin and circling about—as swift motion forms a vortex, retrograde and station result.
translations.idiomatic: all arise naturally, like water swirling in a basin and circling about—as swift motion forms a vortex, station and retrograde motion result.

sentences.zh: 於五星西行，日月盈縮，皆設譬多方，言之近理。

translations.literal: On the five planets' westward motion and the sun and moon's excess and deficit, he offered many analogies that sound plausible.
translations.idiomatic: On the five planets' westward motion and the sun and moon's varying speed, he offered many analogies that sound plausible.

sentences.zh: 康熙己巳，以草稿寄梅文鼎，抄其精語為一卷，稱其『深明西術，而又別有悟入，其言多古今所未發』。

translations.literal: In the jisi year of Kangxi he sent a draft to Mei Wending, who copied its finest passages into one juan, praising him as 'deeply versed in Western methods yet with separate insight of his own; his remarks mostly express what antiquity and the present had never articulated.'
translations.idiomatic: In the jisi year of Kangxi he sent a draft to Mei Wending, who copied its finest passages into one juan and praised him as 'deeply versed in Western methods yet with insight of his own; his remarks mostly say what antiquity and the present had never articulated.'

sentences.zh: 卒年逾八十。

translations.literal: He died aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 梅文鼎，字定九，號勿庵，宣城人。

translations.literal: Mei Wending, courtesy name Dingjiu, style name Wu'an, a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Wending, whose courtesy name was Dingjiu and style name Wu'an, was a native of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 兒時侍父士昌及塾師羅王賓仰觀星象，輒了然於次舍運轉大意。

translations.literal: As a child, attending his father Shichang and tutor Luo Wangbin, he would gaze at the stars and immediately grasp the broad pattern of lodges and their motion.
translations.idiomatic: As a child, while attending his father Shichang and tutor Luo Wangbin, he would gaze at the stars and immediately grasp the broad pattern of lodges and their motion.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，師事竹冠道士倪觀湖，受麻孟旋所藏台官交食法，與弟文鼐、文鼏共習之。

translations.literal: At twenty-seven he took the Bamboo-Crowned Daoist Ni Guanhu as his master, receiving the Bureau Methods for Conjunctions and Eclipses kept by Ma Mengxuan, and studied them with his brothers Wenlin and Wenji.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he took the Bamboo-Crowned Daoist Ni Guanhu as his master, received the Bureau Methods for Conjunctions and Eclipses kept by Ma Mengxuan, and studied them with his brothers Wenlin and Wenji.

sentences.zh: 稍稍發明其立法之故，補其遺缺，著歷學駢枝二卷，後增為四卷，倪為首肯。

translations.literal: He gradually explained the reasons behind the methods, filled their gaps, and wrote Calendar Learning Parallels in two juan, later expanded to four; Ni approved.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually explained the reasons behind the methods, filled their gaps, and wrote Calendar Learning Parallels in two juan, later expanded to four; Ni gave his approval.

sentences.zh: 值書之難讀者，必欲求得其說，往往廢寢忘食。

translations.literal: Whenever he encountered a difficult book, he had to obtain its meaning, often neglecting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he encountered a difficult book, he had to grasp its meaning, often neglecting sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 殘編散帖，手自抄集，一字異同，不敢忽過。

translations.literal: From scattered fragments and loose sheets he copied and assembled by hand, not daring to overlook even a single character's difference.
translations.idiomatic: From scattered fragments and loose sheets he copied and assembled by hand, not daring to overlook even a single character's difference.

sentences.zh: 疇人子弟及西域官生，皆折節造訪，有問者，亦詳告之無隱，期與斯世共明之。

translations.literal: Disciples of calendrical families and Western-region official students all humbled themselves to visit; to any who asked, he explained fully without concealment, hoping to clarify matters together with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples of calendrical families and Western-region official students all humbled themselves to visit him; to any who asked, he explained fully without concealment, hoping to clarify matters together with the age.

sentences.zh: 所著曆算之書凡八十餘種。

translations.literal: The books on calendrics and calculation that he wrote numbered more than eighty kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The books on calendrics and calculation that he wrote numbered more than eighty kinds.

sentences.zh: 讀元史授時曆經，歎其法之善，作元史歷經補註二卷。

translations.literal: Reading the Shoushi Calendar Classic in the Yuan History, he admired the excellence of its methods and wrote Supplementary Notes to the Yuan History Calendar Classic in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Shoushi Calendar Classic in the Yuan History, he admired the excellence of its methods and wrote Supplementary Notes to the Yuan History Calendar Classic in two juan.

sentences.zh: 又以授時集古法大成，因參校古術七十餘家，著古今曆法通考七十餘卷。

translations.literal: Seeing that Shoushi gathered ancient methods into a great synthesis, he collated more than seventy ancient methods and wrote Comprehensive Inquiry into Ancient and Modern Calendar Methods in more than seventy juan.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Shoushi gathered ancient methods into a great synthesis, he collated more than seventy ancient methods and wrote Comprehensive Inquiry into Ancient and Modern Calendar Methods in more than seventy juan.

sentences.zh: 授時以六術考古今冬至，取魯獻公冬至證統天術之疏，然依其本法步算，與授時所得正同，作春秋以來冬至考一卷。

translations.literal: Shoushi used six methods to investigate ancient and modern winter solstices; taking Duke Xian of Lu's winter solstice to prove the deficiencies of the Tongtian method, yet following its original method in step calculation, the result matched Shoushi exactly—he wrote Investigation of Winter Solstices since the Spring and Autumn in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi used six methods to investigate ancient and modern winter solstices; taking Duke Xian of Lu's winter solstice to prove the deficiencies of the Tongtian method, yet following its original method in step calculation, the result matched Shoushi exactly—he wrote Investigation of Winter Solstices since the Spring and Autumn Annals in one juan.

sentences.zh: 元史西征庚午元術，西征者，謂太祖庚辰；

translations.literal: The Yuan History's Western Campaign Gengwu Origin method—'Western Campaign' refers to Taizu's gengchen year;
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan History's Western Campaign Gengwu Origin method—'Western Campaign' refers to Taizu's gengchen year;

sentences.zh: 庚午元者，上元起算之端也。

translations.literal: 'Gengwu Origin' is the starting point for upper-origin reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: 'Gengwu Origin' is the starting point for upper-origin reckoning.

sentences.zh: 曆志訛太祖庚辰為太宗，不知太宗無庚辰也。

translations.literal: The Calendar Treatise wrongly makes Taizu's gengchen into Taizong's, not knowing Taizong had no gengchen year.
translations.idiomatic: The Calendar Treatise wrongly makes Taizu's gengchen into Taizong's, not knowing Taizong had no gengchen year.

sentences.zh: 又訛上元為庚子，則於積年不合。

translations.literal: It also wrongly makes the upper origin gengzi, which then does not agree with the accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: It also wrongly makes the upper origin gengzi, which then does not agree with the accumulated years.

sentences.zh: 考而正之，作庚午元算考一卷。

translations.literal: He investigated and corrected this, writing Investigation of the Gengwu Origin Calculation in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated and corrected this, writing Investigation of the Gengwu Origin Calculation in one juan.

sentences.zh: 授時非諸古術所能方，郭守敬所著歷草，乃歷經立法之根，拈其義之精微者，為郭太史歷草補註二卷。

translations.literal: Shoushi cannot be matched by ancient methods; Guo Shoujing's Calendar Draft was the root of the calendar classic's methods—selecting the subtle points of its meaning, he wrote Supplementary Notes to Grand Astrologer Guo's Calendar Draft in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi cannot be matched by ancient methods; Guo Shoujing's Calendar Draft was the root of the calendar classic's methods—selecting the subtle points of its meaning, he wrote Supplementary Notes to Grand Astrologer Guo's Calendar Draft in two juan.

sentences.zh: 立成傳寫魯魚，不得其說，不敢妄用，作大統立成註二卷。

translations.literal: The ready tables in transmission had scribal errors and their meaning could not be obtained—he dared not use them arbitrarily, and wrote Notes on the Datong Ready Tables in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: The ready tables in transmission had scribal errors and their meaning could not be recovered—he dared not use them arbitrarily, and wrote Notes on the Datong Ready Tables in two juan.

sentences.zh: 授時術於日躔盈縮、月離遲疾，並以垛積招差立算，而九章諸書無此術，從未有能言其故者，作平立定三差詳說一卷，此發明古法者也。

translations.literal: Shoushi methods for solar motion excess and deficit and lunar motion slow and fast both use stacked accumulation and interpolation by differences; the Nine Chapters and other books have no such art, and none had ever been able to say why—he wrote Detailed Explanation of the Three Differences (Level, Upright, Fixed) in one juan—this elucidates ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushi methods for solar motion excess and deficit and lunar motion slow and fast both use stacked accumulation and finite-difference interpolation; the Nine Chapters and other books have no such art, and none had ever been able to say why—he wrote Detailed Explanation of the Three Differences (Level, Upright, Fixed) in one juan—this elucidates ancient methods.

sentences.zh: 唐九執術為西法之權輿，其後有婆羅門十一曜經及都聿利斯經，皆九執之屬。

translations.literal: Tang's Nine Executions method is the source of Western methods; afterward came the Brahmin Eleven Luminaries Sutra and the Zoroastrian Sutra, all belonging to the Nine Executions.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Nine Executions method is the source of Western methods; afterward came the Brahmin Eleven Luminaries Sutra and the Zoroastrian Sutra, all belonging to the Nine Executions.

sentences.zh: 在元則有札馬魯丁西域萬年術，在明則馬沙亦黑、馬哈麻之回回術、西域天文書，天順時具琳所刻天文實用，即本此書，作回回曆補註三卷，西域天文書補註二卷，三十雜星考一卷。

translations.literal: In Yuan there was Jamal al-Din's Western-region forever-year method; in Ming, Mashayihei and Mahama's Huihui methods and Western-region astronomical books; the Tianwen Shiyong engraved by Ju Lin in the Tianshun era was based on this book—he wrote Huihui Calendar Supplementary Notes in three juan, Western-region Astronomical Book Supplementary Notes in two juan, and Investigation of Thirty Miscellaneous Stars in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuan there was Jamal al-Din's Western-region perpetual-year method; in the Ming, Mashayihei and Mahama's Huihui methods and Western-region astronomical books; the Tianwen Shiyong engraved by Ju Lin in the Tianshun era was based on this book—he wrote Huihui Calendar Supplementary Notes in three juan, Western-region Astronomical Book Supplementary Notes in two juan, and Investigation of Thirty Miscellaneous Stars in one juan.

sentences.zh: 表景生於日軌之高下，日軌又因裡差變移，作四省表景立成一卷。

translations.literal: Shadow length arises from the sun's path's height and low; the sun's path in turn shifts with parallax—he wrote Ready Tables for Shadow Length of the Four Provinces in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow length arises from the height and low of the sun's path, and the sun's path in turn shifts with parallax—he wrote Ready Tables for Shadow Length of the Four Provinces in one juan.

sentences.zh: 周髀所言裡差之法，即西人之說所自出，作周髀算經補註一卷。

translations.literal: The parallax method spoken of in Zhou Bi is what Western doctrine derives from—he wrote Supplementary Notes to the Zhou Bi Suan Jing in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The parallax method spoken of in Zhou Bi is what Western doctrine derives from—he wrote Supplementary Notes to the Zhou Bi Suan Jing in one juan.

sentences.zh: 渾蓋之器，最便行測，作渾蓋通測憲圖說訂補一卷。

translations.literal: The armillary and celestial-globe instruments are most convenient for field measurement—he wrote Revised and Supplemented Illustrated Explanation of the Armillary and Celestial Globe for General Measurement in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The armillary and celestial-globe instruments are most convenient for field measurement—he wrote Revised and Supplemented Illustrated Explanation of the Armillary and Celestial Globe for General Measurement in one juan.

sentences.zh: 西國以太陽行黃道三十度為一月，作西國日月考一卷。

translations.literal: Western countries take the sun's thirty degrees along the ecliptic as one month—he wrote Investigation of Western Sun and Moon in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Western countries take the sun's thirty degrees along the ecliptic as one month—he wrote Investigation of Western Sun and Moon in one juan.

sentences.zh: 西術中有細草，猶授時之有通軌也，以歷指大意隱括而注之，作七政細草補註三卷。

translations.literal: Western methods have detailed procedures, as Shoushi has the general track—summarizing the Calendar Directive's main idea in condensed notes, he wrote Supplementary Notes to the Detailed Procedures of the Seven Luminaries in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: Western methods have detailed procedures, as Shoushi has the general track—summarizing the Calendar Directive's main idea in condensed notes, he wrote Supplementary Notes to the Detailed Procedures of the Seven Luminaries in three juan.

sentences.zh: 新法有交食蒙求、七政蒙引二書，並逸，作交食蒙求訂補二卷、附說二卷。

translations.literal: The New Methods had Mengqiu and Mengyin on eclipses and the seven luminaries, both lost—he wrote Revised and Supplemented Eclipse Mengqiu in two juan with two juan of appended explanations.
translations.idiomatic: The New Methods had Mengqiu and Mengyin on eclipses and the seven luminaries, both lost—he wrote Revised and Supplemented Eclipse Mengqiu in two juan with two juan of appended explanations.

sentences.zh: 監正楊光先不得已日食圖，以金環食與食甚分為二圖，而各有時刻，其誤非小，作交食作圖法訂誤一卷。

translations.literal: Supervisor Yang Guangxian, as a last resort on solar-eclipse diagrams, split the annular eclipse and greatest eclipse into two diagrams, each with its own time—the error is no small one—he wrote Correcting Errors in the Method of Drawing Eclipses in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Yang Guangxian, in his makeshift solar-eclipse diagrams, split the annular eclipse and greatest eclipse into two diagrams, each with its own time—the error is no small one—he wrote Correcting Errors in the Method of Drawing Eclipses in one juan.

sentences.zh: 新法以黃道求赤道交食，細草用儀象志表，不如弧三角之親切，作求赤道宿度法一卷。

translations.literal: The New Methods seek ecliptic-to-equator eclipses; the detailed procedures use tables from the Instrument Record, inferior to spherical trigonometry—he wrote Method for Finding Equatorial Lodge Degrees in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The New Methods seek ecliptic-to-equator eclipses; the detailed procedures use tables from the Instrument Record, inferior to spherical trigonometry—he wrote Method for Finding Equatorial Lodge Degrees in one juan.

sentences.zh: 謂中、西兩家之法，求交食起復方位，皆以東西南北為言。

translations.literal: He held that Chinese and Western methods alike, in seeking the directions of eclipse beginning and ending, speak only in terms of east, west, south, and north.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Chinese and Western methods alike, in seeking the directions of eclipse beginning and ending, speak only in terms of east, west, south, and north.

sentences.zh: 然東西南北惟日月行至午規而又近天頂，則四方各正其位。

translations.literal: Yet east, west, south, and north are correct in their positions only when sun and moon reach the meridian and are near the zenith.
translations.idiomatic: Yet east, west, south, and north are correct in their positions only when the sun and moon reach the meridian and are near the zenith.

sentences.zh: 非然，則黃道有斜正之殊，而自虧至复，經歷時刻，輾轉遷移，弧度之勢，頃刻易向。

translations.literal: Otherwise the ecliptic has variations of obliquity and rectitude, and from first contact to totality the elapsed times shift and turn—the arc's momentum changes direction in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the ecliptic has variations of obliquity and rectitude, and from first contact to totality the elapsed times shift and turn—the arc's momentum changes direction in an instant.

sentences.zh: 且北極有高下，而隨處所見必皆不同，勢難施諸測驗。

translations.literal: Moreover the north pole has varying altitude, and what is seen everywhere must differ—it is hard to apply to measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the north pole has varying altitude, and what is seen everywhere must differ—it is hard to apply to measurement.

sentences.zh: 今別立新法，不用東西南北之號，惟人所見日月員體，分為八向，以正對天頂處為上，對地平處為下，上下聯爲直線，作十字橫線，命之曰左、曰右，此四正向也；

translations.literal: He now set forth a new method, not using the names east, west, south, north, but only the round bodies of sun and moon as seen, divided into eight directions—taking the point directly opposite the zenith as 'above' and opposite the horizon as 'below,' linking above and below in a straight line and drawing a cross line, naming them 'left' and 'right'—these four are the cardinal directions;
translations.idiomatic: He now set forth a new method, not using the names east, west, south, and north, but only the round bodies of sun and moon as seen, divided into eight directions—taking the point directly opposite the zenith as 'above' and opposite the horizon as 'below,' linking above and below in a straight line and drawing a cross line, naming them 'left' and 'right'—these four are the cardinal directions;

sentences.zh: 曰上左、上右，曰下左、下右，則四隅向也。

translations.literal: 'Upper-left, upper-right,' 'lower-left, lower-right' are the four diagonal directions.
translations.idiomatic: 'Upper-left, upper-right,' 'lower-left, lower-right' are the four diagonal directions.

sentences.zh: 乃以定其受蝕之所在，則舉目可見，作交食管見一卷。

translations.literal: By this he fixed where the eclipse is received—visible at a glance—he wrote Eclipse Tube Observation in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: By this he fixed where the eclipse is received—visible at a glance—and wrote Eclipse Tube Observation in one juan.

sentences.zh: 太陽之有日差，猶月離交食之有加減時，因表說含糊有誤，作日差原理一卷。

translations.literal: The sun's solar parallax is like the added and subtracted times in lunar motion and eclipses; because the gnomon explanation was vague and wrong, he wrote Principles of Solar Parallax in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's solar parallax is like the added and subtracted times in lunar motion and eclipses; because the gnomon explanation was vague and wrong, he wrote Principles of Solar Parallax in one juan.

sentences.zh: 火星最為難算，至地谷而始密，解其立法之根，作火緯圖法一卷。

translations.literal: Mars is hardest to calculate; only with Tycho did it become precise—explaining the root of its methods, he wrote Diagram Method for Martian Longitude in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Mars is hardest to calculate; only with Tycho did it become precise—explaining the root of its methods, he wrote Diagram Method for Martian Longitude in one juan.

sentences.zh: 訂火緯表記，因及七政，作七政前均簡法一卷。

translations.literal: Revising the notes on the Martian table, extending to the seven luminaries, he wrote Simplified Method for the Seven Luminaries' Prior Mean in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Revising the notes on the Martian table and extending to the seven luminaries, he wrote Simplified Method for the Seven Luminaries' Prior Mean in one juan.

sentences.zh: 天問略取緯不真，而列表從之誤，作黃赤距緯圖辨一卷。

translations.literal: Tianwen Lüe takes incorrect declination but follows it in tables—he wrote Diagram Discourse on Right Ascension and Declination Distance in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianwen Lüe takes incorrect declination but follows it in tables—he wrote Diagram Discourse on Right Ascension and Declination Distance in one juan.

sentences.zh: 新法帝星、句陳經緯刊本互異，作帝星句陳經緯考異一卷。

translations.literal: In the New Methods, printed editions of the Imperial Star and Gouchen longitudes and latitudes differ—he wrote Investigation of Variants in the Imperial Star and Gouchen Longitudes and Latitudes in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the New Methods, printed editions of the Imperial Star and Gouchen longitudes and latitudes differ—he wrote Investigation of Variants in the Imperial Star and Gouchen Longitudes and Latitudes in one juan.

sentences.zh: 測帝星、句陳二星為定夜時之簡法，作星軌真度一卷。

translations.literal: Measuring the Imperial Star and Gouchen as a simplified method for fixing nighttime hours, he wrote True Degrees of Star Tracks in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring the Imperial Star and Gouchen as a simplified method for fixing nighttime hours, he wrote True Degrees of Star Tracks in one juan.

sentences.zh: 以上皆以發明新法算書，或正其誤，或補其缺也。

translations.literal: All the above elucidate the New Methods' computational books, correcting errors or filling gaps.
translations.idiomatic: All the above elucidate the New Methods' computational books, correcting errors or filling gaps.

sentences.zh: 康熙己未，明史開局，曆志為錢塘吳任臣分修，經嘉禾徐善、北平劉獻廷、毗陵楊文言，各有增定，最後以屬黃宗羲，又以屬文鼎，摘其訛誤五十餘處，以算草、通軌補之，作明史曆志擬稿一卷。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year of Kangxi the Ming History project opened; the Calendar Treatise was assigned to Qian Tang's Wu Renchen, with additions from Xu Shan of Jiahe, Liu Xianting of Beiping, and Yang Wenyan of Piling; lastly it was entrusted to Huang Zongxi, then again to Wending, who extracted more than fifty errors and supplemented them with calculation drafts and general tracks, writing Draft of the Ming History Calendar Treatise in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year of Kangxi the Ming History project opened; the Calendar Treatise was assigned to Wu Renchen of Qian Tang, with additions from Xu Shan of Jiahe, Liu Xianting of Beiping, and Yang Wenyan of Piling; lastly it was entrusted to Huang Zongxi, then again to Wending, who extracted more than fifty errors and supplemented them with calculation drafts and general tracks, writing Draft of the Ming History Calendar Treatise in one juan.

sentences.zh: 雖為大統而作，實以闡明授時之奧，補元史之缺略也。

translations.literal: Though written for the Datong system, it in fact elucidates the profundities of Shoushi and supplements the Yuan History's omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Though written for the Datong system, it in fact elucidates the profundities of Shoushi and supplements the Yuan History's omissions.

sentences.zh: 其總目凡三：曰法原，曰立成，曰推​​步。

translations.literal: Its general headings number three: Origins of Methods, Ready Tables, and Step Calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Its general headings number three: Origins of Methods, Ready Tables, and Step Calculation.

sentences.zh: 而法原之目七：曰句股測望，曰弧天割圜，曰黃赤道差，曰黃赤道內外度，曰白道交週，曰日月五星平立定三差，曰裡差刻漏。

translations.literal: Under Origins of Methods there are seven items: right-triangle surveying, arc-of-heaven circle-cutting, ecliptic-equator difference, inner and outer ecliptic-equator degrees, white-path cycle intersection, level-upright-fixed three differences of sun, moon, and five planets, and parallax clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Under Origins of Methods there are seven items: right-triangle surveying, arc-of-heaven circle-cutting, ecliptic-equator difference, inner and outer ecliptic-equator degrees, white-path cycle intersection, level-upright-fixed three differences of sun, moon, and five planets, and parallax clepsydra.

sentences.zh: 立成之目凡四：曰太陽盈縮，曰太陰遲疾，曰晝夜刻，曰五星盈縮。

translations.literal: Ready Tables has four items: solar excess and deficit, lunar slow and fast, day-night quarters, and five-planet excess and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Ready Tables has four items: solar excess and deficit, lunar slow and fast, day-night quarters, and five-planet excess and deficit.

sentences.zh: 推步之目凡六：曰氣朔，曰日躔，曰月離，曰中星，曰交食，曰五星。

translations.literal: Step Calculation has six items: qi and new moon, solar motion, lunar motion, culminating stars, eclipses, and five planets.
translations.idiomatic: Step Calculation has six items: qi and new moon, solar motion, lunar motion, culminating stars, eclipses, and five planets.

sentences.zh: 又作曆志贅言一卷，大意言：『明用大統，實即授時，宜詳元史缺載之事，以補其未備。

translations.literal: He also wrote one juan of Appended Remarks on the Calendar Treatise, the main point of which states: "The Ming used the Datong system, which in fact was the Shoushi system; one should detail what the Yuan History omitted, to supplement what it left incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote one juan of Appended Remarks on the Calendar Treatise, arguing in essence that "although the Ming used the Datong calendar, it was really the Shoushi system in practice, and that the Yuan History's omissions should be fully set forth to fill the gaps.

sentences.zh: 又回回曆承用三百年，法宜備書。

translations.literal: Further, the Hui calendar has been in use for three hundred years; its methods should be fully recorded in writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Islamic calendar had been used for three centuries as well, and its methods deserved full treatment.

sentences.zh: 又鄭世子歷學已經進呈，宜詳述。

translations.literal: Further, the calendar studies of Prince Zheng had already been submitted to the throne; they should be fully described.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zheng's calendar studies had already been presented to the throne and ought to be described in detail.

sentences.zh: 他如袁黃之曆法新書，唐順之、周學述之會通回曆，以庚午元曆之例例之，皆得附錄。

translations.literal: Others such as Yuan Huang's New Book of Calendrical Methods, and Tang Shunzhi and Zhou Xueshu's Unified Hui Calendar—treating them by the precedent of the Gengwu Epoch Calendar—could all be appended.
translations.idiomatic: Other works, such as Yuan Huang's New Book of Calendrical Methods and the Unified Hui Calendar by Tang Shunzhi and Zhou Xueshu, could be appended following the precedent set for the Gengwu Epoch Calendar.

sentences.zh: 其西洋歷方今現行，然崇禎朝徐、李諸公測驗改憲之功，不可沒也，亦宜備載緣起。』

translations.literal: Though the Western calendar is in use today, the achievements of Xu, Li, and others in testing and reforming the calendar in the Chongzhen reign cannot be effaced; their origins too should be fully recorded."
translations.idiomatic: The Western calendar was then in current use, yet the work of Xu, Li, and their colleagues during the Chongzhen reign in observation and calendar reform must not be forgotten; the origins of that reform also deserved full account."

sentences.zh: 己巳，至京師，謁李光地於邸第，謂曰；

translations.literal: On the jisi day, he arrived at the capital, visited Li Guangdi at his residence, and said:
translations.idiomatic: On a jisi day he reached the capital and called on Li Guangdi at his residence, saying:

sentences.zh: 『曆法至本朝大備矣，而經生家猶若望洋者，無快論以發其趣也。

translations.literal: 'Calendrical methods have been fully perfected in our dynasty, yet Confucian scholars still seem like those gazing at the ocean—there is no lively discourse to awaken their interest.
translations.idiomatic: 'Calendrical science is now thoroughly developed in our dynasty, yet classical scholars still stand before it like men gazing at the sea—there is no engaging work to stir their interest.

sentences.zh: 宜略仿元趙友欽革象新書體例，作簡要之書，俾人人得其門戶，則從事者多，此學庶將大顯。』

translations.literal: One should follow in outline the format of Zhao Youqin of the Yuan's New Book of Remodeling the Image, and write a concise book, so that all may find its gateway; then those who engage in it will be many, and this learning will perhaps greatly flourish.'
translations.idiomatic: He suggested writing a concise book modeled on the format of Zhao Youqin's New Book of Remodeling the Image, so that anyone could find a doorway into the subject—then more people would take it up, and the discipline might at last flourish widely.'

sentences.zh: 因作歷學疑問三卷。

translations.literal: Accordingly he wrote Questions on Calendar Studies in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis he wrote Questions on Calendar Studies in three juan.

sentences.zh: 光地扈駕南巡，駐蹕德州，有旨取所刻書籍回奏，光地匆遽未及攜帶，遂以所辢刻歷學疑問謹呈。

translations.literal: Guangdi accompanied the emperor on a southern tour; when the imperial procession halted at Dezhou, an edict ordered books that had been printed to be brought for report; Guangdi in haste had not been able to bring them along, so he respectfully submitted the hastily printed Questions on Calendar Studies instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdi accompanied the emperor on a southern tour and the court halted at Dezhou, an edict called for printed books to be presented. Guangdi had not brought his in the rush, so he respectfully submitted a freshly printed copy of Questions on Calendar Studies instead.

sentences.zh: 奉旨：『朕留心曆算多年，此事朕能決其是非，將書留覽再發。』

translations.literal: He received the edict: 'I have attended to calendrics and calculation for many years; in this matter I can determine right and wrong. Keep the book for my review and send it later.'
translations.idiomatic: The response came: 'I have devoted myself to calendrics and calculation for many years and can judge such matters myself. Keep the book for my review and submit it again later.'

sentences.zh: 二日後，召見光地，上云：『昨所呈書甚細心，且議論亦公平，此人用力深矣，朕帶回宮中仔細看閱。』

translations.literal: Two days later Guangdi was summoned; the emperor said: 'The book submitted yesterday shows great care, and the discussion is also fair. This man has labored deeply. I shall take it back to the palace and read it carefully.'
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Guangdi was summoned. The emperor said, 'Yesterday's book shows great care, and the argument is fair. This author has worked deeply. I shall take it back to the palace and read it through carefully.'

sentences.zh: 光地因求皇上親加御筆，批駁改定，上肯之。

translations.literal: Guangdi then asked that the emperor personally apply the brush to criticize and revise it; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi then asked the emperor to annotate and correct it in his own hand, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年癸未春，駕复南巡，於行在發回原書，面諭光地：『朕已細細看過。』

translations.literal: The next year, in spring of the guiwei year, the emperor again toured south; at the traveling palace he returned the original book and personally instructed Guangdi: 'I have already read it carefully.'
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, in the guiwei year, the emperor toured south again. At the traveling palace he returned the original book and told Guangdi in person, 'I have read it carefully.'

sentences.zh: 中間圈點塗抹及簽貼批語，皆上手筆也。

translations.literal: Among the circles, dots, emendations, and pasted annotation slips within, all were in the emperor's own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Every circle, deletion, and pasted marginal note in it was in the emperor's own hand.

sentences.zh: 光地復請此書疵繆所在，上云：『無疵繆，但算法未備。』

translations.literal: Guangdi again asked where the book's flaws lay; the emperor said: 'There are no flaws, but the computational methods are not yet complete.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi asked again where the book erred. The emperor said, 'There are no errors—but the computational methods are incomplete.'

sentences.zh: 蓋其書本未完成，故聖諭及之。

translations.literal: This was because the book itself was not yet finished, hence the sage's pronouncement touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial remark reflected the fact that the book was still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聖祖西巡，問隱淪之士，光地以關中李顒、河南張沐及文鼎三人對。

translations.literal: Before long, the Sage Emperor toured west and asked about reclusive scholars; Guangdi answered with three men: Li Yong of Guanzhong, Zhang Mu of Henan, and Wending.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on a western tour the Sage Emperor asked about scholars living in retirement, and Guangdi named three: Li Yong of Guanzhong, Zhang Mu of Henan, and Wending.

sentences.zh: 上亦夙知顒及文鼎，乙酉二月，南巡狩，光地以撫臣扈從，上問：『宣城處士梅文鼎焉在？』

translations.literal: The emperor had long known Yong and Wending as well. In the second month of the yiyou year, on a southern hunt, Guangdi followed as provincial governor; the emperor asked: 'Where is the Xuancheng recluse Mei Wending?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already knew Yong and Wending well. In the second month of the yiyou year, during a southern tour, Guangdi attended as provincial governor. The emperor asked, 'Where is the Xuancheng recluse Mei Wending?'

sentences.zh: 光地以『尚在臣署』對。

translations.literal: Guangdi answered, 'He is still at my office.'
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi replied, 'He is still at my office.'

sentences.zh: 上曰：『朕歸時，汝與偕來，朕將面見。』

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'When I return, bring him with you; I shall meet him in person.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'When I return, bring him with me—I shall see him in person.'

sentences.zh: 四月十九日，光地與文鼎伏迎河干，越晨，俱召對御舟中，從容垂問，至於移時，如是者三日。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the fourth month, Guangdi and Wending prostrated themselves to welcome him at the riverbank; the next morning both were summoned for audience in the imperial boat, questioned at leisure for considerable time—so for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day of the fourth month, Guangdi and Wending waited by the river to receive the emperor. The next morning both were summoned to audience aboard the imperial boat and questioned at length, leisurely and without haste—and so for three days running.

sentences.zh: 上謂光地曰：『歷象算法，朕最留心，此學今鮮知者，如文鼎，真僅見也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Guangdi: 'Astronomy and computation I follow most closely; few now understand this learning—someone like Wending is truly rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Guangdi, 'Astronomy and calculation are what I follow most closely. Few people today know this field—someone like Wending is truly a rare find.

sentences.zh: 其人亦雅士，惜乎老矣！』

translations.literal: The man is also a refined scholar—alas, he is old!'
translations.idiomatic: He is a cultivated man as well—alas, he is old!'

sentences.zh: 連日賜御書扇幅，頒賜珍饌。

translations.literal: For days he was granted imperial calligraphy on fans, and fine delicacies were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: For several days running the emperor bestowed fans bearing his own calligraphy and sent him choice delicacies.

sentences.zh: 臨辭，特賜『績學參微』四大字。

translations.literal: At parting he was specially granted four large characters: 'Penetrating Subtlety through Sustained Learning.'
translations.idiomatic: At their parting he was specially granted four characters in the emperor's hand: 'Penetrating Subtlety through Sustained Learning.'

sentences.zh: 越明年，又命其孫瑴成內廷學習。

translations.literal: The following year he furthermore ordered Wending's grandson Jucheng to study within the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he also ordered Wending's grandson Jucheng to study at the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，瑴成奉上諭：『汝祖留心律曆多年，可將律呂正義寄一部去，令看，或有錯處，指出甚好。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, Jucheng received an imperial pronouncement: 'Your grandfather has attended to pitch-pipes and calendar for many years. Send him a copy of Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes to read; if there are errors, pointing them out would be excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year Jucheng received an imperial message: 'Your grandfather has devoted himself to pitch-pipes and calendrics for many years. Send him a copy of Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes to examine. If he finds mistakes, it would be excellent for him to point them out.

sentences.zh: 夫古帝王有「都俞籲咈」四字，後來遂止有「都俞」，即朋友之間，亦不喜人規勸，此皆是私意。

translations.literal: Ancient emperors had the four words 'assenting, approving, calling out, dissenting'; later there remained only 'assenting and approving.' Even among friends, people no longer welcome being admonished—all this comes from private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers honored the four words 'assent, approve, call out, and dissent'; later only 'assent and approve' remained. Even among friends, people no longer welcome correction—all of this springs from private feeling.

sentences.zh: 汝等須竭力克去，則學問長進。

translations.literal: You must strive with all force to overcome this, and then learning will advance.
translations.idiomatic: You must strive with all your strength to overcome this, and your learning will advance.

sentences.zh: 可並將此意寫與汝祖知之。』

translations.literal: You may also write this meaning to your grandfather so that he knows it.'
translations.idiomatic: Write this as well to your grandfather so that he may know my meaning.'

sentences.zh: 恩寵為古所未有。

translations.literal: Such favor had no precedent in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Such imperial favor was without precedent.

sentences.zh: 文鼎圖注各直省及蒙古各地南北東西之差，為書一卷，名分天度裡。

translations.literal: Wending diagrammed and annotated the north-south and east-west differences of each province and various regions of Mongolia, writing one juan titled Dividing Celestial Degrees into Li.
translations.idiomatic: Wending mapped and annotated the north-south and east-west differences among the provinces and Mongol regions, producing one juan titled Dividing Celestial Degrees into Li.

sentences.zh: 地既渾員，則所云二百五十里一度，緯度則然，若經度離赤道遠，則里數漸狹。

translations.literal: Since the earth is a complete sphere, what is called two hundred fifty li per degree holds for latitude; but if longitude is far from the equator, the li per degree gradually narrows.
translations.idiomatic: Because the earth is a sphere, the figure of two hundred fifty li per degree applies to latitude; the farther one moves from the equator in longitude, the narrower each degree becomes in li.

sentences.zh: 故惟路正東西行，自有一定算法；

translations.literal: Therefore only when the route goes due east or west is there a fixed computational method;
translations.idiomatic: Only for routes running due east or west is there a fixed method of calculation;

sentences.zh: 路或斜行，則其法不可用為立法。

translations.literal: if the route runs obliquely, that method cannot be used to establish a normative rule.
translations.idiomatic: if the route runs obliquely, that method cannot serve as a general law.

sentences.zh: 若兩地各有北極高度，又有相距之經度，而無相距里數，是有兩邊一角，而求餘一邊，即可以知斜距之裡。

translations.literal: If two places each have polar altitude, and there is longitudinal difference between them but no distance in li, one has two sides and one angle and seeks the remaining side—then one can know the oblique distance in li.
translations.idiomatic: Given the polar altitude at two places and the longitudinal difference between them, but not the distance in li, one has two sides and one angle and can solve for the remaining side—thus obtaining the oblique distance in li.

sentences.zh: 若先有斜距之里數而求經度，是為三邊求角，亦可以知相距之經度。

translations.literal: If one first has the oblique distance in li and seeks longitude, this is finding an angle from three sides; one can likewise know the longitudinal difference between them.
translations.idiomatic: If one begins with the oblique distance in li and seeks the longitude, it becomes a three-sides-to-angle problem, and the longitudinal difference can be found the same way.

sentences.zh: 其法並用斜弧三角形立算，可與月食求經度之法相參，而且簡易的確。

translations.literal: The method uses spherical triangles throughout for calculation; it can be compared with the method of finding longitude from lunar eclipses, and is moreover simple, easy, and exact.
translations.idiomatic: The method relies throughout on spherical trigonometry; it compares well with finding longitude from lunar eclipses, and is at once simple and exact.

sentences.zh: 文鼎於測算之圖與器，一見即得要領，古六合、三辰、四遊之儀，以意約為小制，皆合。

translations.literal: Wending, regarding diagrams and instruments for surveying and calculation, grasped the essentials at first sight; the ancient instruments of the Six Harmonies, Three Luminaires, and Four Wanders—he reduced them by design to small models, all matching.
translations.idiomatic: In surveying diagrams and instruments, Wending grasped essentials at a glance. He reduced the ancient Six Harmonies, Three Luminaires, and Four Wanders instruments to small-scale models by his own design, and all worked correctly.

sentences.zh: 又自制為月道儀，揆日測高諸器，皆自出新意。

translations.literal: He also made on his own a lunar-path instrument and various instruments for gauging the sun and measuring altitude—all novel designs of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised a lunar-path instrument and various sun-gauging and altitude-measuring devices, all original inventions of his own.

sentences.zh: 嘗登觀像台，流覽新制六儀，及元郭守敬簡儀、明初渾球，指數其中利病，皆如素習。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the observatory tower, surveyed the newly made Six Instruments, as well as Guo Shoujing's simplified armillary of the Yuan and the Ming-dynasty early celestial globe, and pointed out their strengths and flaws—all as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the observatory tower he examined the newly made Six Instruments, Guo Shoujing's simplified armillary from the Yuan, and the early Ming celestial globe, and identified their strengths and flaws as if he had long been familiar with them.

sentences.zh: 其書有測器考二卷，又自鳴鐘說一卷，壺漏考一卷，日晷備考一卷，赤道提晷一卷，勿菴揆日器一卷，加時日軌高度表一卷，揆日測說一卷，璇璣尺解一卷，測量定時簡法一卷，勿庵測望儀式一卷，勿庵仰觀儀式一卷，月道儀式一卷。

translations.literal: His books include Examination of Surveying Instruments in two juan; also one juan each on Self-sounding Bells, Examination of Clepsydra Vessels, Complete Study of Sundials, Ecliptic Gnomon, Wuan Sun-gauging Instrument, Table of Altitudes of the Solar Track by Added Hours, Discourse on Sun-gauging Measurement, Explanation of the Armillary Scale, Simple Method of Surveying for Fixing Time, Wuan Surveying Instrument Forms, Wuan Upward-gazing Instrument Forms, and Lunar-path Instrument Forms.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Examination of Surveying Instruments in two juan, along with one juan each on self-sounding bells, clepsydra vessels, sundials, the ecliptic gnomon, the Wuan sun-gauging instrument, a table of solar-track altitudes by added hours, a discourse on sun-gauging measurement, an explanation of the armillary scale, a simple method of survey-based timekeeping, the forms of the Wuan surveying and upward-gazing instruments, and the lunar-path instrument.

sentences.zh: 其說曰：『月道出入於黃道，猶黃道之出入於赤道也。

translations.literal: His explanation states: 'The lunar path enters and exits the ecliptic, just as the ecliptic enters and exits the equator.
translations.idiomatic: He explained: 'The Moon's path crosses in and out of the ecliptic just as the ecliptic crosses in and out of the equator.

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有為之儀器者。

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present no one has made an instrument for it.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity until his day, no instrument had been built for it.

sentences.zh: 今依渾蓋北密南疏之度，以黃極為樞，而月道半在其內，半出其外，則月緯大小之理，及正交、中交、交前、交後之法，可以眾著。

translations.literal: Now, following the dense-north sparse-south graduations of the armillary-sphere cover, taking the ecliptic pole as pivot, with the lunar path half within and half without, then the principle of the Moon's latitude magnitude, and the methods of direct crossing, middle crossing, before crossing, and after crossing, can be made plain to all.
translations.idiomatic: Following the armillary sphere's denser graduations toward the north and sparser toward the south, with the ecliptic pole as pivot and the lunar path half inside and half outside it, the logic of lunar latitude and the methods for direct, middle, pre-nodal, and post-nodal positions could all be made plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 儀以銅為之，略如渾蓋，其上盤為月道，亦如渾蓋天盤之黃道圈；

translations.literal: The instrument is made of bronze, roughly like an armillary-sphere cover; its upper plate is the lunar path, also like the ecliptic circle on the armillary's upper plate;
translations.idiomatic: The instrument was cast in bronze, roughly like an armillary cover; its upper plate represents the lunar path, corresponding to the ecliptic ring on the armillary's upper plate;

sentences.zh: 其下盤黃道經緯，分宮分度，並以黃極為心，而侭邊以黃緯九十五度少半為限。

translations.literal: its lower plate bears ecliptic longitude and latitude, divided by mansions and degrees, all centered on the ecliptic pole, with the rim limited to ecliptic latitude of ninety-five and a half degrees.
translations.idiomatic: the lower plate shows ecliptic longitude and latitude by mansion and degree, all centered on the ecliptic pole, with the rim set at a limit of ninety-five and a half degrees of ecliptic latitude.

sentences.zh: 出黃道南五度少半，月道所到也。』

translations.literal: Five and a half degrees south of the ecliptic is where the lunar path reaches.'
translations.idiomatic: Five and a half degrees south of the ecliptic marks the limit reached by the lunar path.'

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中李煥鬥嘗從文鼎問曆法，作答李祠部問歷一卷。

translations.literal: Li Huandou, Director in the Ministry of Rites, once questioned Wending on calendrical methods; he answered in one juan, Reply to Director Li's Questions on the Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huandou, a director in the Ministry of Rites, once studied calendrics with Wending; Wending answered his questions in one juan titled Reply to Director Li's Questions on the Calendar.

sentences.zh: 滄州老儒劉介錫同客天津，問曆法，作答劉文學問天象一卷。

translations.literal: Liu Jiexi, an old scholar of Cangzhou, while lodging together as guests in Tianjin, asked about calendrical methods; he answered in one juan, Literary Liu's Questions on Celestial Phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiexi, an elder scholar of Cangzhou, while staying with Wending as guests in Tianjin, asked about calendrical methods; Wending answered in one juan titled Literary Liu's Questions on Celestial Phenomena.

sentences.zh: 又言生平於難讀之書，每手疏而攜諸篋，以待明者問之，於歷學尤多，作思問編一卷。

translations.literal: He also said that in his life, for books hard to read, he would write notes by hand and carry them in his case, waiting for the learned to question him; in calendar studies there were especially many such, compiled as one juan, Reflections on Questions.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that throughout his life, whenever he encountered a difficult book he would make handwritten notes and keep them in his satchel against the day a knowledgeable person might ask about them; he had especially many such notes on calendrics, which he compiled as one juan titled Reflections on Questions.

sentences.zh: 緯度以測日高，因知北極為用甚博，古用二至二分，今則逐日可測，承友人之問，作七十二候太陽緯度一卷。

translations.literal: Latitude is known by measuring solar altitude; thus one knows the uses of the north pole are very broad. Formerly only the two solstices and two equinoxes were used; now it can be measured day by day. Responding to a friend's question, he wrote one juan on Solar Latitude for the Seventy-two Pentades.
translations.idiomatic: Latitude is found by measuring the sun's altitude, from which one sees how widely the north celestial pole is applicable. Antiquity used only the two solstices and two equinoxes; now measurement can be taken day by day. At a friend's request he wrote one juan on Solar Latitude for the Seventy-two Pentades.

sentences.zh: 潘天成從文鼎學歷，而苦於布算，作寫歷步曆法一卷授之。

translations.literal: Pan Tiancheng studied calendar science with Wending but found spread calculation burdensome; he wrote one juan on Written Calendar Step Methods and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tiancheng studied calendrics with Wending but struggled with rod calculation; Wending wrote one juan on Written Calendar Step Methods and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 又授時步交食式一卷，文鼎季弟文鼏之稿也。

translations.literal: Also one juan of Shoushi Step Methods for Eclipses—the draft of Wending's youngest brother Wenmi.
translations.idiomatic: There was also one juan of Shoushi Step Methods for Eclipses—a draft by Wending's youngest brother Wenmi.

sentences.zh: 步五星式六卷，文鼎與其仲弟文鼐共成之者也。

translations.literal: Step Methods for the Five Planets in six juan—completed jointly by Wending and his second brother Wenai.
translations.idiomatic: Step Methods for the Five Planets in six juan was completed jointly by Wending and his second brother Wenai.

sentences.zh: 文鼎每得一書，皆為正其訛闕，指其得失，又古歷列星距度考一卷，從殘壞之本，尋其普天星宿，入宿去極度分，中缺二星，又從閩中林侗寫本補完之，而斷以為授時之法。

translations.literal: Whenever Wending obtained a book, he corrected its errors and omissions and pointed out its strengths and weaknesses. He also wrote one juan, Examination of Fixed Star Distances in the Ancient Calendar, from a damaged original seeking the stars spanning the whole sky, their mansion entry and polar distance in degrees and minutes; two stars were missing, and he supplemented them from Lin Tong's copy in Min, adjudicating by the Shoushi method.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wending acquired a book, he corrected its textual errors, identified its gaps, and assessed its merits and flaws. He also wrote one juan titled Examination of Fixed Star Distances in the Ancient Calendar, working from a damaged original to recover the whole-sky star positions, their mansion entries, and polar distances in degrees and minutes. Two stars were missing; he restored them from a copy made by Lin Tong in Fujian and adjudicated the result by Shoushi methods.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中利瑪竇入中國，始倡幾何之學，以點線面體為測量之資，制器作圖，頗為精密。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign Matteo Ricci entered China and first advocated the study of geometry, taking points, lines, surfaces, and solids as the basis of surveying, making instruments and drawing diagrams with considerable precision.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign Matteo Ricci came to China and first promoted the study of geometry, using points, lines, surfaces, and solids as the basis of measurement; the instruments he made and diagrams he drew were notably precise.

sentences.zh: 學者張皇過甚，未暇深考，輒薄古法為不足觀；

translations.literal: Scholars exaggerated overly, without leisure for deep examination, and readily belittled ancient methods as unworthy of regard;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars exaggerated its claims, without taking time for thorough study, and readily dismissed traditional methods as beneath notice;

sentences.zh: 而株守舊法者，又斥西人為異學：兩家之說，遂成隔礙。

translations.literal: while those clinging to old methods in turn denounced Westerners as heterodox learning—so the two schools' doctrines became mutually obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: while those who clung to the old methods denounced Western learning as alien doctrine, so the two schools became walled off from each other.

sentences.zh: 文鼎集其書而為之說，用籌、用尺、用筆，稍稍變從我法。

translations.literal: Wending gathered their books and wrote explanations; using counting rods, rulers, and brush, he gradually adapted them to our methods.
translations.idiomatic: Wending collected their books and wrote commentaries, adapting rod, ruler, and brush calculation gradually to Chinese methods.

sentences.zh: 若三角、比例等，原非中法可賅，特為表出。

translations.literal: Such things as trigonometry and proportion originally could not be subsumed under Chinese methods; he set them forth separately.
translations.idiomatic: Trigonometry, proportion, and the like had no native Chinese equivalent; he set them forth separately.

sentences.zh: 古法方程，亦非西法所有，則專著論，以明古人之精意不可湮沒。

translations.literal: The ancient method of simultaneous equations likewise was not something Western methods possessed; he therefore wrote dedicated treatises to show that the ancients' fine insights must not be buried.
translations.idiomatic: Traditional simultaneous equations, which Western methods lacked, he treated in dedicated essays to show that the ancients' fine insights must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 又為九數存古，以著其概。

translations.literal: He also wrote Preserving the Ancients in the Nine Numbers to set forth the outline.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Preserving the Ancients in the Nine Numbers to set forth the general picture.

sentences.zh: 總為中西算學通例一卷。

translations.literal: In all this amounted to one juan, General Principles of Chinese and Western Mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: These were combined as one juan titled General Principles of Chinese and Western Mathematics.

sentences.zh: 餘分九種：一，勿庵籌算七卷。

translations.literal: The remainder comprises nine works: first, Wuan Counting-rods in seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder comprises nine works: first, Wuan Counting-rods in seven juan.

sentences.zh: 二，筆算五卷。

translations.literal: Second, Brush Calculation in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Second, Brush Calculation in five juan.

sentences.zh: 皆易橫為直，以便中文。

translations.literal: Both change horizontal layout to vertical, for the convenience of Chinese script.
translations.idiomatic: Both convert horizontal notation to vertical, to suit Chinese writing.

sentences.zh: 三，度算一卷，原無算例，其弟文鼏補之，而參以嘉禾陳藎謨尺算用法。

translations.literal: Third, Degree Calculation in one juan—originally without worked examples; his brother Wenmi supplemented them, drawing also on Chen Jingmo of Jiahe's ruler-calculation usage.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Degree Calculation in one juan—originally without worked examples, which his brother Wenmi supplied, incorporating Chen Jingmo of Jiahe's ruler-calculation methods.

sentences.zh: 又有矩算，用一尺一方板，則文鼎所創。

translations.literal: There is also rectangle calculation, using a one-foot square board—Wending's own invention.
translations.idiomatic: There is also rectangle calculation, using a one-foot square board—an invention of Wending's own.

sentences.zh: 四，比例數解四卷。

translations.literal: Fourth, Explanation of Proportional Numbers in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Explanation of Proportional Numbers in four juan.

sentences.zh: 釋穆尼閣所譯之對數。

translations.literal: It explains the logarithms translated by Verbiest.
translations.idiomatic: It explains the logarithms in Verbiest's translation.

sentences.zh: 五，三角法舉要五卷。

translations.literal: Fifth, Essentials of Trigonometry in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Essentials of Trigonometry in five juan.

sentences.zh: 其目有五：曰測量名義，曰算例，曰內容外切，曰或問，曰測量。

translations.literal: Its headings are five: Surveying Terminology, Worked Examples, Inscribed and Circumscribed, Questions, and Surveying.
translations.idiomatic: It has five sections: Surveying Terminology, Worked Examples, Inscribed and Circumscribed Figures, Questions, and Surveying.

sentences.zh: 六，方程論六卷，安溪李鼎徵為刻於泉州。

translations.literal: Sixth, Treatise on Simultaneous Equations in six juan, printed at Quanzhou by Li Dingzheng of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, Treatise on Simultaneous Equations in six juan, printed at Quanzhou by Li Dingzheng of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 七，幾何摘要三卷，就原本刪繁補遺。

translations.literal: Seventh, Summary of Geometry in three juan, pruning the original's redundancies and filling its gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, Summary of Geometry in three juan, trimming the original's excess and repairing its omissions.

sentences.zh: 八，句股測量二卷，就周髀、海島諸術，錄要以存古意。

translations.literal: Eighth, Right-triangle Surveying in two juan, selecting essentials from the methods of the Zhou Bi and Sea Island to preserve ancient intent.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, Right-triangle Surveying in two juan, gathering essentials from the Zhou Bi and Sea Island methods to preserve the spirit of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 九，九九數存古十卷，九數即九章隸首之法，僅存者九章之目耳。

translations.literal: Ninth, Preserving the Ancients in the Nine Numbers in ten juan—the Nine Numbers being the methods of the first chapter of the Nine Chapters; only the chapter headings of the Nine Chapters survive.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, Preserving the Ancients in the Nine Numbers in ten juan—the Nine Numbers being the methods of the first chapter of the Nine Chapters; only the chapter titles of the Nine Chapters now survive.

sentences.zh: 後有作者，莫能出其範圍。

translations.literal: Later authors could not go beyond its scope.
translations.idiomatic: Later writers could not surpass its range.

sentences.zh: 外有書一十七種為續編：一，少廣拾遺一卷。

translations.literal: Outside these are seventeen works forming a sequel: first, Supplementary Recovery of Lesser Breadth in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these are seventeen works forming a sequel: first, Supplementary Recovery of Lesser Breadth in one juan.

sentences.zh: 古有一乘方至九乘方相生之圖，而莫詳所用。

translations.literal: Antiquity had a diagram of mutual generation from one power to nine powers, but no one explained its use.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had a diagram showing mutual generation from the first through the ninth power, but no one explained how it was used.

sentences.zh: 後或增之至十乘，惟四乘方與十乘方不可藉用他法，因為推演至十二乘方，有條不紊。

translations.literal: Later some extended it to the tenth power; only the fourth and tenth powers could not be handled by other methods, so he derived them up to the twelfth power in orderly fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Later writers extended it to the tenth power; only the fourth and tenth powers could not be handled by other methods, so he worked them out systematically up to the twelfth power.

sentences.zh: 二，方田通法一卷，算家有捷田二十三法，廣之為百二十有四。

translations.literal: Second, General Method for Rectangular Fields in one juan—calculators had twenty-three shortcut field methods; he expanded them to one hundred twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Second, General Method for Rectangular Fields in one juan—earlier calculators knew twenty-three shortcut field formulas; he expanded them to one hundred twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 三，幾何補編四卷。

translations.literal: Third, Supplement to Geometry in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Supplement to Geometry in four juan.

sentences.zh: 幾何原本六卷，止於測面，七卷以後，未經譯出，取測量全義量體諸率，實考其作法根源，以補原書之未備。

translations.literal: The first six juan of Euclid's Elements stop at plane measurement; from the seventh juan onward nothing was translated. He took the solid ratios from Complete Meaning of Measurement and verified their construction in practice, to supplement what the original book left incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: The first six books of Euclid's Elements stop at plane measurement; the seventh and following books were never translated. He took the solid ratios from Complete Meaning of Measurement, verified their construction in practice, and used them to fill what the original left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 而原書二十等面體之說，向固疑其有誤者，今乃得其實數。

translations.literal: As for the original book's account of twenty-sided solids, he had long suspected error; now he obtained their true values.
translations.idiomatic: He had long suspected the original's treatment of twenty-sided solids was wrong; now he obtained their true values.

sentences.zh: 又原本理分中末線，但有求作之法，而莫知所用。

translations.literal: Also in the original, the mean and extreme ratio lines had methods of construction but no one knew their use.
translations.idiomatic: The original also gave methods for constructing mean and extreme ratio lines, but no one knew what they were for.

sentences.zh: 今依法求得十二等面及二十等面之體積，因得其各體中棱線及輳心對角諸線之比例。

translations.literal: Now by those methods he found the volumes of twelve- and twenty-sided solids, and thereby the ratios among their edge lines, center-to-vertex lines, and diagonal lines.
translations.idiomatic: Applying those methods, he found the volumes of twelve- and twenty-sided solids and thereby the ratios among their edges, center-to-vertex lines, and diagonals.

sentences.zh: 又兩體互相容及兩體與立方、立員諸體相容各比例，並以理分中末線為法，乃知此線不為徒設。

translations.literal: He also determined the ratios by which two solids inscribe one another, and by which two solids inscribe cubes, cylinders, and other solids; all by the mean and extreme ratio line—thus showing that this line was not set down in vain.
translations.idiomatic: He also worked out the ratios by which two solids inscribe each other, and by which two solids inscribe cubes, cylinders, and other figures—all by the mean and extreme ratio line, showing that it had not been introduced without purpose.

sentences.zh: 四，西鏡錄訂註一卷。

translations.literal: Fourth, Revised Annotation to the Western Mirror in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, Revised Annotation to the Western Mirror in one juan.

sentences.zh: 五，權度通幾一卷。

translations.literal: Fifth, Weights and Measures Applied to Geometry in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, Weights and Measures Applied to Geometry in one juan.

sentences.zh: 重學為西術一種，載於比例規解者多譌誤，今以南勳卿儀象志互相訂補，其數始真。

translations.literal: Statics is one branch of Western mathematics; what appears in Explanation of the Proportional Compass contains many errors. Now, cross-checking against Nan Xunqing's Treatise on Instruments and Images, the figures become correct.
translations.idiomatic: Statics is one branch of Western mathematics; the account in Explanation of the Proportional Compass contains many errors. Cross-checking against Nan Xunqing's Treatise on Instruments and Images, he corrected the figures.

sentences.zh: 六，奇器補註二卷。

translations.literal: Sixth, Supplementary Annotation to Marvelous Devices in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, Supplementary Annotation to Marvelous Devices in two juan.

sentences.zh: 關中王公徵奇器圖說所述引重轉木諸制，並有裨於民生日用，而又本於西人重學，以明其意。

translations.literal: The lifting and turning mechanisms described in Wang Zheng's Diagrams and Explanations of Marvelous Devices from Guanzhong all benefit daily life, and he also drew on Western statics to clarify their principles.
translations.idiomatic: The lifting and turning mechanisms described in Wang Zheng's Diagrams and Explanations of Marvelous Devices from Guanzhong all serve daily life; he also drew on Western statics to explain their principles.

sentences.zh: 嘗以書史所傳，如漢杜詩作水《廠義》以便民，及王氏農書諸水器之類，睹記所及，如劉繼莊詩集載筒車灌田法，稍為輯錄，以補其所遺，而圖與說不相應者正之，以西字為識者易之。

translations.literal: He also gathered from histories and records such traditions as Han Du Shi's water-powered bellows made to benefit the people, and the various water devices in Wang Zhen's Book of Agriculture; from whatever notes he chanced upon, such as the bucket-wheel irrigation method in Liu Jizhuang's collected poems, he compiled a little to fill omissions; where diagrams and text did not match he corrected them, and replaced Western characters with ones easier to recognize.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected from histories and records such examples as Han Du Shi's water-powered bellows built for the people's benefit and the various water devices in Wang Zhen's Book of Agriculture; from notes he happened upon, such as the bucket-wheel irrigation method in Liu Jizhuang's collected poems, he compiled what was missing; where diagrams and text did not agree he corrected them, and replaced Western characters with more familiar ones.

sentences.zh: 七，正弦簡法補一卷。

translations.literal: Seventh, Supplement to the Simplified Sine Method in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, Supplement to the Simplified Sine Method in one juan.

sentences.zh: 大測諸書，言作八線表之法詳矣，薛鳳祚書有用矢線求度法，為之作圖，以明其意。

translations.literal: Books on grand surveying explain in detail how to construct the eight-line table; Xue Fengzuo's book has a method of finding degrees by versed sine lines—for this he made diagrams to clarify the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Books on grand surveying explain in detail how to construct the eight-line table; Xue Fengzuo's book gives a method of finding degrees by versed sine lines—for this Wending made diagrams to clarify the idea.

sentences.zh: 因得兩法，在六宗、三要之外，而為用加捷。

translations.literal: Thus he obtained two methods, outside the Six Divisions and Three Essentials, yet more convenient in use.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he obtained two methods beyond the Six Divisions and Three Essentials, and more convenient to apply.

sentences.zh: 兩法者，一曰正弦方冪倍而退位得倍弧之矢，一曰正矢進位折半得半弧正弦上方冪。

translations.literal: The two methods are: first, double the sine square and shift the decimal place back to obtain the versed sine of double the arc; second, advance the place of the versed sine and halve it to obtain the square above the sine of half the arc.
translations.idiomatic: The two methods are these: one doubles the sine squared and shifts the decimal to obtain the versed sine of a double arc; the other advances the versed sine's place value and halves it to obtain the squared term above the sine of a half arc.

sentences.zh: 八，弧三角舉要五卷。

translations.literal: Eighth, Essentials of Spherical Trigonometry in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, Essentials of Spherical Trigonometry in five juan.

sentences.zh: 曆書皆三角法也，內分二支：一曰平三角，一曰弧三角。

translations.literal: Calendar books all employ trigonometry, divided internally into two branches: plane trigonometry and spherical trigonometry.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar books all use trigonometry, divided into two branches: plane trigonometry and spherical trigonometry.

sentences.zh: 凡曆法所測，皆弧度也，弧線與直線不能為比例，則剖析渾員之體，而各於弧線中得其相當直線。

translations.literal: All that calendrical methods measure are arc degrees; arcs and straight lines cannot form proportions, so one dissects the body of the sphere and from each arc obtains its corresponding straight line.
translations.idiomatic: Everything calendrical methods measure is arc measure; since arcs and straight lines cannot be proportional, one dissects the sphere and from each arc derives its corresponding straight line.

sentences.zh: 即於無句股中尋出句股，此法之最奇而確者。

translations.literal: Thus one finds right triangles where none seem to exist—this method is the most marvelous and precise.
translations.idiomatic: It finds right triangles where none seem to exist—the most marvelous and exact of methods.

sentences.zh: 弧三角之用法雖多，而其最著明者，為黃赤交變一圖。

translations.literal: Although spherical trigonometry has many applications, the clearest is the single diagram of ecliptic-equator variation.
translations.idiomatic: Spherical trigonometry has many uses, but the clearest is the diagram of variation between the ecliptic and the equator.

sentences.zh: 反覆推論，瞭如列眉，熟此一端，則其餘不難推及矣。

translations.literal: Through repeated reasoning it becomes as clear as brows on a face; master this one point and the rest is not hard to extend.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated reasoning makes it as plain as the brows on one's face; master this one point and the rest follows easily.

sentences.zh: 測量全義第七、第八、第九卷專明此理，而舉例不全，且多錯謬。

translations.literal: Volumes seven, eight, and nine of Complete Meaning of Measurement explain this principle exclusively, but their examples are incomplete and contain many errors.
translations.idiomatic: Volumes seven through nine of Complete Meaning of Measurement treat this principle, but their examples are incomplete and riddled with errors.

sentences.zh: 其散見諸歷指者，僅存用數，無從得其端倪。

translations.literal: What appears scattered in various Calendar Guides preserves only the working numbers, with no way to grasp the underlying principle.
translations.idiomatic: What appears scattered in various calendar guides gives only the working numbers, offering no clue to the underlying principle.

sentences.zh: 天學會通圈線三角法，作圖草率，往往不與法相應。

translations.literal: The circular-line trigonometry in Compendium of Astronomical Learning draws diagrams carelessly, often failing to match the methods.
translations.idiomatic: The circular-line trigonometry in Compendium of Astronomical Learning is diagrammed carelessly, often failing to match the methods.

sentences.zh: 一以正弧三角為綱，仍用渾儀解之。

translations.literal: He takes right spherical triangles as the framework and still explains them with the armillary sphere.
translations.idiomatic: He takes right spherical triangles as the framework and still explains them with the armillary sphere.

sentences.zh: 正弧三角之理，盡歸句股。

translations.literal: The principles of right spherical triangles all reduce to right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: The principles of right spherical triangles all reduce to right triangles.

sentences.zh: 參伍其變，斜弧三角之理，亦歸句股矣。

translations.literal: By combining and varying them, the principles of oblique spherical triangles also reduce to right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: By combining and varying them, the principles of oblique spherical triangles also reduce to right triangles.

sentences.zh: 其目：曰弧三角體式，曰正弧句股，曰求餘角法，曰弧角比例，曰垂線，曰次形，曰垂弧捷法，曰八線相當。

translations.literal: Its sections are: Forms of Spherical Triangles, Right Spherical Triangles, Methods of Finding Remaining Angles, Ratios of Arcs and Angles, Perpendicular Lines, Secondary Figures, Shortcut Methods for Perpendicular Arcs, and Equivalence of the Eight Lines.
translations.idiomatic: Its sections are: Forms of Spherical Triangles, Right Spherical Triangles, Methods of Finding Remaining Angles, Ratios of Arcs and Angles, Perpendicular Lines, Secondary Figures, Shortcut Methods for Perpendicular Arcs, and Equivalence of the Eight Lines.

sentences.zh: 九，環中黍尺五卷。

translations.literal: Ninth, Millet Measures Within the Sphere in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, Millet Measures Within the Sphere in five juan.

sentences.zh: 舉要中弧度之法已詳，然更有簡妙之用宜知。

translations.literal: Essentials already explains arc methods in detail, yet there are still simpler and more elegant applications worth knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Essentials already explains arc methods in detail, yet simpler and more elegant applications remain worth knowing.

sentences.zh: 測量全義原有斜弧兩矢較之例，所立圖姑為斜望之形，而無實度可言。

translations.literal: Complete Meaning of Measurement originally had an example comparing two versed sines of oblique arcs, but its diagram was merely an oblique view with no actual measurable values.
