translations.idiomatic: Complete Meaning of Measurement originally included an example comparing two versed sines of oblique arcs, but its diagram was only an oblique view with no real measurable values.

sentences.zh: 今一以平儀正形為主，凡可以算得者，即可以器量。

translations.literal: Now he takes the true form on the plane instrument as primary: whatever can be calculated can also be measured with instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Now he takes the true form on the plane instrument as primary: whatever can be calculated can also be measured with instruments.

sentences.zh: 渾儀真像，呈諸片楮，而經緯歷然，無絲毫隱伏假借。

translations.literal: The true image of the armillary sphere is presented on a sheet of paper, with celestial coordinates clearly marked, without the slightest concealment or artifice.
translations.idiomatic: The true image of the armillary sphere is laid out on paper, with celestial coordinates clearly marked and without the slightest concealment or artifice.

sentences.zh: 至於加減代乘除之用，曆書舉其名不詳其說，疑之數十年，而後得其條貫，即初數次數甲數乙數諸法。

translations.literal: As for the use of addition and subtraction in place of multiplication and division, calendar books give the names but not the explanations; he puzzled over them for decades before grasping their logic—the methods of initial numbers, secondary numbers, A-numbers, and B-numbers.
translations.idiomatic: As for using addition and subtraction in place of multiplication and division, calendar books name the methods but do not explain them; he puzzled over them for decades before grasping their logic—the methods of initial numbers, secondary numbers, A-numbers, and B-numbers.

sentences.zh: 其目：曰總論，曰先數後數，曰平儀論，曰三極通幾，曰初數次數，曰加減法，曰甲數乙數，曰加減捷法，曰加減又法，曰加減通法。

translations.literal: Its sections are: General Discussion, First Numbers and Later Numbers, Discussion of the Plane Instrument, Geometry of the Three Poles, Initial and Secondary Numbers, Addition-Subtraction Methods, A-Numbers and B-Numbers, Shortcut Addition-Subtraction Methods, Alternative Addition-Subtraction Methods, and General Addition-Subtraction Methods.
translations.idiomatic: Its sections are: General Discussion, First Numbers and Later Numbers, Discussion of the Plane Instrument, Geometry of the Three Poles, Initial and Secondary Numbers, Addition-Subtraction Methods, A-Numbers and B-Numbers, Shortcut Addition-Subtraction Methods, Alternative Addition-Subtraction Methods, and General Addition-Subtraction Methods.

sentences.zh: 十，巉堵測量二卷。

translations.literal: Tenth, Chan-du Measurement in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, Chan-du Measurement in two juan.

sentences.zh: 古法斜剖立方，成兩巉堵形，巉堵又剖為二，成立三角，立三角為量體所必需，然此義皆未發。

translations.literal: The ancient method of obliquely sectioning a cube yields two chan-du forms; each chan-du is halved to form triangular prisms; triangular prisms are essential for measuring solids—yet none of this had been explained.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient method of obliquely sectioning a cube yields two chan-du forms; each chan-du is halved to form triangular prisms, which are essential for measuring solids—yet none of this had been explained.

sentences.zh: 今以渾儀黃赤道之割切二線成立三角形，立三角本實形，今諸線相遇成虛形，與實形等，而四面皆句股，西法通於古法矣。

translations.literal: Now, using the secant and tangent lines of the ecliptic and equator on the armillary sphere to form a triangular prism—the prism is fundamentally a solid figure, but here the intersecting lines form a virtual figure equal to the solid, with all four faces right triangles—linking Western methods to ancient ones.
translations.idiomatic: Now, using the secant and tangent lines of the ecliptic and equator on the armillary sphere to form a triangular prism—a solid in principle, but here the intersecting lines form a virtual figure equal to the solid, with all four faces right triangles—thus linking Western methods to ancient ones.

sentences.zh: 又於餘弧取赤道及大距弧之割切線，成句股方錐形，亦四面皆句股，即弧度可相求，亦不言角，古法通於西法矣。

translations.literal: Further, from the remaining arc he takes the secant and tangent lines of the equator and great-distance arc to form a right-triangular square pyramid, also with four right-triangle faces, so arc degrees can be found mutually without speaking of angles—linking ancient methods to Western ones.
translations.idiomatic: Further, from the remaining arc he takes the secant and tangent lines of the equator and great-distance arc to form a right-triangular square pyramid, also with four right-triangle faces, so arc degrees can be found mutually without speaking of angles—thus linking ancient methods to Western ones.

sentences.zh: 二者並可以堅楮為儀象之，則八線相為比例之理，瞭如掌紋。

translations.literal: Both can be modeled in stiff paper as instrument figures, making the proportional relations among the eight lines as clear as the lines on one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: Both can be modeled in stiff paper as instrument figures, making the proportional relations among the eight lines as clear as the lines on one's palm.

sentences.zh: 而郭守敬員容方直矢接句股之法，不煩言說而解。

translations.literal: And Guo Shoujing's methods of circular containment, square containment, straight lines, versed sines, and joined right triangles become clear without need of much explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shoujing's methods of circular containment, square containment, straight lines, versed sines, and joined right triangles become clear without much explanation.

sentences.zh: 其目：曰總論，曰立三角摘要，曰渾員內容立三角，曰句股錐，曰句股方錐，曰方巉堵容員巉堵，曰員容方直儀簡法，曰郭太史本法，曰角即弧解。

translations.literal: Its sections are: General Discussion, Summary of Triangular Prisms, Triangular Prisms Within the Sphere, Right-Triangle Pyramids, Right-Triangle Square Pyramids, Square Chan-du Containing Circular Chan-du, Simplified Methods for Circular and Square Containment Instruments, Grand Astrologer Guo's Original Methods, and Explanation That Angles Are Arcs.
translations.idiomatic: Its sections are: General Discussion, Summary of Triangular Prisms, Triangular Prisms Within the Sphere, Right-Triangle Pyramids, Right-Triangle Square Pyramids, Square Chan-du Containing Circular Chan-du, Simplified Methods for Circular and Square Containment Instruments, Grand Astrologer Guo's Original Methods, and Explanation That Angles Are Arcs.

sentences.zh: 十一，用句股解幾何原本之根一卷。

translations.literal: Eleventh, Using Right Triangles to Explain the Foundations of Euclid's Elements in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, Using Right Triangles to Explain the Foundations of Euclid's Elements in one juan.

sentences.zh: 幾何不言句股，而其理莫能外。

translations.literal: Geometry does not speak of right triangles, yet its principles cannot go beyond them.
translations.idiomatic: Geometry does not speak of right triangles, yet its principles cannot go beyond them.

sentences.zh: 故其最難通者，以句股釋之則明。

translations.literal: Therefore what is hardest to grasp becomes clear when explained through right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: What is hardest to grasp becomes clear when explained through right triangles.

sentences.zh: 惟理分中末線似與句股異源，今為遊心於立法之初，仍不外乎句股，益信古句股義包舉無遺。

translations.literal: Only the mean and extreme ratio line seems to have a different origin from right triangles, yet reflecting on the founding of the methods, it still does not go beyond right triangles, confirming that the ancient meaning of right triangles embraces all without omission.
translations.idiomatic: Only the mean and extreme ratio line seems to spring from a different source, yet when one reflects on how the methods were first established, they still do not go beyond right triangles—confirming that the ancient doctrine of right triangles embraces everything.

sentences.zh: 徐光啟譯大測表，名之曰割圜句股八線表，其知之矣。

translations.literal: When Xu Guangqi translated the grand surveying table, he named it the Table of Eight Lines for Circle-Division Right Triangles—he understood this well.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Guangqi translated the grand surveying table, he named it the Table of Eight Lines for Circle-Division Right Triangles—he understood this.

sentences.zh: 十二，幾何增解數則。

translations.literal: Twelfth, Additional Geometric Solutions and Rules.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, Additional Geometric Solutions and Rules.

sentences.zh: 其目有四：曰以方斜較求斜方，曰切線角與員內角交互相應，曰量無法四邊形捷法，曰取平行線簡法。

translations.literal: It has four sections: Finding the Slant and Square by Comparing Square and Slant, Correspondence Between Tangent-Line Angles and Inscribed Circular Angles, Shortcut Method for Measuring Irregular Quadrilaterals, and Simplified Method for Taking Parallel Lines.
translations.idiomatic: It has four sections: Finding the Slant and Square by Comparing Square and Slant, Correspondence Between Tangent-Line Angles and Inscribed Circular Angles, Shortcut Method for Measuring Irregular Quadrilaterals, and Simplified Method for Taking Parallel Lines.

sentences.zh: 並就幾何各題而增，不入補編，附前條共卷。

translations.literal: All are additions to various geometric problems, not entered in the supplement, appended to the preceding entry in the same juan.
translations.idiomatic: All are additions to various geometric problems, not entered in the supplement, appended to the preceding entry in the same juan.

sentences.zh: 十三，仰觀覆矩二卷。

translations.literal: Thirteenth, Gazing Upward and the Inverted Gnomon in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, Gazing Upward and the Inverted Gnomon in two juan.

sentences.zh: 一查地平經度為日出入方位，一查赤道經度為日出入時刻，並依裡差，用弧三角立算，與曆書法微別。

translations.literal: One investigates horizon longitude for the sun's rising and setting direction, one investigates equatorial longitude for the sun's rising and setting times, both according to local difference, calculated by spherical trigonometry, slightly differing from calendar-book methods.
translations.idiomatic: One investigates horizon longitude for the direction of sunrise and sunset, and equatorial longitude for the times of sunrise and sunset; both follow local correction and are calculated by spherical trigonometry, differing slightly from calendar-book methods.

sentences.zh: 十四，方員冪積二卷。

translations.literal: Fourteenth, Square and Circle Powers and Volumes in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth, Square and Circle Powers and Volumes in two juan.

sentences.zh: 曆書周徑率至二十位，然其入算，仍用古率十一與十四之比例，豈非以乘除之際難用多位歟？

translations.literal: Calendar books give the ratio of circumference to diameter to twenty places, yet in calculation they still use the ancient ratio of eleven to fourteen—is this not because it is difficult to use many places in multiplication and division?
translations.idiomatic: Calendar books give the ratio of circumference to diameter to twenty places, yet in calculation they still use the ancient ratio of eleven to fourteen—is this not because many places are awkward in multiplication and division?

sentences.zh: 今以表列之，取數殊易，乃為之約法，則徑與週之比例即方、員二冪之比例，亦即為立方、立員之比例，殊為簡易直捷。

translations.literal: Now tabulating it makes taking values very easy; he devised a simplified method whereby the ratio of diameter to circumference is also the ratio of square and circular areas, and likewise the ratio of cubes and cylinders—a most simple and direct approach.
translations.idiomatic: Tabulating the values makes them easy to use; he devised a simplified method whereby the ratio of diameter to circumference is also the ratio of square and circular areas, and likewise of cubes and cylinders—a simple and direct approach.

sentences.zh: 十五，麗澤珠璣一卷。

translations.literal: Fifteenth, Pearls from the Beautiful Marsh in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth, Pearls from the Beautiful Marsh in one juan.

sentences.zh: 友朋之益，取其有關算學者。

translations.literal: The benefits from friends, selecting what bears on mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: It collects the benefits of friendship, selecting what bears on mathematics.

sentences.zh: 十六，算器考一卷。

translations.literal: Sixteenth, Examination of Calculating Instruments in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth, Examination of Calculating Instruments in one juan.

sentences.zh: 十七，數學星槎一卷。

translations.literal: Seventeenth, Mathematical Star Raft in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth, Mathematical Star Raft in one juan.

sentences.zh: 文鼎歷學疑問，曾呈御覽，後又引申其說，作歷學疑問補二卷，皆平正通達，可為步算家準則。

translations.literal: Wending's Questions on Calendrical Learning was once presented for imperial review; later he extended his views and wrote a two-juan Supplement to Questions on Calendrical Learning—all even-handed and penetrating, serving as standards for computational mathematicians.
translations.idiomatic: Wending's Questions on Calendrical Learning was once presented for imperial review; later he extended his views in a two-juan Supplement to Questions on Calendrical Learning—all even-handed and penetrating, and fit to serve as standards for computational mathematicians.

sentences.zh: 文鼎為學甚勤，劉輝祖同舍館，告桐城方苞曰：『吾每寐覺，漏鼓四五下，梅君猶構燈夜誦，乃今知吾之玩日而愒時也。』

translations.literal: Wending studied with great diligence. Liu Huizu, who shared his lodgings, told Fang Bao of Tongcheng: "Whenever I wake at the fourth or fifth watch, Master Mei is still reading by lamplight; only now do I realize how I have squandered days and wasted time."
translations.idiomatic: Wending studied with great diligence. Liu Huizu, who shared his lodgings, told Fang Bao of Tongcheng: "Whenever I wake at the fourth or fifth watch, Master Mei is still reading by lamplight—and only now do I see how I have squandered my days and wasted my time."

sentences.zh: 居京師時，裕親王以禮延致朱邸，稱梅先生而不名。

translations.literal: When residing in the capital, Prince Yu courteously invited him to his vermilion residence and addressed him as Master Mei without using his given name.
translations.idiomatic: While in the capital, Prince Yu courteously invited him to his vermilion residence and addressed him as Master Mei without using his given name.

sentences.zh: 李文貞公命子鍾倫從學，介弟鼎徵及群從皆執弟子之禮。

translations.literal: Li Wenzhong ordered his son Zhonglun to study under him; his younger brother Dingzheng and all their cousins observed the rites of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong ordered his son Zhonglun to study under him; his younger brother Dingzheng and all their cousins observed the rites of disciples.

sentences.zh: 宿遷徐用錫，晉江陳萬策，景州魏廷珍，河間王之銳，交河王蘭生，皆以得與參校為榮。

translations.literal: Xu Yongxi of Suqian, Chen Wance of Jinjiang, Wei Tingzhen of Jingzhou, Wang Zhirui of Hejian, and Wang Lansheng of Jiaohe all took it as an honor to join in collating.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yongxi of Suqian, Chen Wance of Jinjiang, Wei Tingzhen of Jingzhou, Wang Zhirui of Hejian, and Wang Lansheng of Jiaohe all counted it an honor to join in collating.

sentences.zh: 家多藏書，頻年遊歷，手抄雜帙不下數万卷。

translations.literal: His family had many books; through years of travel he hand-copied miscellaneous works numbering no less than tens of thousands of juan.
translations.idiomatic: His family owned many books, and through years of travel he hand-copied miscellaneous works numbering no less than tens of thousands of juan.

sentences.zh: 歲在辛丑，卒，年八十有九。

translations.literal: In the year xinchou he died, aged eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year he died, aged eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上聞，特命有地治者經紀其喪，士論榮之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he specially ordered the local magistrate to manage the funeral; scholars regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard, he specially ordered the local magistrate to manage the funeral; scholars regarded this as an honor.

sentences.zh: 子以燕，字正謀。

translations.literal: His son was Yiyan, courtesy name Zhengmou.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yiyan, courtesy name Zhengmou.

sentences.zh: 康熙癸酉舉人。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the guiyou year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of the guiyou year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 於算學頗有悟入，有法與加減同理，而取徑特殊，能於恆星曆指中摘出致問，文鼎所謂『能助餘之思』也。

translations.literal: He had considerable insight in mathematics; he had a method analogous to addition-subtraction but taking a special approach, able to extract questions from the Fixed Star Calendar Guide—what Wending called "able to assist my thinking."
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable insight in mathematics; he devised a method analogous to addition-subtraction but taking a special approach, and could extract questions from the Fixed Star Calendar Guide—what Wending called "able to assist my thinking."

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 瑴成，字玉汝，以燕子。

translations.literal: Juecheng, courtesy name Yuru, was Yiyan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Juecheng, courtesy name Yuru, was Yiyan's son.

sentences.zh: 文鼎疑日差既有二根，即宜列二表，瑴成以為：『定朔時既有高卑盈縮之加減矣，復用於此，豈非複乎？』

translations.literal: Wending doubted that since the solar equation has two roots, two tables should be listed. Juecheng argued: "When fixing the new moon, elevation and contraction have already been added and subtracted—using them again here, would that not be redundant?"
translations.idiomatic: Wending doubted that since the solar equation has two roots, two tables should be listed. Juecheng argued: "When fixing the new moon, elevation and contraction have already been added and subtracted—using them again here, would that not be redundant?"

sentences.zh: 文鼎因其說，然後悟交食之非缺，比之童烏九歲能與太玄。

translations.literal: Through his argument Wending came to understand that eclipses were not incomplete—a comparison to Tong Xuan, who at nine could engage with the Supreme Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Through his son's argument Wending came to see that eclipses were not incomplete—comparable to Tong Xuan, who at nine could discuss the Supreme Mystery.

sentences.zh: 康熙乙未進士，改編修，與修國史。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the yiwu year of Kangxi, appointed Hanlin compiler, and participated in compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: A metropolitan graduate of the yiwu year of the Kangxi reign, he was appointed Hanlin compiler and helped compile the National History.

sentences.zh: 瑴成肄業蒙養齋，以故數學日進。

translations.literal: Juecheng studied at the Mengyang Studio, and for this reason his mathematics improved daily.
translations.idiomatic: Juecheng studied at the Mengyang Studio, and for this reason his mathematics improved daily.

sentences.zh: 御製數理精蘊、歷象考成諸書，皆與分纂。

translations.literal: He shared in compiling such works as the Imperially Produced Essentials of Mathematical Principles and Examination of Calendars and Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in compiling such works as the Imperially Produced Essentials of Mathematical Principles and Examination of Calendars and Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 所著增刪算法統宗十一卷，赤水遺珍一卷，操縵卮言一卷。

translations.literal: His works include Revised and Expanded Comprehensive Collection of Computational Methods in eleven juan, Treasures Left at Red Water in one juan, and Random Words at the Loom in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Revised and Expanded Comprehensive Collection of Computational Methods in eleven juan, Treasures Left at Red Water in one juan, and Random Words at the Loom in one juan.

sentences.zh: 明代算家，不解立天元術，瑴成謂立天元一即西法之借根方，其說曰；

translations.literal: Ming mathematicians did not understand the Celestial Element method; Juecheng held that setting Celestial Element Unity is the Western borrowed-root method. His explanation says:
translations.idiomatic: Ming mathematicians did not understand the Celestial Element method; Juecheng held that setting Celestial Element Unity is the Western borrowed-root method. His explanation says:

sentences.zh: 『嘗讀授時曆草求弦矢之法，先立天元一為矢，而元學士李冶所著測圜海鏡，亦用天元一立算。

translations.literal: "I once read in the Draft of the Shoushi Calendar the method of finding chord and versed sine, first setting Celestial Element Unity as the versed sine; and Yuan scholar Li Ye's Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement also uses Celestial Element Unity to set up calculations.
translations.idiomatic: "I once read in the Draft of the Shoushi Calendar the method of finding chord and versed sine, first setting Celestial Element Unity as the versed sine; and Yuan scholar Li Ye's Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement also uses Celestial Element Unity to set up calculations.

sentences.zh: 傳寫魯魚，算式訛舛，殊不易讀。

translations.literal: Copyists introduced errors like fish and deer, and the calculation formats are corrupt—very hard to read.
translations.idiomatic: Copyists introduced fish-and-deer errors, and the calculation formats are corrupt—very hard to read.

sentences.zh: 明唐荊川、顧箬溪兩公互相推重，自謂得此中三昧。

translations.literal: The Ming scholars Tang Jingchuan and Gu Ruxi held each other in esteem and claimed to have mastered the essence of this art.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming scholars Tang Jingchuan and Gu Ruxi held each other in esteem and claimed to have mastered the essence of this art.

sentences.zh: 荊川之說曰：「藝士著書，往往以秘其機為奇，所謂天元一云爾，如積求之云爾，漫不省其為何語。」

translations.literal: Jingchuan said: "Craftsmen who write books often treat concealing their method as a marvel—what they call 'Celestial Element Unity' and such, or 'product accumulation' and such—people casually fail to understand what these terms mean."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchuan said: "Craftsmen who write books often treat concealing their method as a marvel—what they call 'Celestial Element Unity' and such, or 'product accumulation' and such—people casually fail to understand what these terms mean."

sentences.zh: 而箬溪則言：「細考測圜海鏡，如求城徑，即以二百四十為天元，半徑即以一百二十為天元，即知其數，何用算為？

translations.literal: Ruxi said: "Examining Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement closely—as when finding a city wall's diameter, one sets two hundred forty as the Celestial Element, or for the radius sets one hundred twenty as the Celestial Element; once you know the number, what need for calculation?
translations.idiomatic: Ruxi said: "Examining Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement closely—as when finding a city wall's diameter, one sets two hundred forty as the Celestial Element, or for the radius sets one hundred twenty as the Celestial Element; once you know the number, what need for calculation?

sentences.zh: 似不必立可也。」

translations.literal: It seems setting it up may be unnecessary."
translations.idiomatic: It seems setting it up may be unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 二公之言如此，餘於顧說頗不謂然，而無以解也。

translations.literal: Such were the two men's words. I tended to disagree with Gu's view but had no way to explain why.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the two men's words. I tended to disagree with Gu's view but had no way to explain why.

sentences.zh: 後供奉內廷，蒙聖祖仁皇帝授以藉根之法，且諭曰：「西人名此書為阿爾熱八達，譯言東來法也。」

translations.literal: Later, serving in the inner court, I received from the benevolent Emperor Shengzu the borrowed-root method, and was instructed: "Westerners name this book Algebra, translated as the Method from the East."
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving in the inner court, I received from the benevolent Emperor Shengzu the borrowed-root method, and was instructed: "Westerners name this book Algebra, translated as the Method from the East."

sentences.zh: 敬受而讀之，其法神妙，誠算法之指南，而竊疑天元一之術頗與相似。

translations.literal: I respectfully received and read it; the method is marvelous, truly a guide to calculation—and I privately suspected the Celestial Element Unity technique was quite similar.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully received and read it; the method is marvelous, truly a guide to calculation—and I privately suspected the Celestial Element Unity technique was quite similar.

sentences.zh: 復取授時曆草觀之，乃煥然冰釋，殆名異而實同，非徒似之而已。

translations.literal: Taking up the Draft of the Shoushi Calendar again, I saw it clearly—as though ice melted; the names differ but the substance is the same, not merely similar.
translations.idiomatic: Taking up the Draft of the Shoushi Calendar again, I saw it clearly—as though ice had melted; the names differ but the substance is the same, not merely similar.

sentences.zh: 夫元時學士著書，台官治歷，莫非此物。

translations.literal: Yuan scholars who wrote books, calendar officials who regulated the calendar—all used this method.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan scholars who wrote books, calendar officials who regulated the calendar—all used this method.

sentences.zh: 乃歷久失傳，猶幸遠人慕化，復得故物。

translations.literal: Yet after long loss of transmission, fortunately distant peoples admiring our civilization restored the old method.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after long loss of transmission, fortunately distant peoples admiring our civilization restored the old method.

sentences.zh: 東來之名，彼尚不忘所自，而明人視若贅疣而欲棄之。

translations.literal: Its name 'from the East'—they still remembered its origin—yet Ming scholars treated it as a useless growth and wished to discard it.
translations.idiomatic: Its name 'from the East'—they still remembered its origin—yet Ming scholars treated it as a useless growth and wished to discard it.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 好學深思如唐、顧二公，尚不能知其意，而淺見寡聞者，又何足道哉？』

translations.literal: Even diligent and deep thinkers like Tang and Gu could not grasp its meaning—what then of shallow and narrow minds?"
translations.idiomatic: Even diligent and deep thinkers like Tang and Gu could not grasp its meaning—what then of shallow and narrow minds?"

sentences.zh: 明史館開，瑴成與修天文、曆志，呈總裁書曰：『一曆志半系先祖之藁，但屢經改竄，非復原本，其中訛舛甚多。

translations.literal: When the Ming History office opened, Juecheng participated in compiling the astronomical and calendar treatises and submitted a letter to the chief compiler: "First, the Calendar Treatise is half based on our ancestor's draft, but it was repeatedly altered and is no longer the original; there are many errors within.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming History office opened, Juecheng participated in compiling the astronomical and calendar treatises and submitted a letter to the chief compiler: "First, the Calendar Treatise is half based on our ancestor's draft, but it was repeatedly altered and is no longer the original; there are many errors within.

sentences.zh: 凡有增刪改正之處，皆逐條簽出。

translations.literal: Wherever there are additions, deletions, or corrections, each has been flagged item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever there are additions, deletions, or corrections, each has been flagged item by item.

sentences.zh: 一，天文志不宜入曆志，擬仍另編。

translations.literal: First, the Astronomical Treatise should not be placed in the Calendar Treatise; it is proposed to compile it separately.
translations.idiomatic: First, the Astronomical Treatise should not be placed in the Calendar Treatise; it is proposed to compile it separately.

sentences.zh: 蓋歷以欽若授時，置閏成歲，其術委曲繁重，其理精微，為說深長。

translations.literal: For the calendar sets seasons according to time, intercalates months to complete the year—its methods are intricate and weighty, its principles subtle, its explanations deep and long.
translations.idiomatic: For the calendar sets seasons according to time, intercalates months to complete the year—its methods are intricate and weighty, its principles subtle, its explanations deep and long.

sentences.zh: 且有明二百七十餘年沿革非一事，造歷者非一家，皆須入志。

translations.literal: Moreover, over the Ming's more than two hundred seventy years the changes were not of one kind, and calendar-makers were not of one school—all must enter the treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, over the Ming's more than two hundred seventy years the changes were not of one kind, and calendar-makers were not of one school—all must enter the treatise.

sentences.zh: 雖盡力刪削，卷帙猶繁。

translations.literal: Even with every effort at reduction, the volume remains large.
translations.idiomatic: Even with every effort at reduction, the volume remains large.

sentences.zh: 若加入天文誌之說，則恐冗雜不合史法。

translations.literal: If astronomical treatise material were added, it would likely be redundant and violate historiographical form.
translations.idiomatic: If astronomical treatise material were added, it would likely be redundant and violate historiographical form.

sentences.zh: 自司馬氏分歷與天官為二書，歷代因之，似不可易。

translations.literal: Since Sima Qian separated calendar and celestial offices into two books, later dynasties followed this—it seems unchangeable.
translations.idiomatic: Since Sima Qian separated calendar and celestial offices into two books, later dynasties followed this—it seems unchangeable.

sentences.zh: 一，天文志例載天體、星座、次舍、儀器、分野等事，遼史謂天象千古不變，歷代之志天文者近於衍，其說似是而非。

translations.literal: Second, the Astronomical Treatise customarily records celestial bodies, constellations, lodges, instruments, field-allotments, and such; the Liao History says celestial phenomena are unchanged through the ages and that dynastic astronomical treatises verge on redundancy—this view seems plausible but is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the Astronomical Treatise customarily records celestial bodies, constellations, lodges, instruments, field-allotments, and such; the Liao History says celestial phenomena are unchanged through the ages and that dynastic astronomical treatises verge on redundancy—this view seems plausible but is wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋天象雖無古今之異，而古今之言天者，則有疏密之殊。

translations.literal: Though celestial phenomena differ not between ancient and modern times, those who speak of heaven in ancient and modern times differ in precision and detail.
translations.idiomatic: Though celestial phenomena differ not between ancient and modern times, those who speak of heaven in ancient and modern times differ in precision and detail.

sentences.zh: 況恆星去極，交宮中星，晨昏隱現，歲歲有差，安得謂千古不易？

translations.literal: Moreover, fixed stars' polar distance, the stars crossing palace and center, their morning and evening visibility—all vary year by year; how can one say they are unchanged through the ages?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, fixed stars' polar distance, the stars crossing palace and center, their morning and evening visibility—all vary year by year; how can one say they are unchanged through the ages?

sentences.zh: 今擬取天文家精妙之說著於篇；

translations.literal: It is proposed to set down in the text the refined theories of astronomers;
translations.idiomatic: It is proposed to set down in the text the refined theories of astronomers;

sentences.zh: 其不足信者，擬削之。』

translations.literal: and to cut what is not trustworthy."
translations.idiomatic: and to cut what is not trustworthy."

sentences.zh: 又時憲志用圖論曰：『客問於梅子曰：『史以紀事，因而不創。

translations.literal: Also, On Using Diagrams in the Shixian Treatise says: "A guest asked Master Mei: 'History records events and follows precedent without innovation.
translations.idiomatic: Also, On Using Diagrams in the Shixian Treatise says: "A guest asked Master Mei: 'History records events and follows precedent without innovation.

sentences.zh: 聞子之志時憲也用圖，此固廿一史所無，而子創為之，宜執事以為非體而欲去之也。

translations.literal: I hear that in your Shixian Treatise you use diagrams—this is indeed absent from all twenty-one standard histories, yet you have innovated; the chief compiler should consider this improper and wish to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that in your Shixian Treatise you use diagrams—this is indeed absent from all twenty-one standard histories, yet you have innovated; the chief compiler should consider this improper and wish to remove it.

sentences.zh: 而子固執己見，复呶呶上言，獨不記昌黎之自訟乎？

translations.literal: Yet you stubbornly hold your view and repeatedly petition above—do you not recall Han Yu's self-reproach?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you stubbornly hold your view and repeatedly petition above—do you not recall Han Yu's self-reproach?

sentences.zh: 吾竊為子危之！』

translations.literal: I privately worry for you!'
translations.idiomatic: I privately worry for you!'

sentences.zh: 梅子曰：『吾聞史之道貴信而直，餘本不原為史官，總裁謂時憲、天文兩志非專家不能辦，不以為固陋而委任之。

translations.literal: Master Mei replied: "I have heard that the way of history values trustworthiness and directness. I originally did not wish to be a historiographer; the chief compiler said the Shixian and Astronomical treatises required specialists and entrusted them to me without deeming me stubborn and narrow."
translations.idiomatic: Master Mei replied: "I have heard that the way of history values trustworthiness and directness. I originally did not wish to be a historiographer; the chief compiler said the Shixian and Astronomical treatises required specialists and entrusted them to me without deeming me stubborn and narrow."

sentences.zh: 余既不獲辭，不得不盡其職。

translations.literal: Since I could not decline, I cannot but fully perform my duty.
translations.idiomatic: Having been unable to refuse, I have no choice but to fulfill my office to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 今客謂舊史無圖而疑餘之創，竊謂史之記事，亦視其信否耳，因、創非所計也。

translations.literal: Now the guest says the old histories had no diagrams and suspects my innovation; I privately hold that in a history's recording of affairs, one looks only at whether it is trustworthy—whether it follows precedent or is an innovation is not what matters.
translations.idiomatic: You say the earlier histories contained no diagrams and suspect I have invented something new. I would reply that when a history records events, what matters is whether the account is credible—not whether it follows precedent or breaks new ground.

sentences.zh: 夫後史之增於前者多矣，漢書十志，已不侔於八書，而後漢皇后本紀，與魏書之志釋老，唐書之傳公主，宋史之傳道學，皆前史所無，又何疑於國史用圖之為創哉？

translations.literal: Later histories have added much beyond earlier ones—the Ten Treatises of the Book of Han already do not match the Eight Treatises; yet the Basic Annals of Empresses in the Book of Later Han, the Treatise on Buddhism and Daoism in the Book of Wei, the Biographies of Princesses in the Book of Tang, and the Biographies of the Learning of the Way in the History of Song—all were absent from earlier histories. Why then doubt that using diagrams in the national history is an innovation?
translations.idiomatic: Later dynastic histories expanded upon their predecessors in countless ways—the Book of Han's ten treatises already exceed the Former Han's eight; yet the Later Han's annals of empresses, the Wei History's treatise on Buddhism and Daoism, the Tang History's biographies of princesses, and the Song History's biographies of Neo-Confucian scholars—all absent from earlier histories—were accepted without question. Why should using diagrams in our national history be singled out as an unwarranted innovation?

sentences.zh: 且客未讀明史耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, has the guest not read the History of Ming?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not read the History of Ming?

sentences.zh: 明史於割員弧矢、月道距差諸圖，備載曆志，何明史不疑為創，而顧疑餘乎？』

translations.literal: The History of Ming fully includes in its Treatise on the Calendar diagrams for arc-segments, chords and arcs, and lunar path departures—why is the History of Ming not suspected of innovation, yet I am suspected?
translations.idiomatic: The History of Ming fully records in its calendar treatise diagrams for arc-segments, chords and arcs, and lunar path deviations—why is the Ming History never accused of innovation, while I alone am suspected?

sentences.zh: 客曰：『後史增於前者，必非無因，若明史之用圖，亦有說歟？』

translations.literal: The guest said: "Later histories that add to earlier ones surely have their reasons—did the History of Ming also have grounds for using diagrams?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest said: "When later histories expand upon earlier ones, they surely have their reasons. Did the History of Ming also have grounds for using diagrams?"

sentences.zh: 梅子曰：『疑以傳疑，信以傳信，春秋法也，作史者誰能易之？

translations.literal: Master Mei said: "Pass on what is doubtful as doubtful, pass on what is credible as credible—this is the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals; who among historiographers can change it?"
translations.idiomatic: Master Mei said: "Pass on what is doubtful as doubtful and what is credible as credible—that is the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals. What historiographer would presume to alter it?"

sentences.zh: 古之治歷者數十家，大率不過增損日法，益天週，減歲餘，以求合一時而已。

translations.literal: Among the ancient calendrical astronomers there were dozens of schools; for the most part they did nothing more than add to or subtract from the day-count divisor, increase the celestial circumference, and reduce the surplus of the year, seeking only to accord with the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of schools of calendrical astronomy existed in antiquity, but most merely adjusted the day-count divisor, increasing the celestial circumference and reducing the year's remainder—seeking only to fit the calendar to their own age.

sentences.zh: 即太初之起數鍾律，大衍之造端蓍策，亦皆牽合，並未能深探天行之故，而發明其所以然之理。

translations.literal: Even the Taichu calendar's deriving numbers from pitch-pipes and bell-standards, and the Dayan calendar's beginning with yarrow-stalk divination—all were forced alignments; none could deeply probe the causes of celestial motion and elucidate the principles of why things are so.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Taichu calendar's derivation of numbers from pitch-pipes and bells, and the Dayan calendar's origin in yarrow-stalk divination, were strained expedients—none of them truly penetrated the causes of celestial motion or revealed the principles behind them.

sentences.zh: 本未嘗有圖，史臣何從取而載之？

translations.literal: There were originally no diagrams—how could historiographers have taken them and recorded them?
translations.idiomatic: Since there were originally no diagrams to begin with, what could historiographers have drawn upon to include them?

sentences.zh: 至元郭太史修授時，不用積年日法，全憑實測，用句股割員以求弦矢，於是有割圜諸圖載於歷草。

translations.literal: When in the Yuan dynasty Grand Astrologer Guo revised the Shoushi calendar, he abandoned accumulated years and day-count divisors, relying entirely on actual observation, using right triangles and arc-segments to seek chords and arcs—thus there arose circle-division diagrams recorded in the calendar draft.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Astrologer Guo Shoujing revised the Shoushi calendar in the Yuan, he abandoned accumulated-year methods and day-count divisors, relying entirely on observation. Using right-triangle geometry and arc-segment calculations to derive chords and arcs, he produced circle-division diagrams recorded in the calendar draft.

sentences.zh: 作元史時，不知採摭，則宋、王諸公之疏也。

translations.literal: When the History of Yuan was compiled, [the compilers] did not know to gather and select [them]—this was the neglect of the Song and Wang [scholars] and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the History of Yuan was compiled, the editors failed to gather and include these materials—a lapse on the part of Song Lian, Wang Xun, and their colleagues.

sentences.zh: 明之大統，實即授時。

translations.literal: The Ming Great Unity calendar was in fact the Shoushi calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming dynasty's Datong calendar was in essence the Shoushi calendar.

sentences.zh: 本朝纂修明史諸公，以義非圖不明，遂採歷草入志，其識極超。

translations.literal: The gentlemen who compiled the History of Ming in our dynasty, deeming that the meaning could not be made clear without diagrams, gathered the calendar draft into the treatise—their insight was exceedingly far-sighted.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars who compiled the History of Ming in our dynasty, recognizing that the meaning could not be conveyed without diagrams, incorporated the calendar draft into the treatise—an act of exceptional foresight.

sentences.zh: 復經聖君賢相鑑定，不以為非體而去之，俾精義傳於無窮，​​洵足開萬古作史者之心胸矣。

translations.literal: Furthermore, after examination and approval by the sage sovereign and worthy ministers, [the diagrams] were not removed as improper form, enabling subtle principles to be transmitted without end—truly sufficient to open the minds of historiographers for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, after review by the sage emperor and his wise ministers, the diagrams were not removed as violations of proper historiographical form, allowing profound principles to be transmitted for all time—a precedent that truly broadened the horizons of every historiographer since.

sentences.zh: 至於時憲立法之妙，義蘊之奧，悉具於圖，更不可去。

translations.literal: As for the subtleties of the Shixian calendar's establishment of methods and the profundities of its meaning—all are fully contained in the diagrams, and can still less be removed.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Shixian calendar, the elegance of its methods and the depth of its principles are fully embodied in its diagrams—they cannot be removed.

sentences.zh: 如必以去圖為合體，豈以明史為非體，而本朝之制不足法歟？

translations.literal: If removing diagrams must be deemed proper form, would you hold the History of Ming improper, and our dynasty's precedent unworthy of emulation?
translations.idiomatic: If removing diagrams is required for proper historiographical form, would you declare the History of Ming improper—and our dynasty's precedent unworthy of following?

sentences.zh: 且客亦知時憲之圖所自來乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, does the guest also know whence the Shixian diagrams come?
translations.idiomatic: Do you even know where the Shixian diagrams originated?

sentences.zh: 我聖祖仁皇帝憫絕學之失傳，留心探索四十餘年，見透底蘊，始親授儒臣，作圖立說，以闡明千古不傳之秘，即御製歷象考成是也。

translations.literal: Our Sacred Ancestor, the Benevolent Emperor, grieved that a lost learning had ceased to be transmitted; he devoted his attention to exploration for more than forty years, until he saw through to the foundations. Only then did he personally instruct Confucian officials, creating diagrams and establishing theories to elucidate secrets not transmitted for a thousand ages—this is the Imperially Composed Essentials of Calendrical Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Our Sacred Ancestor, the Benevolent Emperor Kangxi, grieved that this supreme learning had fallen out of transmission. For more than forty years he devoted himself to probing its depths until he grasped its foundations. Only then did he personally instruct his Confucian officials, devising diagrams and theories to illuminate secrets withheld for a thousand years—the Imperially Composed Essentials of Calendrical Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 餘親承聖訓，實與彙編之列。

translations.literal: I personally received the sage instruction and am in fact among those who compiled [the work].
translations.idiomatic: I personally received the emperor's instruction and took part in the compilation.

sentences.zh: 彼前輩纂修明史，尚不忍沒古人之善，創例以傳之。

translations.literal: Those predecessors who compiled the History of Ming still could not bear to suppress the merit of the ancients—they created a precedent to transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: The predecessors who compiled the History of Ming could not bear to suppress the achievements of the ancients—they established a new precedent to preserve them.

sentences.zh: 而餘以承學之臣，恭紀御製，顧恐失執事之意，而遷就迎合，以致聖學不彰，貽誤後學，尚得謂之信史乎？

translations.literal: Yet I, as a minister who inherited this learning, reverently recording the imperial composition—if I fear losing the chief compiler's favor and compromise to accommodate, causing the sage learning not to be manifest and misleading later students—can this still be called a faithful history?
translations.idiomatic: As one who inherited this learning, I am charged with reverently recording the imperial work. If I fear displeasing my superiors and compromise to accommodate them, allowing the emperor's learning to go unrecorded and misleading future scholars—can such a history still be called trustworthy?

sentences.zh: 不信之史，人可塞責，而何用餘越俎而代之？

translations.literal: An untrustworthy history—others can evade responsibility; of what use is it for me to overstep my role in its place?
translations.idiomatic: An untrustworthy history lets everyone off the hook—why should I overstep my bounds to substitute for others?

sentences.zh: 餘之呶呶，非沽直，不得已也。

translations.literal: My persistent remonstrance is not to seek a reputation for integrity—it is unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: My persistent remonstrance is not self-righteous posturing—it is something I cannot avoid.

sentences.zh: 然則韓子之自訟，亦謂其言之可以已者耳。

translations.literal: Thus Han Yu's self-reproach also meant only that his words could have stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu's self-reproach meant simply that his words might have stopped short of going so far.

sentences.zh: 使韓子果務為容悅以求倖免，則諍臣之論，佛骨之表，又何為若是其侃侃哉？』

translations.literal: If Han Yu had truly sought to please and curry favor to gain exemption, then why were his remonstrances as a loyal critic and his memorial on the Buddha relics so forthright and unsparing?
translations.idiomatic: If Han Yu had truly sought favor and exemption, why were his remonstrances as a loyal critic and his memorial on the Buddha relics so bold and uncompromising?

sentences.zh: 客唯唯而退。』

translations.literal: The guest assented vaguely and withdrew.'
translations.idiomatic: The guest murmured assent and withdrew.'

sentences.zh: 又儀象論曰：『齊政授時，儀象與算術並重。

translations.literal: There is also a Treatise on Armillary Instruments, which states: "In aligning governance and handing down the seasons, armillary instruments and calculation are equally important.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a Treatise on Astronomical Instruments, which states: "In regulating the calendar and proclaiming the seasons, astronomical instruments and mathematical calculation are equally essential.

sentences.zh: 蓋非算術，無以預推節候以前民用；

translations.literal: For without calculation, there is no means to calculate beforehand the seasonal markers to inform the people's use in advance;
translations.idiomatic: Without mathematical calculation, seasonal markers cannot be computed in advance to guide the people's affairs;

sentences.zh: 非儀象，無以測現在之行度，以驗推步之疏密，而為修改之端也。

translations.literal: Without armillary instruments, there is no means to measure present positions and motions, to verify the density or looseness of computational methods, and thus provide a starting point for correction.
translations.idiomatic: Without astronomical instruments, present celestial positions cannot be measured to test the accuracy of computational methods and provide grounds for revision.

sentences.zh: 虞書『璇璣玉衡』，為儀象之權輿，其制不傳。

translations.literal: The Documents of Yu's "Armillary Sphere and Jade Transverses" are the origin of armillary instruments; their construction was not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The "Armillary Sphere and Jade Transverse" in the Book of Yu represent the earliest astronomical instruments, though their construction has not survived.

sentences.zh: 漢人創造渾天儀，即璣衡遺制，唐、宋皆仿為之。

translations.literal: Han people created the armillary sphere, which is the vestigial form of the armillary transverse; Tang and Song all copied it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han created the armillary sphere, preserving the form of the ancient instruments; Tang and Song dynasties each reproduced them.

sentences.zh: 至元始有簡儀、仰儀、闚幾、景符等器，視古加詳矣。

translations.literal: Only in the Yuan did simplified armillary, altitude instrument, sighting frame, shadow marker, and other instruments appear—more detailed than the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Yuan did instruments such as the simplified armillary, altitude-measuring instrument, sighting frame, and shadow marker appear—considerably more refined than their ancient predecessors.

sentences.zh: 明於齊化門南倚城築觀像台，仿元制作渾儀、簡儀、天體三儀，置於台上，台下有晷影堂，圭表壺漏，國初因之。

translations.literal: In the Ming, south of Qihua Gate, leaning against the city wall they built the Observatory Platform, copying Yuan models to make armillary, simplified armillary, and celestial globe—the three instruments placed on the platform; below the platform were the Sundial Shadow Hall, gnomon table, and clepsydra; at the founding of our dynasty this was continued.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming, an observatory platform was built against the city wall south of Qihua Gate, with armillary sphere, simplified armillary, and celestial globe modeled on Yuan designs placed atop it. Below stood the sundial shadow hall, gnomon, and water clock—the early Qing preserved this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，命造新儀，十一年，告成，安置台上，其舊儀移藏他室。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, an order was issued to construct new instruments; in the eleventh year they were completed and installed on the platform; the old instruments were moved and stored in another chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi, new instruments were commissioned; they were completed in the eleventh year and installed on the platform, while the old instruments were moved to storage elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，西人紀理安欲炫其能而滅棄古法，復奏制象限儀，遂將所遺舊器用作廢銅，僅存明仿元渾儀、簡儀、天體三儀而已。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, the Westerner Kilian Stumpf wished to display his ability while abolishing and discarding ancient methods; he again memorialized to have a quadrant instrument made, and thus had the remaining old instruments melted down as scrap copper—only the Ming copies of the Yuan armillary, simplified armillary, and celestial globe remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi, the Jesuit Kilian Stumpf, seeking to display his own abilities while discarding ancient methods, petitioned to have a quadrant instrument made and had the remaining old instruments melted down for scrap—leaving only the Ming replicas of the Yuan armillary sphere, simplified armillary, and celestial globe.

sentences.zh: 所製象限儀成，亦置台上。

translations.literal: When the manufactured quadrant instrument was completed, it too was placed on the platform.
translations.idiomatic: When the new quadrant instrument was completed, it too was placed on the platform.

sentences.zh: 按明史云：『嘉靖間修相風桿及簡、渾二儀，立四大表以測晷影，而立運儀、正方案、懸晷、偏晷，具備於觀像台，一以元法為斷。』

translations.literal: According to the History of Ming: 'During the Jiajing reign they repaired the wind-vane pole and the simplified and armillary instruments, erected four great gnomons to measure sundial shadows, and established motion instruments, orientation instruments, suspended sundials, and inclined sundials—all complete at the Observatory Platform, following the Yuan method exclusively.'
translations.idiomatic: The History of Ming records: 'During the Jiajing reign, the wind-vane pole and the simplified and armillary instruments were restored; four great gnomons were erected to measure sundial shadows; motion, orientation, suspended, and inclined sundials were all installed on the observatory platform, following Yuan methods throughout.'

sentences.zh: 餘於康熙五十二三年間，充蒙養齋彙編官，屢赴觀像台測驗。

translations.literal: During the fifty-second and fifty-third years of Kangxi, I served as a compiler in the Mengyang Studio and repeatedly went to the Observatory Platform for testing.
translations.idiomatic: During the fifty-second and fifty-third years of Kangxi, while serving as a compiler in the Mengyang Studio, I made repeated visits to the observatory platform for measurements.

sentences.zh: 見台下所遺舊器甚多，而元制簡儀、仰儀諸器，俱有王珣、郭守敬監造姓名。

translations.literal: I saw many old instruments remaining below the platform; the Yuan-made simplified armillary, altitude instrument, and other instruments all bore the supervisory names of Wang Xun and Guo Shoujing.
translations.idiomatic: I found many old instruments stored below the platform; the Yuan-era simplified armillary, altitude instrument, and other instruments all bore the names of Wang Xun and Guo Shoujing as supervising craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 雖不無殘缺，然睹其遺制，想見創造苦心，不覺肅然起敬也。

translations.literal: Though not without damage and loss, yet seeing their surviving forms, one can imagine the painstaking effort of their creation—one cannot but feel solemn reverence arise.
translations.idiomatic: Though damaged in places, contemplating these surviving instruments and imagining the painstaking labor of their creators, one cannot help feeling a solemn reverence.

sentences.zh: 乾隆年間，監臣受西人之愚，屢欲廢台下餘器作銅送製造局，賴廷臣奏請存留，禮部奉旨查檢，始知僅存三儀，殆紀理安之燼餘也。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, the director was misled by Westerners and repeatedly wished to scrap the remaining instruments below the platform as copper for the manufacturing bureau; thanks to court officials memorializing for their preservation, the Ministry of Rites received an imperial order to investigate, and only then learned that only the three instruments remained—likely the cinders left by Kilian Stumpf.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign, the observatory director, misled by Western missionaries, repeatedly sought to melt down the remaining instruments below the platform for the manufacturing bureau. Only when court officials memorialized for their preservation and the Ministry of Rites investigated by imperial order was it discovered that only the three instruments survived—likely all that escaped Kilian Stumpf's destruction.

sentences.zh: 夫西人欲藉技術以行其教，故將盡滅古法，使後世無所考，彼益得以居奇，其心叵測。

translations.literal: The Westerners wish to use technical learning to propagate their religion; therefore they seek to abolish ancient methods entirely, so that later ages have nothing by which to investigate—they may the more hold themselves out as singular; their intentions are inscrutable.
translations.idiomatic: The Westerners seek to use technical learning to propagate their religion; by abolishing ancient methods they leave later generations with nothing to compare against, allowing themselves to hold a monopoly—their motives are not easily fathomed.

sentences.zh: 乃監臣無識，不思存什一於千百，而反助其為虐，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet the director lacked discernment, not thinking to preserve one in a thousand or a hundred, but rather aiding their oppression—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the observatory director, lacking discernment, thought nothing of preserving even a fraction of the heritage and instead aided in its destruction—why?

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年冬，有旨移置三儀於紫微殿前，古人法物，庶幾可以永存矣。』

translations.literal: In the winter of the ninth year of Qianlong, an imperial order transferred the three instruments to before the Hall of Purple Tenuity; the artifacts of the ancients may thus nearly be preserved forever."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the ninth year of Qianlong, an imperial order relocated the three instruments to the forecourt of the Hall of Purple Tenuity—the ancient instruments might at last be preserved for posterity."

sentences.zh: 又論句股曰：『句股和較相求，言算學者莫不留心，其法可謂詳且備矣，未有以句股積與句弦和較為問者。

translations.literal: There is also a Treatise on Right Triangles, which states: "In seeking sums and differences of legs and hypotenuse, students of mathematics all pay attention—the methods can be called detailed and complete; yet no one has posed problems using the product of the legs together with the sum and difference of leg and hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: There is also a Treatise on Right Triangles, which states: "Mathematicians everywhere study the methods for finding sums and differences of triangle sides—these techniques are thorough and well established. Yet no one has posed problems involving both the product of the legs and the sum or difference of a leg and the hypotenuse together.

sentences.zh: 元學士李冶著測圜海鏡，用餘句、餘股立算，神明變化，幾如五花八門，亦未及此。

translations.literal: The Yuan academician Li Ye wrote the Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement, using surplus leg and surplus side to establish calculations—wondrous in transformation, almost like endless variety—yet it too did not reach this.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan scholar Li Ye's Sea Mirror of Circle Measurement, though ingenious in its use of surplus legs and sides and wondrously varied in its transformations, does not reach this case either.

sentences.zh: 豈俱未計及耶？

translations.literal: Did they all fail to consider it?
translations.idiomatic: Did they all fail to consider this?

sentences.zh: 抑有其法而遺之耶？

translations.literal: Or did they have the method but lose it?
translations.idiomatic: Or did they possess the method but allow it to be lost?

sentences.zh: 統宗少廣章內，雖有句股積及句弦較兩題，乃偶合於句三股四之數，非通法。

translations.literal: Within the Lesser Breadth chapter of the Comprehensive Mastery, though there are two problems on the product of legs and the difference of leg and hypotenuse, they happen to agree with the numbers three and four for the legs—not a general method.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mastery's chapter on lesser breadth contains two problems on the product of legs and the leg-hypotenuse difference, but these happen to work only for the classic three-four-five triangle—not as a general method.

sentences.zh: 昔待罪蒙養齋，彙編數理精蘊，意欲立法以補其缺。

translations.literal: Formerly, bearing my post in the Mengyang Studio, compiling the Essentials of Mathematical Principles, I intended to establish methods to fill this gap.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in the Mengyang Studio compiling the Essentials of Mathematical Principles, I intended to devise methods to fill this gap.

sentences.zh: 先用平方輾轉推求，皆不能禦，思之累日，而後得用帶縱立方求句股二法。』

translations.literal: First using square roots in successive alternation to seek solutions, all could not overcome [the problem]; after thinking for many days, I then obtained two methods using mixed-dimension cubics to seek the legs."
translations.idiomatic: I first tried successive applications of square-root extraction without success. After days of reflection, I finally derived two methods using mixed-dimension cubics to solve for the legs."

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有三，諡文穆。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-three; posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-three and was granted the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 鈁，字導和，瑴成第四子也。

translations.literal: Fang, courtesy name Daohe, was the fourth son of Juecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, styled Daohe, was the fourth son of Juecheng.

sentences.zh: 瑴成纂叢書輯要六十餘卷，圖皆所繪。

translations.literal: Juecheng compiled the Essentials of the Collectanea in more than sixty juan; all the diagrams were drawn by him.
translations.idiomatic: Juecheng compiled the Essentials of the Collectanea in more than sixty volumes; Fang drew all the illustrations.

sentences.zh: 刪訂統宗圖，十之七八，皆出其手。

translations.literal: Revising the diagrams for the Comprehensive Mastery, seven or eight tenths came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: In revising the diagrams for the Comprehensive Mastery, seven or eight tenths were his own work.

sentences.zh: 年二十六，卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty-six, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 文鼐，字和仲，文鼎從弟也。

translations.literal: Wen Nai, courtesy name Hezhong, was Wen Ding's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Nai, styled Hezhong, was Wen Ding's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 初學歷時，未有五星通軌，無從入算。

translations.literal: When he first studied calendrical astronomy, there was no comprehensive ephemeris for the five planets, and there was no way to enter into calculation.
translations.idiomatic: When he first studied calendrical astronomy, no comprehensive ephemeris for the five planets existed, and there was no basis for computation.

sentences.zh: 與兄文鼎取元史歷經，以三差法佈為五星盈縮立成，然後算之，共成步五星式六卷。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Wen Ding he took the calendar classic from the History of Yuan, using the three-difference method to arrange tables of the five planets' expansion and contraction, then calculated them—together completing the Six Fascicles of Methods for Computing the Five Planets.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brother Wen Ding, he drew on the calendar classic in the History of Yuan, using the three-difference method to compile tables of planetary elongation and contraction, then computed from them—producing the Six Fascicles of Methods for Computing the Five Planets.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 文鼏，字爾素，文鼎季弟也。

translations.literal: Wen Bi, courtesy name Ersu, was Wen Ding's youngest brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Bi, styled Ersu, was Wen Ding's youngest brother.

sentences.zh: 著中西經星同異考一卷。

translations.literal: He wrote One Fascicle of an Examination of the Same and Different among Chinese and Western Fixed Stars.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Examination of the Same and Different among Chinese and Western Fixed Stars in one fascicle.

sentences.zh: 以三垣二十八宿星名，依步天歌次第，臚列其目，而以中、西有無多寡分注其下，載古歌、西歌於後。

translations.literal: Taking the star names of the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions, following the order of the Song of Pacing the Heavens, he listed them in detail, annotating below the presence, absence, and number of each in Chinese and Western [catalogues], with the ancient song and Western song appended at the end.
translations.idiomatic: He listed the star names of the Three Enclosures and Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions in the order of the Song of Pacing the Heavens, annotating below each entry whether it appeared in Chinese and Western catalogues and in what numbers, with the ancient and Western star songs appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 古歌即步天歌，西歌則利瑪竇所撰經天該也。

translations.literal: The ancient song is the Song of Pacing the Heavens; the Western song is the Summary of the Heavens composed by Matteo Ricci.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient song is the Song of Pacing the Heavens; the Western song is Matteo Ricci's Summary of the Heavens.

sentences.zh: 其南極諸星，則據湯若望算書及南懷仁儀象志，為考證補歌，附之於末。

translations.literal: As for the stars of the South Pole, he relied on Adam Schall's computational works and Ferdinand Verbiest's Treatise on Astronomical Instruments to provide verification and supplementary songs, appended at the end.
translations.idiomatic: For the stars of the South Pole, he drew on Adam Schall's computational works and Ferdinand Verbiest's Treatise on Astronomical Instruments to provide verification and supplementary songs, appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 其發凡略言：『齊七政，非先定恆星，則無從著手。

translations.literal: In his introductory overview he briefly states: "In aligning the seven luminaries, unless fixed stars are first established, there is no place to begin.
translations.idiomatic: In his introductory overview he briefly states: "To regulate the seven luminaries, one must first establish the fixed stars—without them there is no place to begin.

sentences.zh: 故曰『七政如乘傳，恆星其地志也；

translations.literal: Thus it is said: 'The seven luminaries are like relay horses; fixed stars are their route maps;
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: 'The seven luminaries are like relay horses on a post road; the fixed stars are their route maps;

sentences.zh: 七政如行棋，恆星其楸局也。』

translations.literal: The seven luminaries are like moving pieces in a game; fixed stars are the board.'
translations.idiomatic: The seven luminaries are like chess pieces in motion; the fixed stars are the board.'

sentences.zh: 曰『恆』者，謂其終古不易；

translations.literal: What is called 'fixed' means that they are unchanged from antiquity to the present;
translations.idiomatic: What is called 'fixed' means that they are unchanged from antiquity to the present;

sentences.zh: 曰『經』者，謂其不同緯星南北行，『經』亦有『恆』之義焉。

translations.literal: What is called 'longitude star' means that they differ from latitude stars in moving north and south—'longitude' also carries the meaning of 'fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: What is called 'longitude star' means that they differ from latitude stars in their north-south motion—'longitude' also carries the sense of 'fixed.'

sentences.zh: 是編專以中、西兩家所傳之星歌星名考其多寡同異，故曰經星同異考。

translations.literal: This compilation specifically examines the star songs and star names transmitted by Chinese and Western schools for their numbers, sameness, and difference—hence it is called an Examination of the Same and Different among Fixed Stars.
translations.idiomatic: This work specifically compares the star songs and star names transmitted by Chinese and Western traditions for their numbers, correspondences, and differences—hence its title, Examination of the Same and Different among Fixed Stars.

sentences.zh: 星官之書，自黃帝始，重黎、羲和，志天文者，紛糅不一。

translations.literal: Books on star officials begin with the Yellow Emperor; Chongli, Xi and He—those who recorded astronomy—are mixed and inconsistent.
translations.idiomatic: Star catalogues begin with the Yellow Emperor; Chongli, Xi and He, and later astronomers all recorded the heavens, but their accounts are inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 漢張衡云：『中外之官常明者百有二十四，可名者三百二十，為星二千五百，微星之數蓋萬一千五百二十。』

translations.literal: Zhang Heng of the Han said: "Among the inner and outer officials, those constantly bright number one hundred twenty-four; those that can be named number three hundred twenty, comprising two thousand five hundred stars; the number of faint stars probably exceeds eleven thousand five hundred twenty."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng of the Han wrote: "Among the inner and outer asterisms, those constantly bright number one hundred twenty-four; those that can be named number three hundred twenty, comprising two thousand five hundred stars; faint stars probably exceed eleven thousand five hundred twenty."

sentences.zh: 至三國時，太史令陳卓始列甘、石、巫咸三家所著星，總二百八十三官，一千四百八十四星。

translations.literal: By the Three Kingdoms period, Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo first compiled the stars recorded by the three schools of Gan, Shi, and Wuxian—altogether two hundred eighty-three officials and one thousand four hundred eighty-four stars.
translations.idiomatic: By the Three Kingdoms period, Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo first compiled the stars recorded by the three schools of Gan, Shi, and Wuxian—altogether two hundred eighty-three asterisms and one thousand four hundred eighty-four stars.

sentences.zh: 自唐以來，以儀考測，迨宋兩朝志，始能言某星去極若干度，入某星若干度，為說較詳。

translations.literal: From the Tang onward, instruments were used for examination and measurement; by the annals of the two Song dynasties, one could finally state how many degrees a given star was from the pole and how many degrees it entered a given star—the account became more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang onward, instruments were used for measurement; by the annals of the Northern and Southern Song, astronomers could finally specify how many degrees a given star stood from the pole and how many degrees it entered another star—the accounts became considerably more detailed.

sentences.zh: 此中國之言星學者。

translations.literal: This is the Chinese discourse on star learning.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the Chinese tradition of stellar astronomy.

sentences.zh: 西儒星學遠有端緒，據其書所譯，周赧王丙寅古地末一測，漢永和戊寅多祿某一測，明嘉靖乙酉尼谷老一測，萬曆乙酉第谷一測，崇禎戊辰湯若望一測。

translations.literal: Western scholars' star learning has distant origins; according to their translated books: in the bingyin year of King Nan of Zhou, Giacomo one measurement; in the wuyin year of Yonghe of Han, Tycho Brahe one measurement; in the yiyou year of Jiajing of Ming, Niccolo one measurement; in the yiyou year of Wanli, Tycho one measurement; in the wuchen year of Chongzhen, Adam Schall one measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Western stellar astronomy has ancient origins; according to their translated works, observations were made in the bingyin year of King Nan of Zhou by Giacomo, in the wuyin year of the Han Yonghe era by Ptolemy, in the yiyou year of the Ming Jiajing era by Copernicus, in the yiyou year of Wanli by Tycho Brahe, and in the wuchen year of Chongzhen by Adam Schall.

sentences.zh: 國朝康熙壬子，南懷仁著儀象志，又依歲差改定黃經及赤經。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, in the renzi year of Kangxi, Ferdinand Verbiest wrote the Treatise on Astronomical Instruments, again revising ecliptic longitude and right ascension according to precession.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty, in the renzi year of Kangxi, Ferdinand Verbiest wrote the Treatise on Astronomical Instruments, revising ecliptic and right ascension according to precession.

sentences.zh: 今依南公志表，稽其大小，分為六等。

translations.literal: Now following Master Nan's treatise tables, examining their magnitudes, they are divided into six grades.
translations.idiomatic: Following Verbiest's treatise tables, stars are classified by magnitude into six grades.

sentences.zh: 一等大星一十有六，二等星六十有八，三等星二百有八，四等星五百一十有二，五等星三百四十有二，六等星七百三十有二，總計一千八百七十八。

translations.literal: First-magnitude stars number sixteen; second-magnitude sixty-eight; third-magnitude two hundred eight; fourth-magnitude five hundred twelve; fifth-magnitude three hundred forty-two; sixth-magnitude seven hundred thirty-two—in all one thousand eight hundred seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: First-magnitude stars number sixteen; second-magnitude sixty-eight; third-magnitude two hundred eight; fourth-magnitude five hundred twelve; fifth-magnitude three hundred forty-two; sixth-magnitude seven hundred thirty-two—a total of one thousand eight hundred seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 其微茫小星，則不能以數計。

translations.literal: As for faint and tiny stars, they cannot be counted by number.
translations.idiomatic: Faint and tiny stars are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 此泰西之學也。』

translations.literal: This is the learning of the Far West."
translations.idiomatic: Such is the Western tradition of stellar astronomy."

sentences.zh: 文鼏又有累年算稿，文鼎為錄存，名曰授時步交食式一卷。

translations.literal: Wen Bi also had computational drafts accumulated over many years; Wen Ding recorded and preserved them, titled One Fascicle of Shoushi Methods for Computing Eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Bi also left computational drafts accumulated over many years; Wen Ding preserved them under the title Shoushi Methods for Computing Eclipses in one fascicle.

sentences.zh: 又有幾何類求新法，算書中比例規解，本無算例，文鼎作度算，用文鼏所補，而參之以陳藎謨尺算用法。

translations.literal: There is also a New Method of Geometric Analogical Seeking; in computational books the Explanation of the Proportional Compass originally had no worked examples—Wen Ding wrote degree calculations using Wen Bi's supplements, cross-referenced with Chen Jingmo's Methods for Using the Calculating Ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He also left a New Method of Geometric Analogical Seeking; the Explanation of the Proportional Compass in computational books originally lacked worked examples—Wen Ding wrote degree calculations using Wen Bi's supplements, cross-referenced with Chen Jingmo's Methods for Using the Calculating Ruler.

sentences.zh: 明安圖，字靜庵，蒙古正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ming Antu, courtesy name Jing'an, was a man of the Mongol Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Antu, styled Jing'an, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 官欽天監監正。

translations.literal: He held office as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 受數學於聖祖，預修禦定歷象考成後編、禦定儀象考成。

translations.literal: He received mathematical learning from the Sacred Ancestor and participated in compiling the Later Compilation of the Imperially Fixed Essentials of Calendrical Astronomy and the Imperially Fixed Essentials of Astronomical Instruments.
translations.idiomatic: He studied mathematics under the Sacred Ancestor Kangxi and participated in compiling the Later Compilation of the Imperially Fixed Essentials of Calendrical Astronomy and the Imperially Fixed Essentials of Astronomical Instruments.

sentences.zh: 因西士杜德美用連比例演周徑密率及求正弦、正矢之法，知其理深奧，索解未易，因積思三十餘年，著割圜密率捷法四卷。

translations.literal: Because the Western scholar Pierre Jartoux used continued proportions to derive the precise ratio of circumference to diameter and methods for seeking sine and versed sine, knowing its principles were profound and difficult to solve, he accumulated thought for more than thirty years and wrote the Quick Methods of Circle Division and Precise Ratios in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jesuit Pierre Jartoux used continued proportions to derive the precise ratio of circumference to diameter and methods for computing sine and versed sine, Ming Antu recognized the profound difficulty of these principles. After more than thirty years of reflection, he wrote the Quick Methods of Circle Division and Precise Ratios in four fascicles.

sentences.zh: 一曰步法，於杜氏三法外，補創弧背求通弦、求矢法，仍杜氏原法，但通加一四除耳。

translations.literal: The first is called step methods: beyond Jartoux's three methods, he supplemented and created methods for seeking full chord and versed sine from arc length; still following Jartoux's original methods, but with one added and four divided throughout.
translations.idiomatic: The first section covers step methods: beyond Jartoux's three methods, he devised methods for deriving full chord and versed sine from arc length, still following Jartoux's original approach but with one added and four divided throughout.

sentences.zh: 又弦、矢求弧背，並通弦、矢求弧背，凡六法，合杜氏共成九法。

translations.literal: Further, from chord and versed sine seeking arc length, and from full chord and versed sine seeking arc length—six methods in all; together with Jartoux's, nine methods in total.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised six methods for deriving arc length from chord and versed sine, and from full chord and versed sine—nine methods in all, together with Jartoux's three.

sentences.zh: 其弦求弧背法，以弦為連比例二率，半徑為一率，求得二、四、六、八、十諸率，以一、三、五、七、九之五數各自乘，為累次乘數。

translations.literal: His method of seeking arc length from chord takes the chord as the second term of continued proportion, the radius as the first term, obtaining the second, fourth, sixth, eighth, and tenth terms; the five numbers one, three, five, seven, and nine each multiply respectively, forming successive multipliers.
translations.idiomatic: In his method for deriving arc length from chord, the chord serves as the second term of a continued proportion and the radius as the first; from these one obtains the second, fourth, sixth, eighth, and tenth terms. The odd numbers one, three, five, seven, and nine serve respectively as successive multipliers.

sentences.zh: 二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九相挨，兩兩相乘，為累次除數，即用二率為第一得數。

translations.literal: Two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine in succession, each pair multiplied together, form successive divisors; then using the second term as the first result.
translations.idiomatic: The numbers two through nine in succession, multiplied in adjacent pairs, form successive divisors; the second term of the proportion yields the first result.

sentences.zh: 復置四率，以第一乘數乘之，第一除數除之，為第二得數。

translations.literal: Then set the fourth term, multiply by the first multiplier and divide by the first divisor, obtaining the second result.
translations.idiomatic: Next, taking the fourth term, multiply by the first multiplier and divide by the first divisor to obtain the second result.

sentences.zh: 又置六率，以第一、第二乘數乘之，第一、第二除數除之，為第三得數。

translations.literal: Again set the sixth term, multiply by the first and second multipliers and divide by the first and second divisors, obtaining the third result.
translations.idiomatic: Again taking the sixth term, multiply by the first and second multipliers and divide by the first and second divisors to obtain the third result.

sentences.zh: 又置八率，以第一、第二、第三乘數乘之，第一、第二、第三除數除之，為第四得數。

translations.literal: Again set the eighth term, multiply by the first, second, and third multipliers and divide by the first, second, and third divisors, obtaining the fourth result.
translations.idiomatic: Again taking the eighth term, multiply by the first, second, and third multipliers and divide by the first, second, and third divisors to obtain the fourth result.

sentences.zh: 如是累求，至所得數祗一位止，乃★之，即所求之弧背也。

translations.literal: Proceed thus accumulating and seeking, until the number obtained has only one place remaining and stops; then ★ them, and that is the arc length sought.
translations.idiomatic: Proceed by repeated iteration until the result has only one significant place left; combine the terms, and the sum is the arc length sought.

sentences.zh: 矢求弧背法，倍正矢為連比例三率，亦以半徑為一率，求得五、七、九、十一諸率。

translations.literal: The method of seeking arc length from versed sine: double the versed sine as the third term of continued proportion; also take the radius as the first term, obtaining the fifth, seventh, ninth, and eleventh terms.
translations.idiomatic: In the method for deriving arc length from versed sine, the doubled versed sine serves as the third term of a continued proportion and the radius as the first; from these one obtains the fifth, seventh, ninth, and eleventh terms.

sentences.zh: 以一、二、三、四、五之五數各自乘，為屢次乘數，三、四、五、六、七、八、九、十相挨，兩兩相乘，為屢次除數，即用三率為第一得數。

translations.literal: The five numbers one, two, three, four, and five each multiply respectively, forming successive multipliers; three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten in succession, each pair multiplied together, form successive divisors; then using the third term as the first result.
translations.idiomatic: The numbers one through five serve respectively as successive multipliers; three through ten in succession, multiplied in adjacent pairs, form successive divisors; the third term of the proportion yields the first result.

sentences.zh: 復置五率，以第一乘數乘之，第一除數除之，為第二得數。

translations.literal: Then set the fifth term, multiply by the first multiplier and divide by the first divisor, obtaining the second result.
translations.idiomatic: Next, taking the fifth term, multiply by the first multiplier and divide by the first divisor to obtain the second result.

sentences.zh: 又置七率，以第一、第二乘數乘之，第一、第二除數除之，為第三得數。

translations.literal: Again set the seventh term, multiply by the first and second multipliers and divide by the first and second divisors, obtaining the third result.
translations.idiomatic: Again taking the seventh term, multiply by the first and second multipliers and divide by the first and second divisors to obtain the third result.

sentences.zh: 又置九率，以第一、第二、第三乘數乘之，第一、第二、第三除數除之，為第四得數。

translations.literal: Again set the ninth term, multiply by the first, second, and third multipliers and divide by the first, second, and third divisors, obtaining the fourth result.
translations.idiomatic: Again taking the ninth term, multiply by the first, second, and third multipliers and divide by the first, second, and third divisors to obtain the fourth result.

sentences.zh: 如是累求，至所得數祗一位而止。

translations.literal: Proceed thus accumulating and seeking, until the number obtained has only one place remaining and stops.
translations.idiomatic: Proceed by repeated iteration until the result has only one significant place left.

sentences.zh: 開平方，即所求之弧背也，通弦求弧背，亦各加一四除。

translations.literal: Take the square root, and that is the arc length sought; for seeking arc length from full chord, likewise add one and divide by four throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Extract the square root, and the result is the arc length sought; for deriving arc length from full chord, likewise apply one added and four divided throughout.

sentences.zh: 矢求弧背，則三率又多加一四。

translations.literal: For seeking arc length from versed sine, one additionally adds one to the third term and divides by four.
translations.idiomatic: When deriving arc length from versed sine, one additionally adds one to the third term and divides by four.

sentences.zh: 因更創餘弧求弦矢，餘弦矢求本弧，及借弧與正、餘弦互求四術。

translations.literal: Accordingly he further created four methods: seeking chord and versed sine from remainder arc, seeking the original arc from remainder chord and versed sine, and mutual seeking between borrowed arc and sine and cosine.
translations.idiomatic: He further devised four methods: deriving chord and versed sine from a remainder arc, deriving the original arc from remainder chord and versed sine, and mutual conversion between a borrowed arc and sine and cosine.

sentences.zh: 二曰用法，以角度求八線，及直線、弧線、三角形邊角相求，共設七題。

translations.literal: Second is called application methods: seeking the eight lines from an angle, and mutual seeking among straight lines, arcs, and triangle sides and angles — seven problems in all.
translations.idiomatic: The second section covers application methods: deriving the eight trigonometric lines from an angle, and mutual solution of straight lines, arcs, and the sides and angles of triangles — seven worked problems in all.

sentences.zh: 謂今法所以密於古者，以用三角形也。

translations.literal: It is said that the reason present methods are more precise than ancient ones is that triangles are used.
