translations.idiomatic: The present methods surpass the ancient ones precisely because they employ triangles.

sentences.zh: 然三角形非用八線表不能相求，惟用此法，以之立表則甚易，以之推三角形，則不用表而得數同。

translations.literal: Yet triangles cannot be mutually solved without the eight-line table; only with this method — using it to establish tables is very easy, and using it to derive triangles, one obtains the same numbers without using tables.
translations.idiomatic: Triangles cannot be solved without the eight-line table — yet with this method alone, composing tables becomes very easy, and triangles can be solved to the same numerical results without any table at all.

sentences.zh: 三、四兩卷曰法解，皆闡明弦、矢與弧背相求之根。

translations.literal: The third and fourth juan are called Explication of Methods, all clarifying the roots of mutual seeking among chord, versed sine, and arc length.
translations.idiomatic: The third and fourth fascicles, titled Explication of Methods, explain the foundations of converting among chord, versed sine, and arc length.

sentences.zh: 其法先以一分弧通弦求二分弧通弧弦之數，次以一分、二分弧通弦求三分、四分全弧通弦之數，以一分三分弧通弦求五分全弧通弦之數。

translations.literal: The method first uses the full chord of a one-part arc to seek the number for the full chord of a two-part arc; next uses the full chords of one-part and two-part arcs to seek those of three-part and four-part full arcs; uses the full chords of one-part and three-part arcs to seek that of the five-part full arc.
translations.idiomatic: The method first derives the full chord of a two-part arc from that of a one-part arc; next derives the full chords of three- and four-part arcs from those of one- and two-part arcs; and derives the full chord of a five-part arc from those of one- and three-part arcs.

sentences.zh: 又因二分、五分相乘得十分，十分自乘得百分，十分、百分相乘得千分，十分、千分相乘得萬分。

translations.literal: Further, two-part and five-part multiplied yield ten-part; ten-part self-multiplied yields hundred-part; ten-part and hundred-part multiplied yield thousand-part; ten-part and thousand-part multiplied yield ten-thousand-part.
translations.idiomatic: Two-part and five-part arcs multiplied yield ten-part; ten-part squared yields hundred-part; ten-part and hundred-part multiplied yield thousand-part; ten-part and thousand-part multiplied yield ten-thousand-part.

sentences.zh: 遂以半徑為一率，一分弧通弦為二率，各如相乘之率數，求得十、百、千、萬諸分弧率數。

translations.literal: Then taking the radius as the first term and the full chord of a one-part arc as the second term, according to the numbers of mutually multiplied terms, one obtains the term numbers for ten-, hundred-, thousand-, and ten-thousand-part arcs.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the radius as the first term and the full chord of a one-part arc as the second, and applying the corresponding products of terms, one obtains the proportional terms for ten-, hundred-, thousand-, and ten-thousand-part arcs.

sentences.zh: 比例得弧背求通弦，應減四率二十四分之一，加六率八十分之一，減八率一百六十八分之一，加十率二百八十八分之一，減十二率四百四十分之一，加十四率六百二十四分之一，減十六率八百四十分之一。

translations.literal: By proportion, seeking full chord from arc length: subtract one twenty-fourth from the fourth term, add one eightieth to the sixth term, subtract one one-hundred-sixty-eighth from the eighth term, add one two-hundred-eighty-eighth to the tenth term, subtract one four-hundred-fortieth from the twelfth term, add one six-hundred-twenty-fourth to the fourteenth term, subtract one eight-hundred-fortieth from the sixteenth term.
translations.idiomatic: By proportion, to derive full chord from arc length: subtract one twenty-fourth from the fourth term, add one eightieth to the sixth, subtract one-hundred-sixty-eighth from the eighth, add one two-hundred-eighty-eighth to the tenth, subtract one four-hundred-fortieth from the twelfth, add one six-hundred-twenty-fourth to the fourteenth, and subtract one eight-hundred-fortieth from the sixteenth.

sentences.zh: 各四歸之，則二十四得六，為二三相乘數；

translations.literal: Each divided by four yields: twenty-four gives six, as the product of two and three;
translations.idiomatic: Dividing each by four: twenty-four yields six, the product of two and three;

sentences.zh: 八十得二十，為四五相乘數；

translations.literal: eighty gives twenty, as the product of four and five;
translations.idiomatic: eighty yields twenty, the product of four and five;

sentences.zh: 一百六十八得四十二，為六七相乘數；

translations.literal: one hundred sixty-eight gives forty-two, as the product of six and seven;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred sixty-eight yields forty-two, the product of six and seven;

sentences.zh: 二百八十八得七十二，為八九相乘數；

translations.literal: two hundred eighty-eight gives seventy-two, as the product of eight and nine;
translations.idiomatic: two hundred eighty-eight yields seventy-two, the product of eight and nine;

sentences.zh: 四百四十得一百一十，為十與十一相乘數；

translations.literal: four hundred forty gives one hundred ten, as the product of ten and eleven;
translations.idiomatic: four hundred forty yields one hundred ten, the product of ten and eleven;

sentences.zh: 六百二十四得一百五十六，為十二與十三相乘數；

translations.literal: six hundred twenty-four gives one hundred fifty-six, as the product of twelve and thirteen;
translations.idiomatic: six hundred twenty-four yields one hundred fifty-six, the product of twelve and thirteen;

sentences.zh: 八百四十得二百一十，為十四與十五相乘數。

translations.literal: eight hundred forty gives two hundred ten, as the product of fourteen and fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: eight hundred forty yields two hundred ten, the product of fourteen and fifteen.

sentences.zh: 故以二、三、四、五、六、七、八、九等數兩兩相乘，為屢次除數。

translations.literal: Therefore the numbers two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine, each pair multiplied together, form successive divisors.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the numbers two through nine, multiplied in adjacent pairs, form successive divisors.

sentences.zh: 又以通弦求得二率一分多，四率一分，六率九分，八率二百二十五分，十率一萬一千二十五分，十二率八十九萬三千二十五分，十四率一億八百五萬六千二十五分，得後率分數為實。

translations.literal: Further, from full chord one obtains: the second term one part plus, the fourth term one part, the sixth term nine parts, the eighth term two hundred twenty-five parts, the tenth term eleven thousand twenty-five parts, the twelfth term eight hundred ninety-three thousand twenty-five parts, the fourteenth term one hundred eight million fifty-six thousand twenty-five parts — taking the later term's fractional parts as dividend.
translations.idiomatic: From the full chord one further obtains fractional parts at the second term (one part plus), fourth term (one part), sixth term (nine parts), eighth term (two hundred twenty-five parts), tenth term (eleven thousand twenty-five parts), twelfth term (eight hundred ninety-three thousand twenty-five parts), and fourteenth term (one hundred eight million fifty-six thousand twenty-five parts); these later-term fractions serve as dividends.

sentences.zh: 各遞降二等，使二率降為四率，四率降為六率，得前率分數為法。

translations.literal: Each descends two ranks in succession, making the second term descend to the fourth term and the fourth to the sixth term — obtaining the earlier term's fractional parts as divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Each descends two ranks in succession — the second term to the fourth, the fourth to the sixth — yielding the earlier-term fractions as divisors.

sentences.zh: 以法除實，得四率一分，為一自乘數；

translations.literal: Dividing dividend by divisor yields one part at the fourth term, as the self-square of one;
translations.idiomatic: Dividing dividend by divisor yields one part at the fourth term, the square of one;

sentences.zh: 六率九分，為三自乘數；

translations.literal: nine parts at the sixth term, as the self-square of three;
translations.idiomatic: nine parts at the sixth term, the square of three;

sentences.zh: 八率二十五分，為五自乘數；

translations.literal: twenty-five parts at the eighth term, as the self-square of five;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-five parts at the eighth term, the square of five;

sentences.zh: 十率四十九分，為七自乘數；

translations.literal: forty-nine parts at the tenth term, as the self-square of seven;
translations.idiomatic: forty-nine parts at the tenth term, the square of seven;

sentences.zh: 十二率八十一分，為九自乘數；

translations.literal: eighty-one parts at the twelfth term, as the self-square of nine;
translations.idiomatic: eighty-one parts at the twelfth term, the square of nine;

sentences.zh: 十四率一百二十一分，為十一自乘數；

translations.literal: one hundred twenty-one parts at the fourteenth term, as the self-square of eleven;
translations.idiomatic: one hundred twenty-one parts at the fourteenth term, the square of eleven;

sentences.zh: 十六率一百六十九分，為十三自乘數：故以一、三、五、七、九等數各自乘為屢次乘數。

translations.literal: one hundred sixty-nine parts at the sixteenth term, as the self-square of thirteen: therefore the numbers one, three, five, seven, and nine each multiply respectively, forming successive multipliers.
translations.idiomatic: one hundred sixty-nine parts at the sixteenth term, the square of thirteen; hence the odd numbers one, three, five, seven, and nine serve respectively as successive multipliers.

sentences.zh: 次求通弦法，求得十、百、千、萬諸分弧正矢率數，比例得弧背求正矢，應減五率十二分之一，加七率三十分之一，減九率五十六分之一，加十一率九十分之一，減十三率一百三十二分之一，加十五率一百八十二分之一，減十七率二百四十分之一；

translations.literal: Next the method for seeking full chord: obtaining term numbers for the versed sine of ten-, hundred-, thousand-, and ten-thousand-part arcs; by proportion seeking versed sine from arc length — subtract one twelfth from the fifth term, add one thirtieth to the seventh term, subtract one fifty-sixth from the ninth term, add one ninetieth to the eleventh term, subtract one one-hundred-thirty-second from the thirteenth term, add one one-hundred-eighty-second to the fifteenth term, subtract one two-hundred-fortieth from the seventeenth term;
translations.idiomatic: Next, the method for deriving full chord: having obtained proportional terms for the versed sines of ten-, hundred-, thousand-, and ten-thousand-part arcs, to derive versed sine from arc length by proportion — subtract one twelfth from the fifth term, add one thirtieth to the seventh, subtract one fifty-sixth from the ninth, add one ninetieth to the eleventh, subtract one-hundred-thirty-second from the thirteenth, add one-hundred-eighty-second to the fifteenth, and subtract one two-hundred-fortieth from the seventeenth;

sentences.zh: 而十二為三四相乘數，三十為五六相乘數，五十六為七八相乘數，九十為九與十相乘數，一百三十二為十一與十二相乘數，一百八十二為十三與十四相乘數，二百四十為十五與十六相乘數，故以三、四、五、六、七、八、九等數兩兩相乘，為屢次除數。

translations.literal: And twelve is the product of three and four, thirty of five and six, fifty-six of seven and eight, ninety of nine and ten, one hundred thirty-two of eleven and twelve, one hundred eighty-two of thirteen and fourteen, two hundred forty of fifteen and sixteen; therefore the numbers three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine, each pair multiplied together, form successive divisors.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve is three times four, thirty is five times six, fifty-six is seven times eight, ninety is nine times ten, one hundred thirty-two is eleven times twelve, one hundred eighty-two is thirteen times fourteen, and two hundred forty is fifteen times sixteen; hence three through nine, multiplied in adjacent pairs, form successive divisors.

sentences.zh: 又以正矢求得五率一分多，七率四分，九率三十六分，十一率五百七十六分，十三率一萬四千四百分，十五率五十一萬八千四百分，十七率二千五百四十萬一千六百分，為後率分數，各遞降二等為前率分數。

translations.literal: Further from versed sine one obtains: the fifth term one part plus, the seventh term four parts, the ninth term thirty-six parts, the eleventh term five hundred seventy-six parts, the thirteenth term fourteen thousand four hundred parts, the fifteenth term five hundred eighteen thousand four hundred parts, the seventeenth term twenty-five million four hundred one thousand six hundred parts, as the later term's fractional parts; each descends two ranks in succession for the earlier term's fractional parts.
translations.idiomatic: From the versed sine one further obtains fractional parts at the fifth term (one part plus), seventh term (four parts), ninth term (thirty-six parts), eleventh term (five hundred seventy-six parts), thirteenth term (fourteen thousand four hundred parts), fifteenth term (five hundred eighteen thousand four hundred parts), and seventeenth term (twenty-five million four hundred one thousand six hundred parts) as later-term dividends, each paired by descending two ranks with an earlier-term divisor.

sentences.zh: 如前通弦法，除得五率一分為一自乘數，七率四分為二自乘數，九率九分為三自乘數，十一率十六分為四自乘數，十三率二十五分為五自乘數，十五率三十六分為六自乘數，十七率四十九為七自乘數，故以一、二、三、四、五等數各自乘，為屢次乘數。

translations.literal: As in the previous full-chord method, dividing yields the fifth term one part as the self-square of one, the seventh term four parts as the self-square of two, the ninth term nine parts as the self-square of three, the eleventh term sixteen parts as the self-square of four, the thirteenth term twenty-five parts as the self-square of five, the fifteenth term thirty-six parts as the self-square of six, the seventeenth term forty-nine as the self-square of seven; therefore the numbers one, two, three, four, and five each multiply respectively, forming successive multipliers.
translations.idiomatic: As in the full-chord method above, division yields one part at the fifth term (the square of one), four parts at the seventh (the square of two), nine parts at the ninth (the square of three), sixteen parts at the eleventh (the square of four), twenty-five parts at the thirteenth (the square of five), thirty-six parts at the fifteenth (the square of six), and forty-nine at the seventeenth (the square of seven); hence one through five serve respectively as successive multipliers.

sentences.zh: 書未成而卒，子新續之。

translations.literal: The book was unfinished when he died; his son Xin continued it.
translations.idiomatic: He died before the book was finished; his son Xin completed it.

sentences.zh: 新，字景臻，安圖季子。

translations.literal: Xin, courtesy name Jingzhen, was Ming Antu's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, styled Jingzhen, was Ming Antu's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 充食俸生。

translations.literal: He held the status of stipend student.
translations.idiomatic: He held stipend-student status at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 安圖病且革，以所著捷法授之，新遵父命，與門下士陳際新、張肱共續成之。

translations.literal: When Ming Antu fell critically ill, he passed his Quick Methods manuscript to him; Xin followed his father's command and, together with his disciples Chen Jixin and Zhang Gong, completed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming Antu lay near death, he entrusted his manuscript of the Quick Methods to Xin; obeying his father's charge, Xin together with his disciples Chen Jixin and Zhang Gong brought the work to completion.

sentences.zh: 陳際新，字舜五，宛平諸生。

translations.literal: Chen Jixin, courtesy name Shunwu, was a licentiate of Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jixin, styled Shunwu, was a licentiate of Wanping.

sentences.zh: 官靈臺郎，為監正。

translations.literal: He held office as Assistant Director of the Imperial Observatory and served as Director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Observatory and rose to Director.

sentences.zh: 續明安圖割圜密率捷法，尋緒推究，質以生前面授之言。

translations.literal: He continued Ming Antu's Quick Methods of Circle Division and Precise Ratios, tracing the thread and investigating, verifying against what his teacher had orally taught in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: He continued Ming Antu's Quick Methods of Circle Division and Precise Ratios, following its thread of reasoning and checking it against what his teacher had taught him in person.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆甲午，始克成書。

translations.literal: By the jiawu year of Qianlong, he finally completed the book.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year of the Qianlong reign, he at last finished the book.

sentences.zh: 劉湘煃，字允恭，江夏人。

translations.literal: Liu Xianghuang, courtesy name Yunong, was a native of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianghuang, styled Yunong, came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 聞梅文鼎以曆算名當世，鬻產走千餘裡，受業其門，湛思積悟，多所創獲。

translations.literal: Hearing that Mei Wending was renowned in his age for calendar and calculation, he sold his property and traveled more than a thousand li to study under him; deep thought accumulated into insight, and he made many original discoveries.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mei Wending was famed throughout the age for calendrical astronomy, he sold his estate and traveled more than a thousand li to become his pupil; long brooding ripened into insight, and he made many original discoveries.

sentences.zh: 文鼎得之甚喜，曰：『劉生好學精進，啟予不逮！』

translations.literal: Mei Wending was greatly pleased and said: 'Student Liu is diligent and advancing in his learning — he has opened my eyes where I fall short!'
translations.idiomatic: Mei Wending was delighted and declared: 'Student Liu is diligent and ever advancing — he has taught me what I lacked!'

sentences.zh: 其與人書曰：『金、水二星，歷指所說未徹，得劉生說，而後二星之有歲輪，其理確不可易。』

translations.literal: In a letter to someone he wrote: "The account of Mercury and Venus in the calendrical treatises is not thorough; only with Student Liu's explanation did the existence of annual revolutions for these two planets become a principle that cannot be overturned."
translations.idiomatic: In a letter he wrote: "The account of Mercury and Venus in the calendrical treatises remains incomplete; only after Liu's explanation did the annual revolutions of these two planets become a principle beyond dispute."

sentences.zh: 因以所著歷學疑問囑之討論，湘煃為著訂補三卷。

translations.literal: He therefore entrusted his Questions in Calendar Learning for discussion; Xianghuang wrote three juan of emendations and supplements.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore entrusted his Questions in Calendar Learning to him for discussion, and Xianghuang wrote three fascicles of emendations and supplements.

sentences.zh: 又謂曆法自漢、唐以來，五星最疏，故其遲、留、伏、逆皆入於佔，至元郭守敬出，而五星始有推步經度之法，而緯則猶未備。

translations.literal: He also held that since Han and Tang times, the five planets had been treated most roughly in calendrical methods, so their retrogradation, station, occultation, and opposition all fell to divination; only when Guo Shoujing of Yuan appeared did the five planets first receive methods for computing ecliptic longitude, yet latitude was still incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that since Han and Tang times the five planets had been treated most crudely in calendrical methods, so that their retrogradation, station, occultation, and opposition all devolved upon divination; only with Guo Shoujing in the Yuan did the five planets first receive methods for computing ecliptic longitude — yet latitude remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 西法舊亦未有緯度，至地谷而後有五星緯度，已在守敬後矣。

translations.literal: Western methods originally also lacked latitude; only after Tycho Brahe did five-planet latitude appear — already after Guo Shoujing.
translations.idiomatic: Western methods too originally lacked planetary latitude; only after Tycho Brahe did latitude for the five planets appear — and that was already after Guo Shoujing.

sentences.zh: 曆書有法原、法數，並為曆法統宗。

translations.literal: Calendrical books have Origins of Methods and Tabular Numbers, both serving as the comprehensive lineage of calendrical methods.
translations.idiomatic: Calendrical treatises distinguish Origins of Methods and Tabular Numbers, both forming the comprehensive foundation of calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 法原者，七政與交食之歷指也；

translations.literal: Origins of Methods are the calendrical treatises on the seven luminaries and eclipses;
translations.idiomatic: Origins of Methods are the calendrical treatises on the seven luminaries and eclipses;

sentences.zh: 法數者，七政與交食經緯之表也，故歷指實為造表之根本。

translations.literal: Tabular Numbers are the tables of longitude and latitude for the seven luminaries and eclipses; therefore the calendrical treatises are truly the root of composing tables.
translations.idiomatic: Tabular Numbers are the longitude and latitude tables for the seven luminaries and eclipses; the calendrical treatises are thus truly the root from which tables are composed.

sentences.zh: 今歷所載金、水，歷指如其法以造表，則與所步之表不合，如其表以推算測天，則又密合，是歷雖有表數，而猶未知立表之根也。

translations.literal: The Mercury and Venus entries in the present calendar — if tables are composed by the methods in the calendrical treatises, they do not agree with the computed tables; if the tables are used to calculate and observe the heavens, they fit precisely. Thus though the calendar has tabular numbers, it still does not know the root of establishing tables.
translations.idiomatic: For Mercury and Venus in the present calendar, tables composed by the methods in the calendrical treatises disagree with the computed tables — yet calculations from those tables match the heavens precisely. The calendar thus possesses tabular numbers without knowing the root from which the tables were established.

sentences.zh: 乃作五星法像五卷，文鼎深契其說，摘其要目為五星紀要。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote Five Fascicles on the Images of Five-Planet Methods; Mei Wending deeply agreed with his views and extracted the main points as Essentials of the Five Planets.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote Five Fascicles on the Images of Five-Planet Methods; Mei Wending deeply endorsed his views and extracted the main points under the title Essentials of the Five Planets.

sentences.zh: 湘煃又欲為渾蓋通憲天盤安星之用，以戊辰曆元加歲差，用弧三角法，作恆星經緯表根一卷，及月離交均表根、黃白距度表根各一卷，皆補新法所未及也。

translations.literal: Xianghuang also wished to serve the purpose of placing stars on the armillary-sphere and astrolabe celestial disks for the Comprehensive Ritual of the Armillary Sphere; taking the wuchen calendar epoch and adding precession, using spherical trigonometry, he wrote one juan each on the roots of the fixed-star longitude-latitude table, the lunar-solar eclipse mean table roots, and the solar-lunar separation table roots — all supplementing what the new methods had not yet covered.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghuang also sought to serve the placement of stars on the armillary-sphere and astrolabe disks of the Comprehensive Ritual of the Armillary Sphere; taking the wuchen calendar epoch and adding precession, he applied spherical trigonometry to write one fascicle each on the foundations of the fixed-star longitude-latitude table, the lunar mean-motion and eclipse table, and the solar-lunar separation table — all filling gaps left by the new methods.

sentences.zh: 所著又有論日、月食算稿各一卷，各省北極出地圖說一卷，答全椒吳荀淑曆算十問書一卷。

translations.literal: His writings also include one juan each of draft calculations on solar and lunar eclipses, one juan on maps of polar altitude by province, and one juan of replies to Wu Xunshu of Quanjiao's ten questions on calendar and calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He also left one fascicle each of draft calculations on solar and lunar eclipses, one fascicle on provincial maps of polar altitude, and one fascicle of replies to the ten questions on calendar and calculation posed by Wu Xunshu of Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 王文啟，字宋賢，號惺齋，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenqi, courtesy name Songxian, style name Xingzhai, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenqi, whose courtesy name was Songxian and style name Xingzhai, came from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 乾隆辛未進士，授將樂縣知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the xinwei year of Qianlong, he was appointed magistrate of Jiangle County.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the xinwei year of Qianlong, he was appointed magistrate of Jiangle County.

sentences.zh: 究心律曆句股之學，著書已刻者為惺齋雜著。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to the study of rhythm, calendar, and right-triangle mathematics; his published works appear in the Miscellaneous Writings of Xingzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to pitch-pipes, calendrical astronomy, and right-triangle mathematics; his published works appear in the Miscellaneous Writings of Xingzhai.

sentences.zh: 內有史記、漢書正譌兩種，其正史記之譌者，為律書、曆書、天官書各一卷；

translations.literal: These include two works correcting the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han — for correcting the Grand Historian, the Treatises on Pitchpipes, Calendar, and the Celestial Offices, one juan each;
translations.idiomatic: These include two works emending the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han — emending the Grand Historian's Treatises on Pitchpipes, Calendar, and the Celestial Offices, one fascicle each;

sentences.zh: 正漢書之譌者，為律曆志上下二卷。

translations.literal: for correcting the Book of Han, the Treatise on Pitchpipes and Calendar in two juan, upper and lower.
translations.idiomatic: and emending the Book of Han's Treatise on Pitchpipes and Calendar in two fascicles, upper and lower.

sentences.zh: 未刻者為曆法記疑、句股衍、角度衍、九章雜論。

translations.literal: Unpublished works include Notes on Doubts in Calendrical Methods, Development of Right Triangles, Development of Angles, and Miscellaneous Essays on the Nine Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Unpublished works include Notes on Doubts in Calendrical Methods, Development of Right Triangles, Development of Angles, and Miscellaneous Essays on the Nine Chapters.

sentences.zh: 而句股衍一書，因繁求簡，最為精晰。

translations.literal: Of these, Development of Right Triangles, seeking simplicity from complexity, is the most lucid.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, Development of Right Triangles — distilling simplicity from complexity — is the most lucid.

sentences.zh: 分甲、乙、丙三集，甲集術原三卷，乙集綱要二卷，丙集晰義四卷。

translations.literal: It is divided into three collections A, B, and C: Collection A, Origins of Methods, three juan; Collection B, Essentials, two juan; Collection C, Clarified Meanings, four juan.
translations.idiomatic: It is divided into three collections — A, B, and C: Collection A, Origins of Methods, three fascicles; Collection B, Essentials, two fascicles; Collection C, Clarified Meanings, four fascicles.

sentences.zh: 甲集首卷通論術原，為句股因積求邊張本。

translations.literal: The first juan of Collection A gives a general discussion of the origins of methods, setting forth the basis for deriving sides from areas in right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: The first fascicle of Collection A surveys the origins of methods, laying the groundwork for deriving sides from areas in right triangles.

sentences.zh: 二卷專論立方，因及平方法。

translations.literal: The second juan specializes in cube extraction, extending also to square extraction.
translations.idiomatic: The second fascicle treats cube extraction and extends to square extraction as well.

sentences.zh: 三卷專論和數開立方，所以盡立方諸數之變。

translations.literal: The third juan specializes in cube extraction by sum-number, thereby exhausting the variations of all cube numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The third fascicle treats cube extraction by sum-number, exhausting the variations of all cubic quantities.

sentences.zh: 乙集兩卷，為相求法百二十三則之綱要。

translations.literal: The two juan of Collection B are the essentials of one hundred twenty-three rules of mutual seeking.
translations.idiomatic: The two fascicles of Collection B summarize one hundred twenty-three rules of mutual solution.

sentences.zh: 丙集四卷，即相求法，逐則分晰其義，專取發明立法之意。

translations.literal: The four juan of Collection C are the mutual-seeking methods themselves, analyzing each rule in detail, devoted solely to elucidating the intent of establishing methods.
translations.idiomatic: The four fascicles of Collection C present the mutual-solution methods themselves, analyzing each rule in detail to elucidate the intent behind each method's formulation.

sentences.zh: 其總序曰：『句股弦相求法，參以和較，凡得七十八則，求句股中函數。

translations.literal: Its general preface says: 'Methods for mutual seeking among leg, base, and hypotenuse, incorporating sum and difference — seventy-eight rules in all, seeking quantities contained within the legs and base.
translations.idiomatic: Its general preface reads: 'Methods for mutual solution among leg, base, and hypotenuse, incorporating sum and difference — seventy-eight rules in all, seeking quantities contained within the triangle.

sentences.zh: 又有冪積求容員、容方、容縱方，及依弦作底求容方，與句股求外方、外員之數。

translations.literal: There are also area seeking inscribed circle, inscribed square, inscribed rectangle, and area seeking inscribed square with hypotenuse as base, together with numbers for seeking outer square and outer circle from legs and base.
translations.idiomatic: There are also methods for deriving inscribed circles, squares, and rectangles from area, for inscribing a square with the hypotenuse as base, and for outer squares and circles from the legs and base.

sentences.zh: 又有積數與句股和較相求​​容方，與句股餘數相求之法。

translations.literal: There are also methods for seeking inscribed square from area together with sum and difference of legs and base, and for seeking from remainder numbers of legs and base.
translations.idiomatic: There are also methods for inscribing a square from area together with the sum or difference of legs and base, and for solving from remainder quantities of legs and base.

sentences.zh: 綜而計之，凡得二十九則。

translations.literal: Taken together, twenty-nine rules in all.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether, twenty-nine rules.

sentences.zh: 立表測量，得求高、求遠、求深三則，重表亦然。

translations.literal: Erecting tables for measurement yields three rules for seeking height, distance, and depth; double tables likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying with erected tables yields three rules for height, distance, and depth; double tables add the same.

sentences.zh: 舊算書多簡略，詳者又苦錯出無緒。

translations.literal: Old computational books are mostly brief; detailed ones suffer from scattered presentation without order.
translations.idiomatic: Older computational books are mostly terse; detailed ones scatter their material without order.

sentences.zh: 間嘗力為區別，使各以類從，先定相求法百十三則。

translations.literal: I have occasionally labored to distinguish them so each follows its kind, first establishing one hundred thirteen rules of mutual seeking.
translations.idiomatic: I have labored to sort them by kind, first establishing one hundred thirteen rules of mutual solution.

sentences.zh: 甲申仲秋，复理前緒，逐一布算，捷於舊法，而舊法仍附見，以資參考。

translations.literal: In the mid-autumn of jiashen, I took up my earlier thread again, setting out calculations one by one — swifter than the old methods, while the old methods are still appended for reference.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-autumn of jiashen I resumed my earlier work, working through each calculation in turn — swifter than the old methods, though the old methods are still appended for reference.

sentences.zh: 至以中函積與弦之所和、所較相求而得句、股、弦之正數，舊法罕見，今亦竊擬一法，以附於後。

translations.literal: As for seeking the true numbers of leg, base, and hypotenuse from the contained area together with the sum or difference of the hypotenuse — rarely seen in old methods — I now venture to propose a method as well, appending it at the end.
translations.idiomatic: As for deriving the true leg, base, and hypotenuse from the contained area together with the sum or difference of the hypotenuse — a case rarely treated in old methods — I now venture to propose a method of my own, appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 又別創截弦分兩，及補句求股、補股求句之法，分為六則，使不成句股之形，亦化為句股。

translations.literal: I also separately created methods of dividing the hypotenuse in two sections, and supplementing the leg to seek the base or supplementing the base to seek the leg — six rules in all — so that shapes that are not right triangles may also be transformed into right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: I also devised methods of bisecting the hypotenuse and of supplementing the leg to find the base or the base to find the leg — six rules in all — so that figures that are not right triangles may be reduced to right triangles.

sentences.zh: 並載不成句股求中函積二則，容方、容員四則，外切員徑一則，員內累求句股六則，凡又一十九則。

translations.literal: Also included are two rules for seeking contained area from non-right triangles, four rules for inscribed square and circle, one rule for externally tangent circle diameter, six rules for successive right triangles within a circle — nineteen rules in all.
translations.idiomatic: Also included are two rules for contained area in non-right triangles, four for inscribed squares and circles, one for the diameter of an externally tangent circle, and six for successive right triangles within a circle — nineteen rules in all.

sentences.zh: 以該西術三角之算，兼備割員之用。

translations.literal: To cover Western trigonometry and also serve circle division.
translations.idiomatic: These cover Western trigonometry and serve circle division as well.

sentences.zh: 使學者知周髀一經，於術無所不該。

translations.literal: So that students may know that the Zhou Bi classic embraces every method without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Thus students may see that the Zhou Bi classic embraces every computational method without exception.

sentences.zh: 後人不能觸類旁通，以盡其變，故使西術得出而爭勝，其實西術亦出周髀，不能出折句為股之外也。』

translations.literal: Later men could not extend by analogy to exhaust its variations, and so Western methods were able to come forward and vie for supremacy — yet in truth Western methods also derive from the Zhou Bi and cannot go beyond folding the leg to make the base.'
translations.idiomatic: Later scholars could not extend it by analogy to exhaust its variations, and so Western methods came forward to vie for supremacy — yet Western methods too derive from the Zhou Bi and cannot go beyond folding the leg to form the base.'

sentences.zh: 又略例引言曰：『算家句股一門，為術最繁，非鑿指一數以為布算之準，難以虛領其義。

translations.literal: Again the brief-examples introduction says: 'Among computational specialists, the branch of right triangles has the most elaborate methods; unless one specifies numbers as the standard for setting out calculations, it is hard to grasp the meaning in the abstract.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the introduction to the brief examples reads: 'Among computational specialists, the branch of right triangles is the most elaborate; unless one fixes on concrete numbers as the standard for calculation, it is hard to grasp the meaning in the abstract.

sentences.zh: 然如廣三修四見於經者，特其正例，正例外變例尤多。

translations.literal: Yet cases like width three and height four seen in the classic are only the standard cases; apart from standard cases, variant cases are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like width three and height four in the classic are only standard examples; variant cases are far more numerous.

sentences.zh: 必欲正變兼呈，則一卷中彼此錯出，使閱者耳目數易，轉增煩憒。

translations.literal: If one insists on presenting both standard and variant cases together, then within one juan they contradict each other — making the reader's eyes and ears change repeatedly and increasing confusion.
translations.idiomatic: To present standard and variant cases together in one fascicle is to jumble them endlessly, wearying the reader and adding confusion.

sentences.zh: 茲特標舉略例，併不成句股之形亦附見焉，以盡句股之變，而該三角之法。』

translations.literal: Here I specially mark out brief examples, also appending shapes that are not right triangles, to exhaust the variations of right triangles while covering trigonometric methods.'
translations.idiomatic: Here I mark out brief examples only, also appending non-right-triangle cases, to exhaust the variations of right triangles while covering trigonometric methods.'

sentences.zh: 又答友問句股書曰：『欲求句股，先學開方，方有正方、縱方之異。

translations.literal: Again in Reply to a Friend's Questions on Right Triangles he writes: 'To seek right triangles, one must first learn root extraction; squares have the distinction of square and rectangle.
translations.idiomatic: Again, in Reply to a Friend's Questions on Right Triangles he writes: 'To work with right triangles, one must first learn root extraction; squares divide into true squares and rectangles.

sentences.zh: 縱方則以修廣之和、較數開之，其次則求四率比例，有三率求四率之法，有二率求三率之法，又有一率求三率之法。

translations.literal: For rectangles, extract using the sum and difference of length and width; next seek four-term proportion — there are methods for seeking the fourth term from three terms, for seeking three terms from two, and for seeking three terms from one.
translations.idiomatic: For rectangles, extract roots from the sum and difference of length and width; next apply four-term proportion — methods exist for finding the fourth term from three, three terms from two, and three terms from one.

sentences.zh: 知此即可以知求句、股、弦各無零數法。

translations.literal: Knowing this, one can know methods for seeking leg, base, and hypotenuse each without fractional remainders.
translations.idiomatic: Master this, and one can derive legs, base, and hypotenuse each without fractional remainders.

sentences.zh: 以三率之中率為主，倍中率為股，首末二率相減為句，相加為弦。

translations.literal: Taking the middle term of three as primary, double the middle term for the base, subtract the first and last terms for the leg, add them for the hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: Take the middle term of a three-term proportion as primary: double it for the base, subtract the outer terms for the leg, add them for the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 依此衍之，得句股略例十數則，然後以句、股、弦為正數，兩數相加為和，相減為較。

translations.literal: Extending this, one obtains a dozen or so brief rules for right triangles; then take leg, base, and hypotenuse as true numbers — two numbers added form the sum, subtracted form the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Extending this yields a dozen or so brief rules for right triangles; then treat leg, base, and hypotenuse as true numbers — their sum and difference follow from addition and subtraction.

sentences.zh: 又有句股三數相加減之和較數，弦與和，和弦與較和三數相加之和數也；

translations.literal: There are also sum-difference numbers of the three right-triangle numbers added and subtracted; sum of hypotenuse and sum, and sum of hypotenuse and difference — three numbers added form the aggregate sum;
translations.idiomatic: There are also composite sum-difference quantities formed by adding and subtracting the three right-triangle numbers; the sum of hypotenuse and sum, and the sum of hypotenuse and difference — three quantities whose sum forms the aggregate total;

sentences.zh: 弦與較，較弦與和較三數相減之較數也。

translations.literal: Hypotenuse and difference, and difference of hypotenuse and sum and difference — these are difference numbers formed by subtracting among three numbers.
translations.idiomatic: There are the hypotenuse and the difference, and the difference between the hypotenuse and the sum and difference — difference quantities obtained by subtracting among three numbers.

sentences.zh: 三數相加減，今名之為兼三和較。

translations.literal: The three numbers added and subtracted together are now named the composite triple sum-difference.
translations.idiomatic: When the three numbers are combined by addition and subtraction, the result is now called the composite triple sum-difference.

sentences.zh: 凡正數和較之數各三，兼三和較各二，共十三數。

translations.literal: In all, true numbers and sum-difference numbers are three each, composite triple sum-differences two each — thirteen numbers in total.
translations.idiomatic: There are three true numbers and three sum-difference numbers, two composite triple sum-differences — thirteen quantities in all.

sentences.zh: 十三數中，隨舉兩數，即可求句股弦全數。

translations.literal: Among the thirteen numbers, take any two at random and one can find the complete leg, base, and hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: From any two of the thirteen quantities, one can determine the full leg, base, and hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 凡得相求法九十四則，而容方、容員、截股分兩、立表測量單表、重表之法，猶不與焉。

translations.literal: In all one obtains ninety-four mutual-seeking rules; yet methods for inscribed squares, inscribed circles, cutting the base into two parts, and gnomon measurement with single or double staffs are still not included.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety-four mutual-seeking rules are obtained in all, yet methods for inscribed squares and circles, cutting the base into two parts, and single- or double-staff gnomon measurement are still left out.

sentences.zh: 其次則求截弦分兩之法，是為一句股分兩句股，即可以知不成句股亦可以分兩句股。

translations.literal: Next are methods for cutting the hypotenuse into two parts — this is one right triangle divided into two right triangles; from this one can know that non-right triangles can also be divided into two right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: Next come methods for cutting the hypotenuse into two parts — one right triangle split into two — from which one sees that even non-right triangles can be divided the same way.

sentences.zh: 不成句股分兩句股，即西法三角算之所由名，今則總以句股概之。

translations.literal: Dividing a non-right triangle into two right triangles is precisely what Western trigonometry is named from; now all are subsumed under right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting a non-right triangle into two right triangles is the very origin of Western trigonometry's name; here all such cases are treated under the right-triangle framework.

sentences.zh: 其法取大小兩句股形，小股與大句同數者合為一形，即為不成句股之形。

translations.literal: The method takes two right triangles, large and small; when the small base equals the large leg they are combined into one shape — this is the non-right-triangle shape.
translations.idiomatic: The method takes two right triangles, one large and one small; when the small base equals the large leg and they are joined, the result is a non-right triangle.

sentences.zh: 分之為兩，則所謂中垂線者，即小矩之股，大矩之句。

translations.literal: When divided into two, what is called the median perpendicular is the base of the small rectangle and the leg of the large rectangle.
translations.idiomatic: Split it in two, and the so-called median perpendicular is the base of the smaller rectangle and the leg of the larger one.

sentences.zh: 以此衍之，又得不成句股略例二十餘則。

translations.literal: Extending from this, one further obtains twenty-odd brief rules for non-right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: Extending the method yields twenty-odd brief rules for non-right triangles.

sentences.zh: 依類推之，又得合形分兩、削形求全二法。

translations.literal: Following the categories in extension, one further obtains two methods: composite-shape division and truncated-shape completion.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing the categories further, one obtains two more methods: composite-shape division and truncated-shape completion.

sentences.zh: 合形分兩，則有正合形截偶分兩、反合形截中分兩、偏合形截邊分兩之法。

translations.literal: For composite-shape division there are methods of straight composite cutting at the even division, reverse composite cutting at the center, and oblique composite cutting at the edge.
translations.idiomatic: Composite-shape division includes straight composite cutting at the even point, reverse composite cutting at the center, and oblique composite cutting at the edge.

sentences.zh: 削形求全，則有削去正矩、偏矩之殊，偏矩中又有淺削、深削之分。

translations.literal: For truncated-shape completion there are distinctions between cutting away the true rectangle and the oblique rectangle; within oblique rectangles there is further the distinction of shallow cut and deep cut.
translations.idiomatic: Truncated-shape completion distinguishes cutting away the true rectangle from the oblique rectangle; among oblique rectangles there are further shallow and deep cuts.

sentences.zh: 知此則句股之學盡矣。』

translations.literal: Know this and the study of right triangles is complete.'
translations.idiomatic: Master this, and the study of right triangles is complete.'

sentences.zh: 元啟嘗曰：『我無他長，惟好學深思，心知其意而已。』

translations.literal: Yuan Qi once said: 'I have no other special talent — only that I love learning and think deeply until I know the meaning in my heart.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qi once said: 'I have no other gift — only that I love learning and think deeply until I grasp the meaning in my heart.'

sentences.zh: 然其句股術一書，幾欲駕梅文鼎而上之，為算術中不可少之書云。

translations.literal: Yet his book Right-Triangle Methods nearly surpasses Mei Wending — a work indispensable in computational mathematics.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet his Right-Triangle Methods nearly surpasses Mei Wending — a work indispensable in the mathematical arts.

sentences.zh: 朱鴻，字云陸，秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Hong, courtesy name Yunlu, was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hong, whose courtesy name was Yunlu, came from Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，改翰林院庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after finishing his term was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his term was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，歷給事中，出官督理湖南糧儲道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor, served as supervising secretary, and left office to supervise the Hunan grain and storage circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor, served as supervising secretary, and then left the capital to supervise the Hunan grain and storage circuit.

sentences.zh: 研精算學。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to mastery of computational mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the mastery of computational mathematics.

sentences.zh: 同郡錢儀吉譔三國會要，集乾象、景初二術成，嘗為作注。

translations.literal: Qian Yiji of the same prefecture compiled Essentials of the Three Kingdoms, gathering the Ganxiang and Jingchu calendar systems into one work; Zhu once annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yiji of the same prefecture compiled Essentials of the Three Kingdoms, assembling the Ganxiang and Jingchu calendar systems into one work, and Zhu once annotated it.

sentences.zh: 烏程陳杰時為台官博士，陽湖董祐誠亦客京邸，皆日從講數，各出所得相質問。

translations.literal: Chen Jie of Wucheng was then doctor of the Directorate, and Dong Youcheng of Yanghu also lodged in the capital — all studied computation together daily, each presenting findings for mutual examination.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jie of Wucheng was then doctor of the Directorate, and Dong Youcheng of Yanghu also lodged in the capital; they studied computation together daily, each presenting his findings for mutual critique.

sentences.zh: 舊無橢圓求週術，為祐誠言，圜柱斜剖，則成橢員，可以句股形求之。

translations.literal: There had been no method for finding the circumference of an ellipse; he told Youcheng that when a cylinder is cut obliquely it forms an ellipse, which can be found through right triangles.
translations.idiomatic: No method yet existed for finding the circumference of an ellipse; he told Youcheng that a cylinder cut obliquely forms an ellipse, which can be determined by right triangles.

sentences.zh: 祐誠既發明其說，係以圖釋。

translations.literal: Youcheng developed the theory and illustrated it with diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: Youcheng worked out the theory and illustrated it with diagrams.

sentences.zh: 初得杜德美割圜九術寫本，以示祐誠，創圖解三卷。

translations.literal: First obtaining a manuscript copy of Du Demei's Nine Methods for Circle Division, he showed it to Youcheng and created three juan of illustrated explanations.
translations.idiomatic: When he first obtained a manuscript of Du Demei's Nine Methods for Circle Division, he showed it to Youcheng and produced three juan of illustrated explanations.

sentences.zh: 既成，復得密率捷法於李潢家，則蒙古監正明安圖師弟續繹之書也，與傳寫本互異。

translations.literal: When finished, he further obtained Quick Methods for Precise Ratio at Li Huang's house — a work continued by Mingantu and his disciples, the Mongolian director — which differed from circulated copies.
translations.idiomatic: After it was finished, he obtained Quick Methods for Precise Ratio at Li Huang's home — a work continued by the Mongolian director Mingantu and his disciples — which differed from circulated copies.

sentences.zh: 鴻曾依杜法步算，徑一者，週三一四一五九二六五三五八九七九三二三八四六二六四三一八六三六七四七二二七九五一四，週十者，徑三一八三零九八八六一八三七九零六七一五三七七六七五四六六九六三八九零五六六六一。

translations.literal: Hong once calculated step by step according to Du's method: for diameter one, circumference 3.1415926535897932384626433186; for circumference ten, diameter 3.18309886183790671537766546696389056661.
translations.idiomatic: Hong once worked through Du's method step by step: for a diameter of one, the circumference is 3.1415926535897932384626433186; for a circumference of ten, the diameter is 3.18309886183790671537766546696389056661.

sentences.zh: 徐有玉採入務民義齋算學中。

translations.literal: Xu Youyu included it in Wumin Yizhai's mathematical works.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youyu included it in the mathematical collection of Wumin Yizhai.

sentences.zh: 道光十年後，辭官仍居京師，譔考工記車製參解。

translations.literal: After the tenth year of Daoguang he resigned office but remained in the capital, compiling a commentary on chariot construction in the Kaogongji.
translations.idiomatic: After the tenth year of Daoguang he resigned from office but remained in the capital, compiling a commentary on chariot construction in the Kaogongji.

sentences.zh: 又評程氏易疇考工創物小記，多所糾正云。

translations.literal: He also reviewed Cheng Yichou's Brief Notes on Creating Things in the Kaogongji, correcting many points.
translations.idiomatic: He also reviewed Cheng Yichou's Brief Notes on Creating Things in the Kaogongji and corrected many points.

sentences.zh: 博啟，字繪亭，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Bo Qi, courtesy name Huiting, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Qi, whose courtesy name was Huiting, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，官欽天監監副。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he served as vice-director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he served as vice-director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 嘗因句股和較之術，前人論之極詳，獨句股形中所容之方邊、員徑、垂線三事，尚缺而未備。

translations.literal: Because of right-triangle sum-difference methods — though predecessors discussed them exhaustively — three matters within inscribed right triangles, square side, circle diameter, and altitude, remained incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Working from right-triangle sum-difference methods — though predecessors had treated them exhaustively — he found three matters still missing within inscribed right triangles: the square side, the circle diameter, and the altitude.

sentences.zh: 爰以三事分配和較，創法六十。

translations.literal: Accordingly he distributed the three matters among sum-differences and created sixty methods.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed the three matters among sum-differences and devised sixty methods.

sentences.zh: 惜其書未刊，法不傳。

translations.literal: Regrettably his book was never published and the methods were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Regrettably his book was never published, and the methods were lost.

sentences.zh: 今所傳者，惟有方邊及垂線求句、股、弦一題。

translations.literal: What survives today is only one problem seeking leg, base, and hypotenuse from square side and altitude.
translations.idiomatic: What survives today is only a single problem seeking the leg, base, and hypotenuse from the square side and the altitude.

sentences.zh: 法用平行線剖容方冪為四小句股形，借垂線為小句股和，借方邊為小弦，求小句小股。

translations.literal: The method uses parallel lines to divide the inscribed-square power into four small right triangles; borrowing the altitude as the small sum of leg and base, and the square side as the small hypotenuse, one finds the small leg and base.
translations.idiomatic: The method uses parallel lines to divide the inscribed-square area into four small right triangles; taking the altitude as the small sum of leg and base and the square side as the small hypotenuse, one finds the small leg and base.

sentences.zh: 以小股與垂線比，若方邊與句比；

translations.literal: As the small base is to the altitude, so the square side is to the leg;
translations.idiomatic: As the small base is to the altitude, so the square side is to the leg;

sentences.zh: 以小句與垂線比，若方邊與弦比。

translations.literal: As the small leg is to the altitude, so the square side is to the hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: As the small leg is to the altitude, so the square side is to the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 道光初，方履亨官監正，每舉此題課士。

translations.literal: Early in Daoguang, Fang Lüheng as director tested students with this problem annually.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daoguang era, when Fang Lüheng served as director, he set this problem for students every year.

sentences.zh: 其後得甘泉羅士琳力為表章，博術乃復明於世。

translations.literal: Later Luo Shilin of Ganquan championed it vigorously, and Bo's methods were restored to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Later Luo Shilin of Ganquan championed the methods vigorously, and Bo's techniques were restored to the world.

sentences.zh: 羅論云：『曩者聞方慎菴監正言繪亭監副有是法，失傳。

translations.literal: Luo wrote: 'Formerly I heard Director Fang Shen'an say that Vice-Director Huiting had these methods, but they were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Luo wrote: 'Long ago I heard Director Fang Shen'an say that Vice-Director Huiting had these methods, but they had been lost.

sentences.zh: 因仿監副遺法，用平行線剖半員冪為四小句股形，以半圓徑減垂線餘，借為小句股和，借半員為小弦，求得小句、小股。

translations.literal: Imitating the vice-director's surviving method, use parallel lines to divide the semicircle power into four small right triangles; subtract the altitude from the semicircle radius for the remainder, borrow it as the small sum of leg and base, borrow the semicircle as the small hypotenuse, and find the small leg and base.
translations.idiomatic: Following the vice-director's surviving method, I use parallel lines to divide the semicircle area into four small right triangles; subtract the altitude from the semicircle radius and take the remainder as the small sum of leg and base, the semicircle as the small hypotenuse, and thus find the small leg and base.

sentences.zh: 以小股比垂線，若半員徑比股；

translations.literal: As the small base is to the altitude, so the semicircle radius is to the base;
translations.idiomatic: As the small base is to the altitude, so the semicircle radius is to the base;

sentences.zh: 以小股比股，若半員徑比弦。

translations.literal: As the small base is to the base, so the semicircle radius is to the hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: As the small base is to the base, so the semicircle radius is to the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 又以半員徑減方邊，得較。

translations.literal: Further subtract the square side from the semicircle radius to obtain the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the square side from the semicircle radius to obtain the difference.

sentences.zh: 用平行線剖較冪為四小句股形，借半員徑為小句股和，借較為小弦，求得小句、小股。

translations.literal: Use parallel lines to divide the difference power into four small right triangles; borrow the semicircle radius as the small sum of leg and base, borrow the difference as the small hypotenuse, and find the small leg and base.
translations.idiomatic: Use parallel lines to divide the difference area into four small right triangles; take the semicircle radius as the small sum of leg and base and the difference as the small hypotenuse, and find the small leg and base.

sentences.zh: 以小股比半員徑，若方邊比句；

translations.literal: As the small base is to the semicircle radius, so the square side is to the leg;
translations.idiomatic: As the small base is to the semicircle radius, so the square side is to the leg;

sentences.zh: 以小句比半員徑，若方邊比股，以小股比股，若較比弦。

translations.literal: As the small leg is to the semicircle radius, so the square side is to the base; as the small base is to the base, so the difference is to the hypotenuse.
translations.idiomatic: As the small leg is to the semicircle radius, so the square side is to the base; as the small base is to the base, so the difference is to the hypotenuse.

sentences.zh: 用補副監之遺。

translations.literal: Thus to supplement what the vice-director left incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: In this way I supplement what the vice-director left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 復用天元術演得三事和較六十題，更立天、地兩元為廣例二十五術，撰句股容三事拾遺四卷。

translations.literal: Further using the tianyuan method he derived sixty problems on the three matters' sum-differences, established heaven and earth as two unknowns for twenty-five extended methods, and compiled four juan titled Right-Triangle Inscribed Three Matters: Recovered Fragments.
translations.idiomatic: He further used the tianyuan method to derive sixty problems on the sum-differences of the three matters, set up heaven and earth as two unknowns for twenty-five extended methods, and compiled four juan titled Right-Triangle Inscribed Three Matters: Recovered Fragments.

sentences.zh: 更試變通其術，禦以八線，取方邊用方斜率，得容方中之斜線。

translations.literal: Further attempting to adapt the method, he applied the eight lines — taking the square side by the square oblique ratio to obtain the oblique line within the inscribed square.
translations.idiomatic: He also tried adapting the method through the eight lines, applying the square oblique ratio to the square side to obtain the oblique line within the inscribed square.

sentences.zh: 以垂線為一率，半徑為二率，斜線為三率，求得四率為正割。

translations.literal: Taking the altitude as the first ratio, the radius as the second, the oblique line as the third, the fourth ratio obtained is the secant.
translations.idiomatic: With the altitude as the first ratio, the radius as the second, and the oblique line as the third, the fourth ratio obtained is the secant.

sentences.zh: 檢八線表得度用，與四十五度相加減，得垂線所分之大小兩弧，副以半徑為一率，垂線為二率，小弧正割為三率，求得四率為句。

translations.literal: Consult the eight-line table for the degree value; add and subtract with forty-five degrees to obtain the two arcs, large and small, into which the altitude divides; then with radius as first ratio, altitude as second, small-arc secant as third, the fourth ratio obtained is the leg.
translations.idiomatic: Look up the degree value in the eight-line table; add and subtract it with forty-five degrees to obtain the large and small arcs into which the altitude divides the figure; then with radius as first ratio, altitude as second, and small-arc secant as third, the fourth ratio obtained is the leg.

sentences.zh: 如以大弧正割為三率，求得四率為股，又如以大小兩弧之兩正切為三率，求得四率，為大小兩弧之兩分弦，相併得弦餘。

translations.literal: If instead the large-arc secant is the third ratio, the fourth ratio obtained is the base; or if the two tangents of the large and small arcs are the third ratio, the fourth ratios obtained are the two partial chords of the two arcs — added together they give the chord complement.
translations.idiomatic: If the large-arc secant is taken as the third ratio, the fourth ratio obtained is the base; or if the tangents of the large and small arcs are taken as the third ratio, the fourth ratios obtained are the partial chords of the two arcs — added together they give the chord complement.

sentences.zh: 二題倣此，其得數同，而尾數有奇零。

translations.literal: The other two problems follow this pattern; the results agree numerically, but fractional remainders appear at the end.
translations.idiomatic: The other two problems follow the same pattern; the results agree, but odd fractional remainders appear at the end.

sentences.zh: 以八線表所列之數至單位止，單位以下，棄其餘分，故不能如句股與天元所得之密合。

translations.literal: Because the eight-line table lists numbers only to the unit place, discarding fractions below — hence it cannot match the exact agreement obtained by right triangles and tianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because the eight-line table gives numbers only to the unit place and discards everything below, it cannot match the exact agreement obtained by right triangles and the tianyuan method.

sentences.zh: 或有妄詆天元術不能馭三角和較者，抑知天元創於宋、明之間，安能逆知西法之有三角而豫為立法？

translations.literal: Some rashly denigrate the tianyuan method as unable to handle triangular sum-differences — yet do they not know that tianyuan was created between Song and Ming? How could it anticipate Western trigonometry and legislate in advance?
translations.idiomatic: Some rashly denounce the tianyuan method as unable to handle triangular sum-differences — yet tianyuan arose between the Song and Ming; how could it have foreseen Western trigonometry and legislated for it in advance?

sentences.zh: 要在學者善為會通耳。

translations.literal: What matters is that scholars skillfully integrate the two.
translations.idiomatic: What matters is that scholars know how to integrate the two traditions skillfully.

sentences.zh: 試設平三角形，有一角而角在兩邊之中，有大邊與對邊和，有小邊與對邊和，求三道及垂線，此西人常法所不能御者。

translations.literal: Suppose a plane triangle with one angle between two sides, given the sum of a large side and its opposite, and the sum of a small side and its opposite — seek the three sides and the altitude; this Western routine methods cannot handle.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a plane triangle with one angle between two sides, given the sum of a large side and its opposite and the sum of a small side and its opposite — to find the three sides and the altitude; ordinary Western methods cannot handle this.

sentences.zh: 若立天元一術，則任求何邊或和數或較數，皆一平方即得。

translations.literal: If one sets up a single tianyuan method, then whichever side, sum, or difference one seeks — all are obtained by a single quadratic.
translations.idiomatic: Set up a single tianyuan method, and whichever side, sum, or difference one seeks is obtained at once by one quadratic equation.

sentences.zh: 然則天元之與西法，其優劣可見矣。』

translations.literal: Thus the superiority of tianyuan over Western methods is evident.'
translations.idiomatic: From this the relative strengths of tianyuan and Western methods are plain.'

sentences.zh: 許如蘭，字芳谷，全椒人。

translations.literal: Xu Rulan, courtesy name Fanggu, was a native of Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rulan, whose courtesy name was Fanggu, came from Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十年舉人，大挑知縣，分發福建。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination, was selected as magistrate in the grand assignment, and was posted to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong he passed the provincial examination, was selected as a magistrate in the grand assignment, and was posted to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 因親老改江西，歷任浮梁、新建等縣事。

translations.literal: Because his parents were elderly he was transferred to Jiangxi and served successively in Fuliang, Xinjian, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Because his parents were elderly he was transferred to Jiangxi, where he served successively in Fuliang, Xinjian, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 丁憂服闋，赴福建，題補侯官，未履任，會瘴氣發，病卒。

translations.literal: After mourning and completing the mourning period, he went to Fujian and was appointed to Houguan, but before taking office miasma broke out and he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his parents, he went to Fujian and was appointed to Houguan, but before he could take office a miasma outbreak struck and he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 如蘭性敏，所讀書皆究心精妙，於曆算始習西法，通薛鳳祚所譯天步真原、天學會通。

translations.literal: Rulan was quick by nature; every book he read he pursued to its finest subtleties. In calendrical astronomy he first studied Western methods and mastered Xue Fengzuo's translations True Principles of Celestial Steps and Comprehensive Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Rulan was quick by nature and pursued every book he read to its finest subtleties. In calendrical astronomy he first studied Western methods and mastered Xue Fengzuo's translations True Principles of Celestial Steps and Comprehensive Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 時同縣山西寧武同知吳烺受梅文鼎學於劉湘煃，如蘭因並習梅氏曆算。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Liang of the same county, vice-prefect of Ningwu in Shanxi, received Mei Wending's learning from Liu Xiangkui; Rulan therefore also studied Mei's calendrical astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Liang of the same county, vice-prefect of Ningwu in Shanxi, had studied Mei Wending's learning under Liu Xiangkui, and Rulan therefore studied Mei's calendrical astronomy as well.

sentences.zh: 又於乾隆四十年夏，謁戴震於京都，受句股割圜記。

translations.literal: Again in the summer of the fortieth year of Qianlong he visited Dai Zhen in the capital and received his Record of Right Triangles and Circle Division.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fortieth year of Qianlong he visited Dai Zhen in the capital and received his Record of Right Triangles and Circle Division.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，謁董化星于常州。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he visited Dong Huaxing in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year he visited Dong Huaxing in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 戴傳緝古算經十書，而董則專業薛氏者也。

translations.literal: Dai transmitted the ten books of the Collected Ancient Mathematical Classics, while Dong specialized in the Xue school.
translations.idiomatic: Dai transmitted the ten books of the Collected Ancient Mathematical Classics, while Dong specialized in the Xue school.

sentences.zh: 由是兼通中、西之學。

translations.literal: From this he mastered both Chinese and Western learning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he mastered both Chinese and Western learning.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂其弟子胡早春曰：『古人以句股方程列於小學，童而習之，人人能曉，今則老宿不能通其義。

translations.literal: He once told his disciple Hu Zaochun: 'The ancients placed right triangles and equations in elementary studies; children learned them and everyone could understand — now even old masters cannot grasp their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He once told his disciple Hu Zaochun: 'The ancients placed right triangles and equations in elementary studies; children learned them and everyone understood — now even venerable scholars cannot grasp their meaning.

sentences.zh: 一則時尚帖括，視句股為不急之務；

translations.literal: First, the fashion for examination essays makes right triangles seem unurgent;
translations.idiomatic: First, the fashion for examination essays makes right triangles seem unimportant;

sentences.zh: 再則習為風雅，不屑持籌握算，效疇人子弟所為。

translations.literal: Second, cultivating literary elegance, they disdain holding counting rods and doing calculation, imitating what astronomers' sons do.
translations.idiomatic: Second, people cultivate literary elegance and disdain holding counting rods and doing calculation, as astronomers' sons are expected to do.

sentences.zh: 噫，過矣！』

translations.literal: Alas, this is excessive!'
translations.idiomatic: Alas, this goes too far!'

sentences.zh: 又謂：『士大夫不精弧矢之術，雖識天文，無益也。

translations.literal: He also said: 'If scholar-officials do not master arc-and-arrow methods, though they know astronomy, it is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'If scholar-officials do not master arc-and-arrow methods, knowing astronomy does them no good.

sentences.zh: 疇人算工不明像數之理，雖能步算，無益也。』

translations.literal: If astronomers and calculators do not understand the principles of image and number, though they can compute step by step, it is of no use.'
translations.idiomatic: If astronomers and calculators do not understand the principles of image and number, being able to compute step by step does them no good.'

sentences.zh: 著有乾象拾遺、春暉樓集諸書，今多散佚。

translations.literal: He authored such works as Recovered Fragments of the Ganxiang Calendar and the Chunhui Lou Collection; most are now scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: He authored works including Recovered Fragments of the Ganxiang Calendar and the Chunhui Lou Collection; most are now scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 其存者，有書梅氏月建非專言斗柄論後，略曰：『天氣渾淪，無可識認，古人不得已，即以恆星為天以識日躔。

translations.literal: Among what survives is a postscript to Mei's essay that monthly establishment does not speak exclusively of the Dipper handle, which briefly says: 'Heavenly qi is undifferentiated chaos, with nothing by which to recognize it; the ancients, having no alternative, took the fixed stars as heaven to mark the sun's motion.
translations.idiomatic: Among what survives is a postscript to Mei's essay that monthly establishment does not speak exclusively of the Dipper handle, which reads in part: 'Heavenly qi is undifferentiated chaos, with nothing by which to recognize it; the ancients, having no alternative, took the fixed stars as heaven to mark the sun's motion.

sentences.zh: 恆星積久而差，冬至日躔不在原宿，始立歲差之法。

translations.literal: Fixed stars over long accumulation drift; at winter solstice the sun's motion is no longer in its original lodge — hence the method of precession was established.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed stars drift over long ages; at winter solstice the sun no longer stands in its original lodge, and so the method of precession was established.

sentences.zh: 古謂恆星不動，而黃道西移。

translations.literal: The ancients said fixed stars do not move while the ecliptic shifts westward.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients held that fixed stars do not move while the ecliptic shifts westward.

sentences.zh: 今測普天星座皆動，其經緯之度，不隨赤道運轉，而順黃道東移。

translations.literal: Now measurement shows all constellations throughout heaven move; their degrees of longitude and latitude do not rotate with the equator but shift eastward along the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Modern measurement shows that all constellations move; their longitudes and latitudes do not rotate with the equator but shift eastward along the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 故謂黃道不動，而恆星東行，與七政同一法。』

translations.literal: Hence one says the ecliptic does not move while fixed stars move eastward — the same principle as the seven luminaries.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence one holds that the ecliptic is fixed while fixed stars move eastward — the same principle applied to the seven luminaries.'

sentences.zh: 又謂：『古人以中數為歲，朔數為年。

translations.literal: He also said: 'The ancients took the median count as the year and the new-moon count as the annual cycle.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'The ancients took the median count as the year and the new-moon count as the annual cycle.

sentences.zh: 上古氣朔同日，故月建起於節氣，而不起於中氣；

translations.literal: In high antiquity qi and new moon fell on the same day, so monthly establishment began from solar terms and not from median qi;
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity solar terms and new moons fell on the same day, so monthly establishment began from solar terms rather than median qi;

sentences.zh: 日躔過宮，起於中氣，而不起於節氣。

translations.literal: The sun's passage through lodges began from median qi and not from solar terms.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's passage through lodges began from median qi rather than solar terms.

sentences.zh: 起於節氣，故曰冬至子之半；

translations.literal: Beginning from solar terms, hence it is said 'winter solstice at the midpoint of zi';
translations.idiomatic: Because it began from solar terms, one says 'winter solstice at the midpoint of zi';

sentences.zh: 起於中氣，故曰冬至日躔星紀之次也。

translations.literal: Beginning from median qi, hence it is said 'at winter solstice the sun's motion is in the lodge Xingji.'
translations.idiomatic: Because it began from median qi, one says 'at winter solstice the sun stands in the lodge Xingji.'

sentences.zh: 然則一歲十二建，乃天道經歷十二辰，故謂之月建，此萬古不易者也。

translations.literal: Thus the twelve establishments of one year are heaven's way passing through the twelve branches — hence called monthly establishment; this is what never changes through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the twelve monthly establishments of a year mark heaven's passage through the twelve branches — hence the term monthly establishment; this is what never changes through the ages.

sentences.zh: 斗柄所指分位不真，且恆星東移，積久有差，辨之誠是也。

translations.literal: The position indicated by the Dipper handle is not exact, and fixed stars shift eastward — over long accumulation there is drift; to distinguish this is indeed correct.
translations.idiomatic: The position indicated by the Dipper handle is inexact, and fixed stars shift eastward — over long ages drift accumulates; to distinguish this is indeed correct.

sentences.zh: 但古人云：「斗為帝車，斟酌元氣而布之四方」。

translations.literal: But the ancients said: 'The Dipper is the emperor's chariot, measuring out primordial qi and distributing it to the four directions.'
translations.idiomatic: But the ancients said: 'The Dipper is the emperor's chariot, measuring out primordial qi and distributing it to the four directions.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「招搖柬指。」

translations.literal: They also said: 'The Dipper indicator points east.'
translations.idiomatic: They also said: 'The Dipper indicator points east.'

sentences.zh: 不過言天道無跡。

translations.literal: — this merely means the Way of Heaven leaves no trace.
translations.idiomatic: — this merely means the Way of Heaven leaves no visible trace.

sentences.zh: 可見順時布化，斗柄有像可徵耳。

translations.literal: One can see that in distributing transformation according to the seasons, the Dipper handle provides an image that can serve as evidence.
translations.idiomatic: One can see that in distributing seasonal transformation, the Dipper handle provides a visible sign.

sentences.zh: 拘泥其詞，則惑矣。』

translations.literal: Cling rigidly to the words and one is misled.'
translations.idiomatic: Cling rigidly to the words and one is led astray.'

sentences.zh: 其歲差說略曰：『恆星一年東行五十餘秒，又黃、赤二道斜交，並非平行，於左旋至速之中，微斜牽向右。

translations.literal: His brief account of precession says: 'Fixed stars move eastward more than fifty seconds a year; further, the yellow and red paths cross obliquely and are not parallel — amid the swiftest leftward rotation, they are slightly pulled obliquely to the right.
translations.idiomatic: His brief account of precession reads: 'Fixed stars move eastward more than fifty seconds a year; moreover, the ecliptic and equator cross obliquely and are not parallel — amid the swiftest leftward rotation, they are slightly pulled obliquely to the right.

sentences.zh: 日之於天，猶經緯之於日也。

translations.literal: The sun with respect to heaven is like longitude and latitude with respect to the sun.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's relation to heaven is like longitude and latitude in relation to the sun.

sentences.zh: 日行至黃道分至節氣之限，則春秋寒暑皆隨之而應。

translations.literal: When the sun's motion reaches the limits of equinoxes, solstices, and solar terms on the ecliptic, spring and autumn, cold and heat all respond accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun reaches the equinoxes, solstices, and solar terms on the ecliptic, spring and autumn, cold and heat all respond in turn.

sentences.zh: 七政躔於各宮，遇各宮燥濕寒溫風雨，則隨恆星之性而應。

translations.literal: The seven luminaries traverse the various palaces; encountering the dryness, moisture, cold, warmth, wind, and rain of each palace, they respond according to the nature of the fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: As the seven luminaries pass through the zodiacal palaces, they respond to each palace's climate—dry or damp, cold or warm, windy or rainy—according to the character of the fixed stars there.

sentences.zh: 然則冬、夏二至，乃黃道上子、午之位也。

translations.literal: Thus the winter and summer solstices are the positions of zi and wu on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The winter and summer solstices therefore mark the zi and wu positions on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 春、秋二分，乃黃道上卯、酉之位也。

translations.literal: The spring and autumn equinoxes are the positions of mao and you on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: The spring and autumn equinoxes mark the mao and you positions on the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 惟唐、虞時冬至日躔虛中，恆星之子中，正逢黃道之子中。

translations.literal: Only in the Tang and Yu eras did the winter solstice solar position reach the middle of Emptiness among the fixed stars, and the middle of zi among the fixed stars exactly coincided with the middle of zi on the ecliptic.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the era of Yao and Shun did the winter solstice sun stand at the middle of the Emptiness lodge, with the fixed stars' zi midpoint coinciding exactly with the ecliptic's zi midpoint.

sentences.zh: 嗣是漸差，而東周在女，漢在斗，今在箕。

translations.literal: Thereafter it gradually shifted: in the Eastern Zhou it was in Maid, in the Han in Dipper, and today in Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: Since then it has drifted steadily—in the Eastern Zhou to Maid, in the Han to Dipper, and today to Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 黃道之子，非恆星之子也。

translations.literal: The zi of the ecliptic is not the zi of the fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic's zi point is not the fixed stars' zi point.

sentences.zh: 以丑宮初度為冬至者，因周時冬至恆星已差至丑，周人即以恆星為黃道之十二次，故命丑為星紀，言諸星以此紀也。

translations.literal: Those who take the first degree of the chou palace as winter solstice do so because in Zhou times the winter solstice among fixed stars had shifted to chou; the Zhou people then took the fixed stars as the twelve stations of the ecliptic, hence naming chou Star Chronicle, meaning the stars are chronicled thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the first degree of the chou palace as winter solstice reflects the Zhou era, when the solstice among fixed stars had drifted to chou; the Zhou identified the fixed-star lodges with the ecliptic's twelve stations, naming chou Star Chronicle—the register by which all stars were reckoned.

sentences.zh: 其實丑乃周時恆星之宿度，並非恆星之子中。

translations.literal: In fact chou was the lodge degree of fixed stars in Zhou times, and was not the middle of zi among fixed stars.
translations.idiomatic: In fact chou marked only where the fixed stars stood at the solstice in Zhou times—not the true midpoint of zi among the fixed stars.

sentences.zh: 今並不在丑，又移至寅十餘度矣。

translations.literal: Today it is no longer in chou at all, having shifted again more than ten degrees into yin.
translations.idiomatic: Today the solstice stands nowhere near chou, having shifted another dozen degrees into yin.

sentences.zh: 由今箕一以上溯古虛五，歷年四千有餘，已差至五十八度，此恆星東行之明驗也。』

translations.literal: From today's Winnowing Basket 1° tracing back to ancient Emptiness 5°, over more than four thousand years the difference has reached fifty-eight degrees—this is clear proof of the eastward motion of fixed stars.'
translations.idiomatic: Tracing from today's Winnowing Basket 1° back to the Emptiness 5° of antiquity, more than four thousand years yield a displacement of fifty-eight degrees—clear proof of the fixed stars' eastward drift.'

sentences.zh: 其他著論無關曆算者不錄。

translations.literal: His other treatises unrelated to calendrical calculation are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His other writings unrelated to calendrical astronomy are not included here.
